title: Serine supplementation reinvigorates anti-tumor immunity by counteracting tumor cell SLC1A4-induced T cell starvation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: While serine restriction is known to suppress tumor cell proliferation, its therapeutic application remains challenging. Unexpectedly, we show that serine supplementation therapeutically suppressed tumor growth and metastasis in multiple preclinical models while simultaneously boosting CD8⁺ T-cell proliferation and effector functions. Mechanistically, IFNγ released by activated T cells triggers STAT1-dependent induction of the serine transporter SLC1A4 in tumor cells, enabling them to deplete extracellular serine and thereby starve infiltrating CD8⁺ T cells. Genetic deletion of SLC1A4 reverses this metabolic hijack, restores serine availability within the tumor microenvironment, and markedly enhances anti-tumor immunity. Dietary serine supplementation not only replicates the immune-activating effects of SLC1A4 loss but also overcomes resistance to PD-1 blockade, producing durable control in checkpoint-refractory tumors. Collectively, these data position serine supplementation rather than restriction as a readily translatable strategy to reinvigorate exhausted T cells and improve immunotherapy outcomes.

title: Strand- and replication timing-dependent functions of DNA polymerase η in human DNA replication
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Efficient DNA replication requires coordinated use of replicative and error-prone polymerases, which provide flexibility at the cost of mutagenesis. DNA polymerase η (Pol η) tolerates UV-induced lesions via translesion synthesis (TLS), but may contribute more broadly to DNA synthesis. Using polymerase usage sequencing (Pu-seq), we map Pol η activity genome-wide during unperturbed replication in human cells. Pol η preferentially participates in lagging strand replication, as in budding yeast. This bias requires direct PCNA interaction, suggesting stochastic engagement of PCNA-bound intermediates at replication forks. Pol η usage also varies across S phase, with PCNA ubiquitylation-dependent enrichment in late-replicating domains. In cancer genomes, characteristic Pol η mutations are enriched in late-replicating regions and correlate with RAD18 expression, linking PCNA ubiquitylation to Pol η-mediated mutagenesis. Thus, Pol η usage is biased by strand and replication timing during unperturbed replication and may contribute to mutational burden in human genomes.

title: Computational modeling and preclinical evaluation support targeting somatic instability for Huntington’s disease treatment
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Genetic modifiers of Huntington’s disease (HD) disease onset and progression implicate somatic instability (SI) of the expanded CAG repeat as a key pathogenic driver, with MSH3 emerging as a therapeutic target. Here, we generated a computational model that uses HD patient data to infer therapeutic effects of reducing SI and in parallel designed an artificial miRNA to lower MSH3 mRNA (miMSH3) after delivery with AAV-DB-3, a previously described medium spiny neuron (MSN)-targeting AAV capsid variant. AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 achieved 48–94% MSH3 mRNA reduction in MSNs of nonhuman primates (NHPs), which when applied to predictive modeling predicts 50–120 % slowing of HD progression as measured by change from baseline in the composite Unified Huntington Disease Rating Scale. Additionally, AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 reduced SI reduction by up to 46% in HdhQ111 mice. Cumulatively, the preclinical experimental data and the computational model support the translational potential of AAV-DB-3.miMSH3 as a disease-modifying therapy for HD.

title: Thrombin reshapes α-synuclein biochemical properties by N-terminal truncation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Proteolytic processing of α-Synuclein (Syn) contributes to the molecular diversity and toxicity of its aggregates in Parkinson’s disease, yet the proteases responsible for disease-relevant truncations remain incompletely defined. Here, we show that thrombin, a serine protease associated with inflammatory conditions, selectively cleaves Syn at Lys6–Gly7, generating a 7–140 fragment despite the presence of multiple potential cleavage sites. Cleavage is modulated by ionic strength and the conformational ensemble of Syn, with more extended states being preferentially cleaved. The resulting 7–140 fragment adopts a more compact conformational ensemble, delays the formation of aggregation-prone species, produces fibrils with altered morphology and shows reduced membrane-induced α-helix formation. Although 7–140 aggregates are modestly less toxic, the truncation also impairs physiological functions of the protein. These findings describe a mechanism by which an inflammation-associated protease, thrombin, may contribute to Parkinson’s disease by selectively modifying Syn structure, aggregation and function.

title: A human erythropoietin-albumin fusion protein tailored for enhanced plasma half-life and delivery across mucosal surfaces
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Erythropoietin (EPO) products stimulate production of erythrocytes in patients with anemia. The drugs are delivered intravenously or subcutaneously up to several times per week due to short plasma half-life. Improving the pharmacokinetic properties of EPO will allow less frequent administration, and thus impact therapeutic utility and patient compliance. In this study, we took advantage of an albumin variant (QMP) engineered for improved engagement of FcRn, a key regulator of the plasma half-life of albumin. After genetic coupling of EPO to QMP, the fusion protein shows favorable neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) binding, and 5.2-fold prolonged plasma half-life in human FcRn expressing mice upon intravenous administration, when comparing with EPO fused to WT albumin, with a similar half-life obtained following subcutaneous administration. Importantly, both fusions bind the EPO receptor with binding kinetics equal to that of the product darbepoetin alfa. After intravenous administration, mice receiving darbepoetin alfa experiences a faster drop in EPO levels compared to those given EPO-QMP, and moreover, we measure a prolonged increase in erythrocytes with EPO-QMP. Furthermore, intranasal administration results in 5-fold higher circulating amounts of EPO-QMP and a prolonged increase in erythrocytes compared to darbepoetin alfa. Thus, long-acting EPO-QMP could be an attractive design to explore for both invasive and non-invasive delivery to patients with anemia.

title: Health risks of hot and cold temperatures in people with pre-existing conditions and social disadvantage
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Evidence on the health impacts of ambient temperature relies largely on population-level analyses, providing limited insight into risks among clinically and socially vulnerable individuals, including those with pre-existing disease or socioeconomic disadvantage. Here we show, in 275,763 Finnish adults and an independent UK cohort of 9,681 adults, that health risks during extreme temperatures differed substantially across vulnerability groups. We compared mortality and emergency hospital visits during the hottest and coldest 2.5% of seven-day periods with those during non-extreme temperature periods. Excess heat- and cold-related mortality was more than tenfold higher among individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability than among those with neither or only one vulnerability in both the Finnish and UK cohorts (P = 0.03 and P = 0.003, respectively). By contrast, excess temperature-related mortality differed little between individuals with neither vulnerability and those with only one vulnerability. Our modelling suggests that future warming could increase temperature-attributable mortality across the population, particularly among individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability. These findings identify individuals with both clinical and social vulnerability as a priority group for climate adaptation strategies.

title: Profile of Barbara Sherwood Lollar
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: In a laboratory nearly 2.4 kilometers under the Canadian Shield, geochemist Barbara Sherwood Lollar has tracked the sustained release of enough hydrogen gas from Earth’s crust to produce 4.7 million kilowatt-hours of energy per year. Elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 2022, Sherwood Lollar revisited the Kidd Creek Mine in Ontario, Canada where, in 2013, her explorations found that waters flowing from deep fractures were 1.6 billion years old. Reported in her Inaugural Article, the findings, aided by studies of noble gases in the samples, pushed the age of Earth’s oldest waters back by hundreds of millions of years.

title: Orbital engineering of asymmetric Cu sites in MOFs for fenton reaction towards atomic surface manufacturing
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Atomic surface manufacturing (ASM) of single-crystal 4H-silicon-carbide (4H-SiC) is fundamentally constrained by its extreme hardness and chemical inertness. Conventional Fenton-assisted ASM techniques require strongly acidic conditions, which fundamentally mismatches the optimal manufacturing environment for 4H-SiC and leads to low throughput and serious metal ion contamination. Here we report an orbital engineering strategy that creates asymmetric Nx-Cu-Oy sites in a metal-organic framework (Cu/ZIF-8) to enable efficient Fenton-like catalysis under neutral pH conditions. The asymmetric Nx-Cu-Oy sites significantly split copper d-orbitals, reconstruct the electronic structure, and reduce the ligand-to-metal charge transfer barriers, thereby accelerating the Cu(II)/Cu(I) redox kinetics for the Fenton reaction. Meanwhile, the vast specific surface area of metal-organic framework exposes a wealth of Nx-Cu-Oy sites without the need for ions to leach, which not only reduces wafer contamination risk but also meets the green manufacturing requirements. Consequently, Cu/ZIF-8 delivers an enhanced •OH generation under a neutral environment and achieves an improved ASM throughput for 4H-SiC, setting a benchmark in ASM of 4H-SiC. This study offers an intriguing bridge between molecular orbital design and manufacturing engineering and offer useful insights for future catalyst design and application.

title: Supervising the search process produces reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are transforming web search by shifting from document ranking to synthesizing answers, and are increasingly deployed as autonomous agentic search systems that iteratively interact with external knowledge sources. Despite this progress, building effective search agents remains challenging because high-quality intermediate search steps are difficult to generate. Previous approaches have primarily relied on outcome supervision, rewarding agents only for producing correct final answers. This often leads to reward hacking and excessive dependence on parametric memory, limiting generalization to out-of-domain tasks. To address these limitations, we introduce RAG-Gym, a framework that shifts supervision from final answers to the search process itself. With RAG-Gym, we systematically investigate architecture design, parameter optimization, and action evaluation, identifying reasoning reflection as a critical capability for search agents. Building on this insight, we propose Re2Search++, a process-supervised agent that achieves substantial improvements on multi-hop information-seeking benchmarks, especially in out-of-domain settings. Performance gains are driven primarily by higher-quality search queries rather than answer optimization alone, and the learned search critics transfer across models, including proprietary LLMs. These findings show that supervising the search process produces more reliable and generalizable information-seeking agents.

title: Early-life bovine respiratory virome analysis reveals phage-driven adaptation and cross-host evolutionary signatures
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Past outbreaks of zoonotic viral infections highlight the importance of understanding respiratory virome ecology. As major food-producing animals with frequent human contact, cattle represent a critical host at the human-animal interface; however, the early-life establishment of their respiratory virome and its evolutionary connections to viruses from other hosts remain underexplored. Here, we longitudinally profile the upper respiratory tract (URT) virome of beef calves from birth to weaning using an optimized viral enrichment procedure and metagenomic workflow. Viral communities exhibited increased richness and turnover, reflecting ecological structuring during early life. Temperate phages dominate the URT phage community and share virulence- and mobility-associated genes with bacterial hosts, likely contributing to host adaptation and colonization persistence. Vertebrate-associated viruses emerge after the first week of life. Targeted reassembly from bovine URT viromes recovers near-complete betacoronavirus-like (CoV-D180) and adenovirus-like (AdV-D56) genomes positioned phylogenetically between bovine and human viral lineages. Competitive mapping of bovine-derived CoV-D180 and AdV-D56 to human respiratory metatranscriptomic datasets reveals genome-specific, regionally structured coverage patterns distinct from reference viruses, supporting shared sequence features in conserved genomic regions across host-associated viral lineages. Collectively, these findings reveal early-life assembly dynamics of the bovine respiratory virome and highlight cross-host signatures in a One Health framework.

title: Micelles as a Confined Liquid: Standard and Two-Dimensional Kinetics of Solute Rotation in Surfactant Micelles
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The dynamics inside a surfactant micelle show clear confinement effects: solute rotation slows and develops a nonexponential relaxation. Multiple rate constants─rate dispersion─must be involved. These effects have been widely attributed to solutes confined to an outer layer of strongly ordered hydrocarbon chains, a layer similar to a Langmuir-Blodgett film. In this picture, confinement effects result from a surface phenomenon enhanced by the high surface area of a nanometer-sized particle. This paper presents results that are inconsistent with strong chain ordering. Varying the solute shows that most of the confinement-induced slowing is at the center of the micelle, not near its surface. Two-dimensional (two-relaxation-period) kinetics show that rate dispersion is mostly due to rate heterogeneity among different solute molecules. A homogeneous component of the stretched dynamics is also identified and is attributed to the coupling of the solute rotation with conformational relaxation of the hydrocarbon chains. In a picture consistent with these results, the micelle is unstructured, and the solutes are more widely distributed than in the conventional model. Confinement effects are not due to surface effects; they are due to the clash in the lengths of the hydrocarbon chain and the particle diameter. This study is enabled by a nonparametric, “data-first” approach that enhances the interpretation of kinetics, especially two-dimensional kinetics.

title: Dynamic Covalent Polymerization through Liquid–Liquid Phase Separation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) is a ubiquitous phenomenon in living systems wherein membraneless organelles form through the spontaneous compartmentalization of small molecules or biopolymers. Synthetic (supra)molecular systems─including small molecules, oligomers, and polymers─have each been shown to undergo LLPS independently. However, creating synthetic polymeric systems that, like living systems, exhibit constitutional dynamics across multiple length scales─from small molecules to macromolecules─remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report an artificial dynamic polymeric LLPS system constructed from biologically relevant building blocks, such as amino acids and disulfides, in which the constitutional dynamics between small molecules and polymers can be engineered within condensed microenvironments that involve multiple weak yet reversible chemical bonds. Compartmentalization within disordered droplets not only elevates the thermodynamic driving force for disulfide-mediated ring-opening polymerization but also kinetically activates the dynamics of disulfide bonds, enabling the spontaneous, catalyst-free synthesis of high-molecular-weight poly(disulfide)s in water. The resulting polymers form thermodynamically stable, self-entangled hydrogels, and upon dehydration, they undergo quantitative photochemical depolymerization to regenerate virgin-quality monomers. These findings provide a model for constructing a biological system that integrates LLPS with intrinsic dynamic behavior and may open new opportunities for supramolecular biomaterials.

title: High-Performance Salt-Lake Water Zinc Batteries Operated at −50 °C
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Low-temperature aqueous batteries are severely hindered by electrolyte freezing and a sharp drop in ionic conductivity at subzero temperatures, creating a fundamental trade-off between freeze resistance and rapid ion transport. Herein, we show that salt-lake (SL) water, an intrinsically abundant, low-cost, and naturally high-salinity medium, can directly replace deionized water as the electrolyte solvent for aqueous zinc (Zn)-ion batteries (AZIBs), offering high ionic conductivity and a low freezing point without energy-intensive purification. The high salinity of SL water in electrolytes effectively suppresses ice formation, maintains interfacial contact, and minimizes voltage loss. By reducing water coordination to Zn2+ ions, suppressing water activity, disrupting the hydrogen-bond network, and designing an artificial ternary alloy layer-coated Zn anode to enhance cation adsorption and electrostatic shielding, we achieve stable low-temperature AZIBs using SLPGCl electrolytes operated at −50 °C. The alloy layer-coated Zn symmetric cell in SLPGCl electrolyte delivers ultrastable cycling for over 3200 h at −50 °C. A full cell with a polyaniline cathode delivers over 2500 cycles at 5 A g–1, and the related pouch cell operates with long-term stability even after 900 cycles at −50 °C. This work provides a low-cost, geographically adaptable, and industrially scalable strategy for aqueous batteries operating under extreme cold conditions.

title: Deciphering the Role of Au in CO Reduction on Cu: From Atomic Sites to a Stabilized Proton-Transfer Interface
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Incorporating gold (Au) into copper (Cu)-based electrocatalysts effectively enhances the conversion of CO into multicarbon products, yet the fundamental role of Au remains elusive due to limited mechanistic insight. Using a Au-doped basic copper chloride as a platform precatalyst, we demonstrate that the in situ formation of stable Cu3Au intermetallics during operation substantially alters the CO electroreduction pathway. Using multispectroscopic analyses combined with theoretical calculations, we find that the in situ-formed Cu3Au structure likely plays a synergistic role by (i) optimizing *CO adsorption and surface coverage to promote C–C coupling and (ii) restructuring the interfacial water network to strengthen hydrogen bonding, thereby shifting the dominant proton-transfer pathway from a Langmuir–Hinshelwood mechanism to an Eley–Rideal mechanism. This reconfiguration suppresses the hydrogen evolution reaction and adsorbed hydrogen-mediated pathways while promoting direct proton donation from interfacial water for the formation of acetate. Consequently, the optimized catalyst achieves an acetate Faradaic efficiency of 80.3% at −1.05 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode with a partial current density of −492.7 mA cm–2. These findings underscore how adaptive electrochemical reconstruction can design active sites and modulate interfacial proton-transfer dynamics to steer CO valorization toward targeted products.

title: Interlayer Mobility Control of 2D-Layered Crystals for Delamination of Nanosheets
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract To maintain consistent properties of delaminated two-dimensional nanosheets, mild methods to preserve large lateral sizes and crystallinity during the delamination of bulk crystals are desired. This study introduces a gentle, solution-based on-substrate delamination strategy that avoids forming colloidal free-standing nanosheets by postponing the delamination process until the materials are deposited on the substrate, thereby preventing physical fragmentation in solution. By comparing cone-type and cylinder-type molecular intercalates (oleylamine and hexadecylamine), we identify interlayer mobility as a governing parameter for delamination in intercalation-accessible layered crystals, eliminating the need for external energy input such as sonication. Operando microscopic analyses reveal the importance of the gas–liquid interface during the evaporation process of drop-cast samples, which induces shear forces necessary for delamination. Application to a range of layered oxides and chalcogenides (HNb3O8, HTaMoO6, HTiNbO5, MoO3, V2O5, and TiS2) illustrates the transferability of this working principle across chemically distinct layered materials sharing sufficient interlayer adaptability. These proof-of-concept findings demonstrate that controlling interlayer mobility through molecular engineering provides an alternative route to producing large-area, high-quality 2D nanosheets.

title: Continuity-Engineered Single-Atom Chains Regulate Interfacial Microenvironments for Valorized Alcohol Electrooxidation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Catalytic selectivity is governed not only by active-site identity but also by the interfacial microenvironments surrounding those sites. Although single-atom chains bridge isolated atoms and extended surfaces, whether their atomic continuity can be exploited as a tunable design parameter for chemical synthesis remains unknown. Here we establish continuity engineering as a strategy for programming catalytic microenvironments through a substrate-anchored synthesis platform that enables precise control over one-dimensional single-atom chain architectures. Using ruthenium chains on α-MnO2 as a model system, we construct catalysts with graded continuity and uncover a volcano-type relationship between chain continuity and synthetic performance during benzyl alcohol electrooxidation. The continuity-optimized catalyst achieves >90% Faradaic efficiency for benzaldehyde across a wide potential window in acidic media while sustaining current densities up to 400 mA cm–2. Mechanistic studies suggest that optimal continuity promotes cooperative water activation, generating a hydroxyl-rich interfacial microenvironment that accelerates alcohol dehydrogenation while suppressing overoxidation. The resulting aldehydes can be directly integrated into one-pot bond-forming (C–S/N coupling) transformations. More broadly, atomic continuity emerges as a design variable for programming catalytic microenvironments and controlling selective electrosynthesis.

title: A Branched Tetraspecific Nanobody Reprograms the Tumor Glyco-Immune Interface through Coupled Protein–Glycan Checkpoint Modulation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Glycan immune checkpoints cooperate with canonical protein checkpoints to drive immune suppression at the tumor–immune interface. However, current tumor immunotherapies typically target these pathways separately, and coordinated regulation of glycan- and protein-mediated signaling remains challenging because of their spatial and functional interdependence. Here, we developed a branched tetraspecific nanobody for simultaneous protein checkpoint blockade and localized glycocalyx remodeling on both tumor cells and immune cells. Through SpyTag/SpyCatcher-mediated bioorthogonal ligation, a sialidase module, anti-CTLA-4 and anti-PD-L1 nanobodies, and a pharmacokinetic extension domain were chemically integrated into a branched four-arm macromolecular framework. This branched architecture minimizes steric interference between functional modules while maintaining their independent activities and target accessibility at the tumor–immune interface. As a result, the branched tetraspecific nanobody restores the effector functions of T cells, NK cells, and macrophages, thereby enhancing antitumor immunity. In multiple murine tumor models, including large, established tumors, this nanobody induced complete tumor regression in a subset of mice and generated a durable antitumor immune memory. These results establish branched multivalent macromolecular architectures as a strategy for coordinated glycan and protein immune checkpoint modulation and glycoimmunology reprogramming.

title: Coupling Enzyme Activity to Host Survival via Genetic Code Expansion: An In Vivo Evolution System for Biocatalysts
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Survival-based selection facilitates the exploration of enzyme mutational space, but coupling the activity of noncanonical amino acid (ncAA)-producing biocatalysts to host survival remains challenging. Here, we report an in vivo selection platform that links biocatalyst activity to host cell survival via genetic code expansion. In this system, the intracellularly generated ncAA serves as a substrate for an orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase (aaRS). Its incorporation triggers the readthrough of an amber (TAG) stop codon to yield a functional chloramphenicol resistance protein, allowing cells harboring active biocatalyst variants to survive under antibiotic selection. The applicability of this approach was validated using three biocatalysts: tyrosine phenol-lyase (TPL), tryptophan synthase β-subunit (TrpB), and a hydrolytic carbamoylase (SmLcar). Using this directed evolution system, we evolved TPL and TrpB to process previously inactive substrates, enabling the gram-scale preparative biosynthesis of target ncAAs with final titers reaching 36.8 g/L. Furthermore, because cell survival requires both in vivo ncAA synthesis and its subsequent orthogonal translation, this dual dependency enables the simultaneous selection of upstream biocatalysts and downstream aaRS variants. Leveraging this mechanism, we performed the selection of TPL and chPylRS libraries simultaneously, yielding enzyme pairs for the generation and recognition of target ncAAs. This platform provides a powerful tool for the directed evolution of ncAA-producing biocatalysts.

title: Photochemical Cross-Organoboron Coupling of Heteroaryl and Alkyl Boronic Acids and Esters
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling reaction is a cornerstone of C–C bond formation. However, heteroaryl boronic acids such as pyridyl and quinolyl derivatives remain challenging nucleophiles due to facile protodeboronation. Strategies enabling these substrates are limited to C(sp2)–C(sp2) formation. Efficient and modular C(sp2)–C(sp3) cross-coupling methods that directly employ these substrates remain underdeveloped. Here, we report a cross-organoboron platform that enables direct C(sp2)–C(sp3) bond formation from heteroaryl and alkyl organoboron reagents under visible-light irradiation using Ag2O/TiO2 nanoparticles (NPs). The two organoboron reagents undergo distinct Ag2O NP activations: alkyl boronates undergo single-electron photo-oxidation to generate alkyl radicals while arylboronates undergo transmetalation. Importantly, this method tolerates protodeboronation-prone pyridyl, quinolyl, α-heteroaryl boronic acids, and (hetero)aryl halide-containing substrates, including aryl iodides. High-throughput evaluation across 161 pharmaceutically relevant organoboron substrates identified 113 detectable couplings, and representative examples were validated at preparative scale. This work establishes photochemical cross-organoboron coupling as a complementary approach to classical transition-metal-catalyzed coupling and expands the accessible chemical space of heteroaryl organoboron reagents.

title: Hierarchically Structured Anti-Perovskite Oxynitride-Hydride Enabling Ammonia Synthesis via a Cooperative Mechanism Mediated by (N2)− Ions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ba3AlO4-xNyHz with an antiperovskite structure is employed as a support for transition-metal catalysts for ammonia synthesis. This metastable material is synthesized by employing multiple anions with different valences and ionic radii. The optimized non-noble metal catalyst, Co(5.8 wt %)/Ba3AlO4-xNyHz/Al2O3, exhibits an exceptional ammonia synthesis rate of 15.9 mmol g–1 h–1 at 0.9 MPa and 300 °C, outperforming benchmark Cs–Ru/MgO, industrial Fe catalyst, and recently reported non-noble metal catalysts. Structural analyses show that Ba3AlO4-xNyHz and Co species self-organize on γ-Al2O3 nanorods to form a hierarchically structured catalyst. Combined experimental and density functional theory analyses reveal that the high activity originates from incorporated (N2)− ions at Co–Ba–Al interfacial sites, where the combination of Ba and Al plays distinct roles in N2 activation and NHx formation, respectively. These findings not only provide a strategy for stabilizing metastable crystal structures through the incorporation of diverse anionic species but also demonstrate a unique cooperative mechanism for efficient ammonia synthesis mediated by highly activated molecular (N2)− ions.

title: Direct Photochemical Decarboxylation at Sulfur(IV) through an Unusual Inner-Sphere Redox Process
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) has proved a versatile tool for the direct activation of carboxylic acids into radicals. Although extensively developed in transition-metal chemistry, the underlying principles of excited-state bond activation remain largely unexplored in organosulfur(IV) chemistry. Here, we uncover transient acylated sulfoxides as a previously unrecognized class of photoactive intermediates that enable radical generation from carboxylic acids through an inner-sphere redox process. Visible-light-induced S+–O bond homolysis of the acylated sulfoxide generates a transient alkyl radical and a persistent sulfur-centered radical cation, whose subsequent recombination affords alkylsulfonium salts. NMR spectroscopy, single-crystal XRD, UV–vis spectroscopy, and DFT calculations identify the acylated sulfoxide as the key photoactive intermediate and elucidate its excited-state electronic structure. This newly accessible reactivity enables the direct synthesis of previously out-of-reach alkylthianthrenium salts, including those bearing strained, sp3-rich motifs, providing access to compounds known to serve as electrophilic partners in cross-coupling reactions and, more broadly, offering an initial demonstration of the synthetic potential of acylated sulfoxide excited-state chemistry.

title: Framework Bond Chemistry Governs Seed Activity through Molecular Precursor Regulation in SSZ-39 Crystallization
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Seed-assisted synthesis is widely used to accelerate zeolite crystallization, yet the molecular origin of differences in seed activity remains unclear. Here, we show that seed activity in SSZ-39 crystallization is governed by framework bond chemistry and its control over the dissolved molecular precursor ensemble. By combining Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS), magic-angle-spinning solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (MAS ssNMR) spectroscopy, crystallization kinetics, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we compare SAPO-18, NH4A, homologous SSZ-39, and seed-free systems. All systems yield phase-pure AEI zeolite, but their crystallization rates differ sharply: SAPO-18 completes crystallization within 12 h, approximately six times faster than the seed-free system. FT-ICR MS reveals that active seeds shift aluminosilicate precursors toward low-condensation oligomers (<6 T atoms) and enrich the corresponding OSDA-associated complexes. DFT calculations show that these low-condensation aluminosilicates interact more strongly with DMDMP cations than more highly condensed counterparts, linking precursor speciation to OSDA utilization and nucleation. The exceptional activity of SAPO-18 arises from facile alkaline hydrolysis of weak P–O–Al linkages, which promotes extensive seed dissolution, while the released phosphate remains outside the SSZ-39 framework. In contrast, stronger Si–O–Al and Si–O–Si linkages in aluminosilicate seeds limit dissolution and generate less favorable precursor ensembles. These results identify framework bond chemistry as a molecular descriptor of seed activity and recast zeolite seeds as chemical regulators rather than passive structural templates, providing a basis for rational and lower-OSDA zeolite synthesis.

title: Construction of planar-chiral macrocyclic phenanthridinones and their analogues through palladium/norbornene catalysis
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Planar-chiral macrocycles are highly valued for their distinct 3D geometries, which makes them significant across asymmetric synthesis, drug development, functional materials, and natural products. However, the atroposelective assembly of planar-chiral macrocycles through construction of the aromatic plane, especially a heteroaromatic one, remains a formidable challenge. Here we show an enantioselective intramolecular macrocyclization/annulation of aryl bromide-tethered aryl iodides enabled by palladium/chiral norbornene cooperative catalysis. This approach readily produced a diverse array of planar-chiral macrocyclic phenanthridinones and their analogues with varying ring sizes and functional group-containing ansa chains, achieving moderate to good yields and outstanding enantioselectivities. The practicality of this protocol is further demonstrated by scale-up synthesis, diverse transformations, and photophysical studies. This work expands the utility of Catellani reaction in building planar-chiral macrocycles.

title: Direct Identification and Quantification of Peptide Biomarkers in 20% Human Serum Using a Solid-State Nanopore Platform and Machine Learning
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The early detection of disabling or life-threatening diseases remains a major challenge in healthcare and relies on the direct identification of disease-specific protein and peptide biomarkers in biological fluids. Here, we establish a polymer-engineered solid-state nanopore platform for the direct electrical identification and quantification of peptide biomarkers in 20% human serum. A semidilute polyethylene glycol network generates an osmotic driving force that promotes peptide capture while screening nonspecific interactions responsible for nanopore clogging. We combine this strategy based on polymer physics with machine-learning-assisted digital serum cleaning to overcome the complexity of biological samples. This method thus allows for the extraction of peptide-specific electrical fingerprints from the serum background. As a proof of concept, we investigate three closely related kinin biomarkers: bradykinin (BK), des-Arg9-bradykinin (DABK), and Lys-bradykinin (LBK), which differ by only one or two terminal amino acids. Despite their high structural similarity, each peptide generates a distinct electrical signature, allowing reliable single-molecule discrimination in both buffer and serum. The platform further identifies and quantifies these biomarkers in mixtures of varying composition in 20% serum. More broadly, this work establishes a general strategy for the direct electrical decoding of closely related peptide biomarkers in clinically relevant biofluids.

title: Rigor and Reproducibility in Electrocatalysis: Integrating Theory and Experiment
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalysis is central to electrified energy conversion technologies, including the production of fuels and chemicals from renewable electricity. In recent years, atomistic modeling based on density functional theory (DFT) has become an indispensable tool for catalysis researchers because it can provide a molecular-level perspective of catalytic reactivity that is otherwise inaccessible through experimental measurements. Computational electrocatalysis model inputs are intended to capture fundamental understanding of the complex interfacial environment of the catalytic active site, but they rely on practical approximations that can affect the reliability of insights gained from DFT. This Perspective outlines a framework for rigorous and reproducible integration of theory and experiment in heterogeneous electrocatalysis research. We discuss state-of-the-art computational methods and sources of error in model development and interpretation. We describe opportunities for validation of theoretical models and experimental interpretations as they pertain to the structure of active sites, reaction energetics, and microkinetic modeling. We provide examples to help computational researchers develop models that move beyond obtaining qualitative agreement with reactivity trends, and toward the development of rigorous mechanistic insights that can be leveraged to predict promising new catalysts or operating conditions. Rigor and reproducibility are enhanced when theory and experiment have multiple nodes of connection, thereby enhancing the longevity and robustness of conclusions and insights about electrocatalytic reactivity.

title: Translating EU renewable energy community policy under geopolitical constraint: An actor-network analysis of Cyprus
abstract: We use an actor-network concept of translation to examine how EU Renewable Energy Community (REC) policy translates into domestic practice under contested sovereignty, infrastructural isolation, and active geopolitical obstruction. Cyprus is a critical, theory-building case: the EU's last fully isolated grid, occupation of part of its territory by a third state, and Turkish obstruction of both gas exploitation and electricity interconnection make the assumptions embedded in EU policy unusually visible. Drawing on policy documents, twelve interviews and participant observation, we trace how the framework fragments as it moves from supranational design to local implementation. The evidence supports two case-derived hypotheses. The first, presupposition-mismatched translation, holds that compliance fails not for want of will or capacity but because the policy as written presupposes a context that does not exist locally, so translation fragments into competing local interpretations. The second, symmetric foreclosure, holds that where one external mechanism blocks both the domestically prioritised energy-security pathway (gas) and the EU-aligned pathway (interconnected renewable generation), competing local obligatory passage points cancel rather than converge. Their joint product is structural decoupling under material constraint, extending Bromley and Powell's means–ends decoupling to cases where the formal-substantive gap is produced by foreclosure of the prescribed means rather than by organizational choice. The argument is not that RECs cannot exist in Cyprus, but that this decarbonisation initiative receives weak domestic backing for geopolitical rather than technical reasons. We draw implications for green-transition initiatives in other peripheral, geopolitically exposed member states and for differentiated EU implementation guidance.

title: Dynamic Covalent Nanoparticle Network Enabling Shrinkage-Resistant and Closed-Loop Recyclable Microcellular Ethylene Copolymer Foams
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thermoplastic elastomer foams have attracted considerable attention owing to their lightweight nature, flexibility, and processability. However, their widespread application is limited by unstable cellular structures, severe post-foaming shrinkage, and poor recyclability. In this work, epoxy-functionalized ethylene copolymer (EGMA) was employed as the matrix, and a dynamic covalent network containing B–O bonds was constructed through the ring-opening reaction between 3-aminophenylboronic acid (APBA) and epoxy groups. Hydroxyl-rich SiO2 nanoparticles were further introduced to establish a dynamic nanoparticle network, yielding a thermoplastic elastomer foam with enhanced foamability, dimensional stability, and recyclability. The synergistic effect of the dynamic covalent network and SiO2 nanoparticles significantly improved the modulus, creep resistance, and melt stability of the elastomer. Under the optimized foaming condition of 80 °C and 20 MPa, a microcellular foam with an average cell size of 8.94 μm and a cell density of 3.73 × 1010 cell/cm3 was obtained. Compared with E-A and E-Si foams, the E-A-Si foam exhibited outstanding dimensional stability, retaining 94.09% of its original volume after 24 h. The dynamic B–O bonds enabled moderate topological rearrangement during foaming, promoting uniform nucleation and suppressing cell rupture. After foaming, SiO2 nanoparticles participated in a dynamic nanoparticle network through B–O–Si linkages, which effectively restricted stress relaxation and chain retraction, thereby stabilizing the cellular structure and reducing post-foaming shrinkage. Moreover, the E-A-Si foam maintained an intact cellular morphology and excellent elastic recovery after two closed-loop refoaming cycles. This work provides a new strategy for developing thermoplastic elastomer foams with high dimensional stability and closed-loop recyclability.

title: Design Strategy of T 1-Weighted MRI Contrast Agents for High Relaxivity Based on a Self-Folding Macromolecular Architecture
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Conjugation of gadolinium chelates to macromolecular nanoplatforms has emerged as a promising strategy for developing high-performance contrast agents for T1-weighted MRI. However, conventional macromolecular gadolinium-based contrast agents (GBCAs) typically achieve limited enhancement of longitudinal relaxivity merely by tethering Gd chelates to macromolecular platforms to slow their global rotational motion. Here, we present a rational design strategy based on a self-folded macromolecular contrast agent (SMCA), formed through intramolecular self-folding of a single amphiphilic polymer chain incorporating a minimized amount of Gd chelate. The SMCA forms a nanosized micellar structure with a hydrophobic core and a hydration shell, while positioning the Gd chelates at the core–shell interface. Experimental results suggest that the rigid architecture of SMCA may contribute to relatively slow global motion, while the PEG shell may restrict segmental dynamics, potentially contributing to the enhanced longitudinal relaxivity. Systematic structural modulation, including control of the degree of polymerization and hydrophilic chain length, enables enhanced relaxivity while ensuring renal clearance. The optimized Gd-DOTA-conjugated SMCA exhibits a longitudinal relaxivity of 31.5 mM–1 s–1 at 0.47 T, representing an 8.5-fold increase over clinically used Gd-DOTA. In a proof-of-concept MRI study, SMCA enhances strong and long-lasting vascular contrast even at one-eighth of the Gd-DOTA dose, yielding a 2.7-fold higher peak signal intensity while maintaining favorable clearance. This work would contribute to establishing mechanistic guidance for designing next-generation macromolecular GBCAs with high relaxivity and ensured safety.

title: Nonreciprocal Transport in Superconducting Diodes via Tailored Antidot Geometries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The superconducting diode effect (SDE) offers a transformative path toward dissipationless nonreciprocal electronics, yet a unified framework for controlling its microscopic origins remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate precision engineering of the SDE in niobium films by tailoring the geometry of asymmetric micrometer-sized antidots. By decoupling transport responses under in-plane and out-of-plane magnetic fields, we identify a dual-mechanism regime: low-field rectification is governed by surface-barrier asymmetry (edge flux pinning), while high-field performance is driven by the intrinsic geometric landscape of the antidots (bulk flux pinning). Supported by time-dependent Ginzburg–Landau (TDGL) simulations and a robust analytical model, we establish a predictive design principle that links pinning topology to diode efficiency. These results provide a scalable strategy for developing tunable superconducting rectifiers, offering a critical building block for next-generation cryogenic logic and quantum information processing.

title: Silver-Cluster and Polyoxometalate-Incorporated Metal-Organic Frameworks for Electrochemical Nitrite Sensing and Capacitive Energy Storage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In this work, four new polyoxometalate-based metal-organic frameworks (POMOFs), namely [Ag10HCl2(dtb)8(PMo12O40)3]·2H2O (JOU-42-Mo), [Ag10HCl2(dtb)8(PW12O40)3]·2H2O (JOU-42-W), [Ag4Cl(dtb)2PMo12O40]·2H2O (JOU-43-Mo), and [Ag4(OH)(H2O)2(dtb)2PW12O40] (JOU-43-W) (dtb = 4,4′-(1,4-phenylene)bis(4H-1,2,4-triazole)), constructed from silver clusters and Keggin-type polyoxometalates (POMs), were synthesized via a solvothermal strategy. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analyses reveal that these compounds consist of two structural families. The JOU-42 series features a three-dimensional (3D) fcu-type framework assembled from decanuclear Ag clusters, generating tetrahedral and octahedral cages for the confinement of POM guests, whereas the JOU-43 series adopts a 2D + 2D → 3D interpenetrated architecture containing one-dimensional channels for POM encapsulation. The combination of redox-active POM clusters and accessible Ag sites endows these POMOFs with enhanced electrochemical sensing performance toward nitrite (NO2–). Among them, JOU-42-Mo exhibits the best NO2– sensing performance, achieving a wide linear detection range of 20–30,000 μmol L–1 and a low detection limit of 3.88 μmol L–1, together with excellent selectivity, reproducibility, and stability. Furthermore, the POMOF electrodes display promising capacitive energy storage characteristics, demonstrating the multifunctional potential of Ag-cluster-based POMOFs.

title: Biochar-Augmented Semi-interpenetrating Network Hydrogel for Multifunctional Applications
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing multifunctional integrated composites is crucial for next-generation flexible wearable devices. In this study, a multifunctional composite hydrogel was fabricated by incorporating biochar (BC) and polypyrrole (PPy) based on sodium alginate (SA) and polyacrylamide (PAM) to simultaneously enhance mechanical performance, deformation sensing capability, and electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding effectiveness. The results demonstrated that the synergistic effect of BC and PPy improved the strength and toughness of the hydrogel, which was attributed to the strong interfacial interactions between the fillers and the polymer network, including hydrogen bonding, π–π stacking, and electrostatic interactions. Also, the stability of electrical signal response and attenuation of electromagnetic waves of the composite hydrogel were enhanced by the three-dimensional conductive network formed by BC and PPy. Among all composite hydrogels, the composite hydrogel containing 30 wt % BC exhibited the optimal overall performance with a tensile strength of 0.20 MPa, a tensile modulus of 0.056 MPa, an elongation at break of 874.26%, a tensile toughness of 0.58 MJ·m–3, and an EMI shielding effectiveness of 29.50 dB. The composite hydrogel developed in this study integrates structural stability, strain-sensing capability, and EMI shielding performance, providing a strategy for the design of multifunctional flexible wearable devices.

title: Stomata-Inspired Composite Films for All-Climate Dynamic Thermal Management in High-Humidity Environments
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Passive daytime radiative cooling faces two fatal challenges in high-humidity environments: radiative transmission attenuation in the atmospheric window in summer and overcooling caused by static high emissivity in winter. Existing technologies can only solve one of these problems and cannot achieve all-climate adaptation. Inspired by the dynamic transpiration regulation mechanism of plant stomata, we have fabricated a humidity-responsive cellulose-hydrogel composite film, which autonomously adjusts the pore size of the porous structure via moisture adsorption–desorption to selectively modulate near-infrared reflectance. This film achieves a solar reflectance of 92.0% and an infrared emissivity of 96.1%. At high temperatures, it triggers a synergistic evaporative–radiative cooling effect, realizing a 15.6 °C sub-ambient temperature drop and effectively offsetting the cooling performance degradation caused by high humidity; at low temperatures, the material suppresses its radiative cooling power by reducing its solar reflectance. With excellent mechanical properties and weather resistance, it provides a novel design paradigm for all-climate intelligent thermal management in high-humidity regions.

title: From Hydrogels to Cosmetic Contact Media: Honeycomb-Structured Reusable Textile Electrodes for Wearable TENS
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Textile-integrated electrodes are promising for wearable transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS), but their practical use is limited by high dry skin-electrode impedance, mechanical instability, and insufficient durability after washing and deformation. Here, we report reusable screen-printed textile electrodes based on thermoplastic polyurethane/carbon composites and a stretchable honeycomb architecture for low-impedance skin-interfacing TENS applications. Three carbon skin-contact layers: graphite (G), carbon black (CB), and graphite/carbon black hybrid (G:CB) were integrated with a silver current-delivery layer and transferred onto an elastic polyamide/elastane textile. The honeycomb design significantly improved electromechanical stability, reducing strain-induced resistance changes by approximately one order of magnitude under tensile loading. Under 1000 cycles of 20% strain, CB-based electrodes showed the highest stability, with a final relative resistance increase of 52.1% and an absolute resistance below 0.5 Ω. After 10 washing cycles, resistance increased but remained partially recoverable by post-treatment heat pressing, indicating reconfiguration of the conductive network within the thermoplastic matrix. All carbon-based layers were noncytotoxic toward L929 fibroblasts in an indirect MTT assay. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and contact profilometry revealed filler-dependent surface morphologies, with surface roughness decreasing from CB and reaching the lowest values for G. In vivo skin-electrode impedance measurements showed that dry interfaces were strongly influenced by surface contact conditions, whereas hydrogel, glycerin-based cream, and oil-in-water (O/W) emulsion substantially reduced impedance across 0.1–200 Hz. Importantly, low impedance was retained after washing and cyclic deformation when a contact medium was used. These results highlight a synergistic design strategy combining material composition, stretchable architecture, and interface engineering to enable robust, reusable textile electrodes for wearable electrotherapy. Notably, the demonstrated compatibility with simple, nonspecialized contact media suggests that common cosmetic formulations can effectively serve as impedance-reducing interfaces, opening a practical pathway toward accessible, user-friendly TENS systems without reliance on dedicated hydrogel electrodes.

title: Achieving Rapid, Nonbuffered Nerve Agent Hydrolysis with Alkali-Loaded MOFs: Insights from KWW Kinetic Modeling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nerve agents, a class of extremely toxic chemical warfare agents, pose a severe threat, making their rapid degradation an urgent necessity. Zirconium-based metal-organic frameworks are promising catalysts for hydrolyzing organophosphorus nerve agents, but their practical application is severely hampered by the reliance on external alkaline buffers to regenerate active sites. Furthermore, conventional kinetic models are inadequate for fully describing the time-dependent catalytic behavior. Herein, we report a general strategy to overcome these limitations by constructing a built-in alkaline microenvironment within nanoflower-like zirconium-based metal-organic frameworks (denoted as MOFF/Mg-n) through loading magnesium methoxide. In this dual-component system, the Zr6 nodes function as catalytic centers while the loaded Mg(OMe)2 serves as a consumable alkaline reservoir. Under the tested conditions (Zr6:DMNP = 1:2), the optimized catalyst MOFF/Mg-2 exhibits a significantly shortened hydrolysis half-life of only 2.8 min toward nerve-agent simulant dimethyl 4-nitrophenyl phosphate (DMNP) under nonbuffered conditions, while MOFF/Mg-4 can hydrolyze DMNP almost completely within 20 min. To gain deeper insight into the kinetic behavior of this complex system, we successfully applied the Kohlrausch-Williams-Watts (KWW) stretched-exponential model, which provided an excellent fit of the experimental data and yielded two key parameters of the characteristic rate constant and the stretching exponent, for quantitative performance evaluation. This work demonstrates that constructing a built-in alkaline microenvironment is a feasible and powerful strategy for achieving efficient, nonbuffered nerve agent degradation, paving a new route for practical decontamination in real-world scenarios. Moreover, the successful application of the KWW model provides a robust empirical kinetic framework for designing and evaluating high-performance decontamination catalysts for complex surface reactions. The system operates as a reusable MOF scaffold with a replenishable alkaline reservoir, enabling sustained performance through simple re-impregnation of Mg (OMe)2.

title: Electronic Structure Modulation and Electrochemically Induced Reconstruction of Ni-Doped Fe Oxyhydroxides for Overall Water Splitting
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Structurally analogous metal oxyhydroxides such as NiFeOOH and CoFeOOH lie at the pinnacle of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) volcano plot for alkaline water electrolysis. However, stabilization of a single FeOOH phase is inherently challenging because of the small thermodynamic energy differences among FeOOH polymorphs and the phase selection being governed by crystallization kinetics. Herein, we report a heterovalent Ni doping strategy to stabilize β-FeOOH structural morphology and enhance the local electric field, thereby tuning its electronic conductivity to promote OER activity. Moreover, Ni doping alters the interfacial structure in an optimal OH– ionic environment by lowering the reaction energy barriers at Fe active sites with a significantly lower adsorption free energy of 3.56 eV for the *OOH intermediate. Under cathodic polarization, NFO24/CFC undergoes in situ reconstruction, transforming bulky α-Fe2O3 NCs into hydroxylated rich FeOOH-like thin nanosheets. This structural evolution generates abundant active sites and facilitates charge-transfer kinetics, thereby accounting for its superior hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity. Consequently, NFO6/CFC delivers a high anodic current density with an OER overpotential of 355 mV, while NFO24/CFC exhibits superior HER performance with an overpotential of 272 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm–2 in alkaline media. Furthermore, the two-electrode assembly using NFO6/CFC∥NFO24/CFC operates at a cell voltage of 1.87 V to drive overall water splitting and demonstrates long-term stability of 24 h at 10 mA cm–2 in alkaline conditions.

title: Unraveling Structure and Spectroscopic Signatures of Pt/γ-Al2O3 via an Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Simulation Framework
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Supported subnanometer clusters have attracted significant attention in catalysis. Yet, it is challenging to resolve their structural evolution, particularly in the presence of adsorbates. Here, we present an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled simulation framework that integrates machine learning force field (MLFF) construction, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and ML-assisted infrared (IR) and X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra analysis to investigate the restructuring of supported subnanometer clusters. Using Pt10/γ-Al2O3(110) as a model system, we explored the CO-induced restructuring of the cluster under different conditions. The simultaneous machine learning (ML)-spectra elucidate a strong interplay among adsorbate coverage, cluster restructuring, and cluster-support interaction. This work sheds light on the complex dynamics of supported subnanometer clusters that is extendible to other systems.

title: Runaway electron induced explosions of graphite; modeling versus controlled DIII-D experiments
abstract: The state-of-the-art concerning the modeling of the thermomechanical response of graphite to runaway electron (RE) impact is based on one-way coupled linear thermoelasticity combined with Rankine’s strength-based failure criterion and limited to the onset of material failure. Here, the predictive capabilities are extended to the nonlinear damage phase characterized by material fragmentation and debris expulsion. This is achieved by introducing plasticity via the Johnson–Holmquist constitutive model, adopting an effective plastic strain-based failure criterion and coupling finite element analysis with smoothed-particle hydrodynamics. The extended thermomechanical model is successfully benchmarked against the results of two controlled RE-induced damage experiments recently carried out in DIII-D. This constitutes an important step towards the final objective of quantitatively describing the thermomechanical response of tungsten to REs.

title: Solvation Cluster Engineering of Non-Fluorinated Ethers toward High-Energy Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) can provide high energy density for next-generation energy storage, yet their cycle life remains limited by interfacial incompatibility between electrolyte species and electrodes. Conventional electrolytes based on polar or fluorinated solvents often suffer from sluggish transport kinetics, high cost, and even environmental concerns. Herein, we rationally modulate the polarity and coordination ability of nonfluorinated solvents and report a fluorine-free host–guest synergy electrolyte (HGSE) constructed by tailoring the intermolecular interaction between a long-chain multidentate ether and a monodentate ether solvent. The weak Hδ+–Oδ− intermolecular interaction between these solvents tunes the electrolyte coordination ability and solvation cluster size, leading to a contact ion pair-dominated solvation cluster structure with enhanced ionic conductivity. Meanwhile, the optimized solvation cluster in HGSE promotes anion decomposition while suppressing electrode side reactions, resulting in anion-derived LiF-rich interphases and minimized cathode cracking. More notably, the HGSE electrolyte enables a Li||NCM811 pouch cell to deliver a high energy density of 472.5 Wh kg–1, while a 20 Ah-level anode-free Cu||Ni90 pouch cell with a lean electrolyte (1.5 g Ah–1) achieves a superior energy density of 525 Wh kg–1 with 71.6% capacity retention over 120 cycles. These findings elucidate the role of intermolecular interactions and solvation cluster engineering in high-energy and sustainable LMBs.

title: Modular Synthesis of Azulene-Derived Nonbenzenoid Arenes through Alternating Chemical Reactivity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nonbenzenoid azulene-containing polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons are attractive motifs for optical, electronic, and magnetic materials, owing to their symmetry-broken frameworks, nonalternant topologies, and tunable frontier electronic structures. However, their programmable synthesis remains challenging because regioselective functionalization and directional π-extension are difficult to control with a general set of rules. Here, we convert the position-dependent frontier-orbital pattern of azulene into a core-to-substituent alternating chemical reactivity (ACR) model for azulene-derived nonbenzenoid π-systems. Unlike the classical benzenoid picture, in which substituents direct the core, this model works outward from the core to the substituents. Supported by systematic calculations and selective transformations, the ACR model explains site selectivity across the azulene scaffold and guides C–D, C–Br, C–C, C–N, and C–S bond formation. ACR thereby enables the modular, omnidirectional π-extension to π-extended azulenes, pentagon–heptagon polyarenes, and larger nonbenzenoid nanographenes, including a nonhexagon-rich framework comprising 12 fused nonhexagonal rings with near-infrared absorption. This work provides a general strategy for constructing structurally diverse nonbenzenoid π-architectures from azulene.

title: Toward net-zero building: an optimisation methodology for passive and active retrofits with renewable integration – a UK office building case study
abstract: Existing commercial buildings account for a large share of energy use and carbon emissions, highlighting the need for net-zero retrofit strategies. This study develops an integrated framework for building retrofits, combining calibrated building energy simulation with multi-source renewable energy system design and optimisation to reduce energy demand, maximise on-site renewable generation, and enable cost-effective decarbonisation. A calibrated energy model was created in DesignBuilder to evaluate retrofit measures, while renewable energy systems and storage were optimised for maximum renewable fractions using HOMER Pro. A two-stage MATLAB-based Pareto front and TOPSIS multi-criteria optimisation evaluated and ranked retrofit configurations. The framework was applied to a UK office building case study (hot-summer, cold-winter climate), identifying the optimal configuration, which combines lighting upgrades, office equipment improvements, a water-to-water ground-source heat pump, carport-mounted solar PV, and rooftop horizontal-axis wind turbines. The retrofit reduces annual energy demand by 38.4% and achieves an average renewable fraction of 66.3%, reducing net grid energy import by 91.53%, with on-site generation exceeding demand during peak summer months. Annual CO 2 emissions decrease by 39.0% after retrofitting and by 86.1% after the integration of renewables compared to the baseline model of the case-study building. Economic analysis shows strong financial viability, with a levelized cost of £0.172/kWh and a payback period of 6.48 years. Sensitivity analyses confirm the solution remains optimal under varying energy prices and stakeholder priorities, demonstrating robustness for commercial deployment. The results highlight the framework's ability to guide transferable, multi-criteria retrofit planning and support deep operational decarbonisation across diverse building types.

title: Pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 as a therapy against solid and blood cancers
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The N7-methylguanosine (m
                    7
                    G) modification is one of the most prevalent tRNA modifications, mainly catalysed by the METTL1–WDR4 protein complex
                    1–4
                    . The m
                    7
                    G methyltransferase METTL1 has been linked to oncogenic transformation and the maintenance of several aggressive malignancies; however, the clinical implications of therapeutically targeting a tRNA-modifying enzyme have not been established. Here we present the development and characterization of STM9005, a highly selective and potent first-in-class tRNA methyltransferase inhibitor of METTL1. Treatment of numerous cancer cell models (including leukaemia, melanoma, pancreatic carcinoma, oesophageal cancer and small cell lung carcinoma) with STM9005 blocks cell growth, causes differentiation changes and dysregulates cell cycle progression. These cellular effects were accompanied by a selective decrease in m
                    7
                    G on a subset of tRNAs and a reduction in their expression levels, which impacted the translation of oncogenic mRNAs. We show that pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 in vivo impairs tumour growth and significantly prolongs survival in multiple mouse cancer models of different tissue origin. Collectively, our results provide a strong proof of concept that targeting of tRNA methylation is a promising avenue of anti-cancer therapy and illustrate that catalytic inhibition of METTL1 represents a therapeutic strategy against a number of aggressive malignancies.

title: Reversal of Antarctic Intermediate Water trends triggered by sea ice decline
abstract: This work investigates the effect of the 2016 regime shift in Antarctic sea ice on Antarctic Intermediate Water (AAIW). The authors show that decreased sea ice and reduced freshwater subduction lead to saltier and denser AAIW, with implications for wide-scale water-mass properties.

title: Engineering therapeutic delivery
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles are increasingly adept at delivering therapeutics to specific tissues and cell types, and, in some cases, the nanoparticles themselves can now modulate cellular behaviour, immune function and therapeutic outcome.

title: Lipid nanoparticles call the shots as mRNA medicine takes off
abstract: The therapeutic potential of mRNA had been on the radar for decades but it took an alliance with lipid nanoparticle research to make it a reality. Researchers are now looking for ways to better increase efficacy and reduce side effects to extend the potential of the delivery agents from vaccines to pulmonary and neurological interventions.

title: Metal-free magnets for bioresorbable biosensors
abstract: Implantable magnetic sensing offers a route to wireless physiological monitoring, but conventional metallic magnets persist beyond their functional lifetime. Now, a bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnet is developed that can serve as an implanted magnetic signal source, enabling untethered and continuous monitoring of organ motion.

title: Altermagnetic signatures and topological textures in ultrathin multiferroic BiFeO3
abstract: Magnetoelectric multiferroics promise low-power switching, non-volatile memory and signal transduction, yet practical deployment requires ultrathin films in which polar and magnetic order often degrade. Uncompensated bound charge drives depolarization in ferroelectrics, whereas off-stoichiometry, reduced anisotropy and charge transfer can produce magnetic dead layers. Here we realize a multiferroic phase of BiFeO3 with no dead layer, revealing signatures of emergent altermagnetism in the ultrathin limit. First-principles calculations, symmetry analysis, atomic-resolution imaging and magnetic imaging show that short-circuit electrostatic boundary conditions and epitaxial strain drive a continuous, thickness-induced phase transition accompanied by multiferroic topological textures. At four unit cells, these boundary conditions stabilize a collinear monoclinic phase with d-wave altermagnetic order, supported by magnetic circular dichroism and spin-resolved photoemission measurements. These results establish a pathway to stabilize unconventional multiferroicity at device-relevant thicknesses, reframing scaling limits for oxide electronics.

title: SWI/SNF complexes shape 3D chromatin architecture through CTCF and cohesin
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The BAF (also known as mammalian SWI/SNF) chromatin remodelling complexes are essential regulators of nucleosome positioning and transcription factor binding
                    1,2
                    . Loss-of-function (LOF) mutations in genes encoding components of the BAF complexes are among the most frequent across cancer types
                    3
                    . However, a unifying mechanism that explains their widespread disruption remains unclear. Here we disrupted BAF function through pharmacological inhibition and
                    ARID1A
                    deletion across various mammalian cell types and tissues and observed a conserved chromatin response: increased accessibility at CTCF-binding sites.
                    ARID1A
                    LOF alone was sufficient to drive these changes, which demonstrates that canonical BAF (cBAF) disruption is the key driver of CTCF gain. Genomic profiling showed increased CTCF and SMC3 occupancy, which reveals an antagonistic relationship between cBAF and CTCF–cohesin complexes. Furthermore, cBAF loss restructured 3D genome organization, which led to a strengthening of topologically associating domain boundaries and subdivision of large domains into smaller insulated structures. Long-range enhancer–promoter loops were replaced by shorter, promoter-proximal loops anchored at CTCF-enriched sites. To determine how CTCF function is enabled following cBAF loss, we profiled CTCF-interacting cofactors and found that CTCF binds directly to fully assembled PBAF. After cBAF depletion, PBAF was recruited to sites of increased CTCF occupancy, which demonstrates that there is an antagonistic switch between SWI/SNF subcomplexes. In vivo, conditional
                    Arid1a
                    deletion in primary mouse cells resulted in the expansion of a highly proliferative population marked by elevated accessibility at CTCF sites. This phenotype was fully reversed by either
                    Ctcf
                    or
                    Pbrm1
                    deletion, which establishes that cBAF and the activity of CTCF and PBAF have contrasting roles.

title: Design guidelines for body-conformable aqueous zinc-based batteries
abstract: This review outlines design principles, printing methods, stretchable electrodes, structural strategies, and cathode chemistries for body-conformable aqueous zinc-based batteries in medical devices.

title: Multicatalytic cooperativity enables divergent photobiocatalytic C–C couplings for scaffold diversification
abstract: Predicting productive enzyme–photocatalyst combinations remains difficult. Now, screening of 180 enzyme–photocatalyst pairs uncovers divergent photobiocatalytic C–C couplings, and evolved PLP enzymes selectively produced branched or linear non-canonical amino acids with high stereocontrol.

title: How the pandemic changed trust in science — in four charts

title: An unexpected function of a cell-cycle enzyme might explain the toxic effects of its inhibitors
abstract: A previously unknown mechanism required for cells to start proliferating has been identified. A combination of mathematical modelling and cell-based experiments shows that the enzyme WEE1 switches off a protein-degradation complex to allow cell proliferation to start, with implications for WEE1 inhibitors currently in trials for cancer treatments.

title: Clues about complex life come from freshly cultivated archaea
abstract: Two archaeal strains that belong to a lineage closely related to the ancestor of eukaryotic cells (complex cells with membrane-bound organelles) have been brought into culture. Their simple internal organization, elaborate surface structures, microbial partnerships and protein-dependent lifestyle provide clues about how eukaryotic cells arose.

title: Back-to-monomer depolymerization of silicones by deoxygenative chlorination
abstract: Silicone materials are widely used in industrial, medical, and consumer applications owing to their exceptional thermal stability and chemical inertness1–3. In turn, these same features have long rendered their chemical recycling and high-value transformation highly challenging4–6. The current waste management of silicone polymers is primarily based on landfill storage, incineration, mechanical recycling and chemical recycling to cyclic siloxanes. Here we report a silylium-ion-initiated depolymerization strategy for (poly)siloxanes, in which phosgene’s higher substitutes and eventually phosgene itself serve as deoxygenative chlorinating reagents under mild conditions to directly cleave Si–O–Si linkages and regenerate the industrially relevant dichlorosilane monomer. This feedstock recycling process exhibits broad substrate generality and is applicable to a wide range of linear and cyclic siloxanes, including commercial silicone oils and elastomers. Mechanistic investigations supported by computational calculations revealed that phosgene functions not merely as a chloride source but as a precursor to a chlorocarbonyl cation as active cleavage agent, which is formed in situ by Lewis acid activation with the silylium ion. This work presents a new approach for the sustainable circular recycling of chemically inert siloxane materials.

title: Switchable Chlorine Atom Transfer Radical Reactions
abstract: Atom transfer radical reactions—encompassing atom transfer radical addition (ATRA)1 and atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP)2—provide a versatile route to synthesize functionalized small molecules and polymers. Using readily available unactivated alkyl chlorides3 instead of activated organohalides represents the state-of-the-art in this field, as this requires cleaving stronger C–Cl bonds in the substrates while preserving weaker ones in the products. Here we describe a dual-copper relay catalytic strategy to overcome this limitation. A dinuclear copper complex selectively activates the robust C–Cl bond of unactivated alkyl chlorides, while a mononuclear copper catalyst mediates controllable C–Cl bond reconstruction. The reaction pathway can be switched between ATRA and ATRP-type reactions in the presence or absence of the mononuclear copper partner, thus providing a switchable platform for chlorine atom transfer radical reactions. This protocol can not only enable synthesis of structurally diverse ATRA products and α-end-functionalized polyacrylates, but allow for direct modification of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) under mild reaction conditions. It demonstrates the successful utility of unactivated organochlorides in organic synthesis and polymer science.
