title: Machine Learning‐Driven Vapor Passivation Enables Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have achieved remarkable power conversion efficiency (PCE) recently, yet the device instability induced by defects remains a bottleneck. Despite the effectiveness of passivation strategies in reducing defects, conventional solution‐based methods may compromise the perovskite crystallinity. Thus, vapor‐based molecules are expected to penetrate into crystals and reduce defects. Screening effective vapor‐assisted passivation materials usually takes substantial trial‐and‐error costs. Here, we propose a hybrid workflow integrating machine learning models with first‐principles calculations to screen the key functional groups for vapor‐assisted passivation molecules and provide physical insights. The phenyl and halogen atoms were identified by Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) analysis to be effective. Theoretical calculations also indicated that there was a strong cation‐ π interaction between Pb 2+ and benzene ring. Besides, halogenated benzene could intercalate into the iodine vacancies on perovskite surfaces. Such robust interactions synergistically contribute to the stability of [PbI 6 ] 4− octahedral framework, and thus the formation of defects and structural collapse could be effectively suppressed. Moreover, the thermal conductivity of modified perovskite films was remarkably enhanced. Finally, the device modified with iodobenzene vapor achieved the champion PCE of 26.94%. This workflow integrating data‐driven discovery and atomistic understandings, provides an innovative strategy to screen vapor‐assisted passivation materials.

title: Sustainable Biomass‐Based Fiber Materials as Structural and Functional Scaffolds for Advanced Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Biomass‐based fiber materials, including cellulose, chitosan, bacterial cellulose, and their derivatives, have emerged as a distinctive class of structural and functional scaffolds, effectively bridging renewable materials chemistry with advanced energy storage technologies. This review systematically elucidates their hierarchical structural characteristics, classifications, and the intrinsic structural‐function‐application relationships that underpin their versatility. Furthermore, the critical roles of these materials as key components‐including solid‐state/liquid electrolytes, separators, electrodes, and binders‐in various metal battery systems, particularly lithium‐ and zinc‐based batteries, are comprehensively summarized. The discussion further highlights how the rational architectural design of biomass‐derived fibrous materials can significantly enhance ionic conductivity, interfacial stability, and mechanical integrity. By improving these fundamental properties, such materials provide effective strategies for addressing major challenges, including dendrite formation and cycling instability. Finally, the current challenges and future research perspectives are discussed, with particular emphasis on precise molecular‐level design, scalable fabrication technologies, and standardized evaluation protocols, all of which are essential for advancing the development of next‐generation green and sustainable energy storage devices.

title: Mixed‐Antisolvent Engineering for Crystallization and Defect Regulation in Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT The performance of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) remains critically dependent on the quality of the perovskite absorber, which is largely established during the antisolvent‐assisted crystallization process. Single‐antisolvent engineering, however, is often constrained by the fixed physicochemical properties of the chosen solvent, leaving limited flexibility to balance solvent extraction, crystallization modulation, and defect suppression. Herein, we report a physicochemical‐property‐assisted binary‐antisolvent engineering for high‐efficiency inverted PSCs. A series of binary antisolvent combinations were screened by considering key solvent properties, among which the carbon disulfide/anisole (CS 2 :ANI) system delivered the best device performance. Comprehensive chemical, structural, and optical characterizations reveal that the CS 2 :ANI system enables a more coordinated crystallization process by regulating solvent removal and modifying the precursor environment through interactions between CS 2 ‐derived C═N‐containing species and the Pb–I framework. The resulting perovskite films exhibit compact morphology, reduced residual stress, and suppressed defect‐assisted nonradiative recombination. The optimized inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.73% and a steady‐state output efficiency of 26.43%.

title: Dynamic Hydrogen‑Bond Network Accelerates Lattice Oxygen Regeneration for High‑Current‑Density Seawater Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Seawater electrolysis for green H 2 production is hindered by the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and chloride corrosion at the anode. Although the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) can effectively reduce the overpotential, the sluggish mass transport of OH − at high current densities disrupts the oxygen release–regeneration balance, ultimately leading to a trade‐off between activity and stability. Here, we demonstrate that yttrium (Y) and carboxylate co‐doping reconstruct the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network of NiFe oxyhydroxide, dynamically accelerating OH − delivery and enabling rapid regeneration of lattice oxygen. This catalyst maintains a high LOM contribution (51.7%–54%) while achieving exceptional durability and Cl − resistance. In situ Raman, differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), and rotating ring‐disk electrode (RRDE) analyses confirm rapid peroxide intermediate formation, lattice oxygen participation, and negligible chlorine evolution. The anion‐exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyzer delivers 1000 mA cm −2 at 1.79 V and operates stably for 800 h in alkaline seawater. This work establishes interfacial hydrogen‐bonding engineering as a generalizable strategy to break the activity–stability trade‐off for robust seawater electrolysis.

title: Solvent‐Free Metal–Organic Framework‐Based Porous Liquid Electrolyte for Ultrahigh‐Temperature (180°C) Zn Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Zn metal batteries capable of withstanding ultrahigh temperatures are urgently needed across diverse fields, yet their development is hindered by the poor thermal adaptability of conventional electrolytes. Herein, we develop an innovative electrolyte paradigm represented by a metal–organic framework (MOF)‐based porous liquid electrolyte (PLE) without active organic or H 2 O solvents, which enables long‐term operation of Zn metal batteries at 180°C for the first time. Modeled on UiO‐66, PLE combines permanent microporosity with liquid fluidity, offering non‐flammability, thermal stability, and anode compatibility. The permanent micropores of the UiO‐66 skeleton provide ordered nanoconfined ion transport channels, while flexible grafted polymeric chains offer coordination‐dissociation hopping sites, and ultimately suppress dendrite growth even at high temperatures. Zn||Zn symmetric cells deliver ultra‐long cycling lifespans of 10 000 h at 25°C, 4000 h at 120°C, 2100 h at 150°C, and 600 h at 180°C, far surpassing state‐of‐the‐art Zn battery electrolytes. Zn||V 2 O 5 batteries deliver stable performance across 25−180°C. Moreover, the pore structure of PLE effectively adsorbs polyiodides and polysulfides, enabling high‐temperature Zn||I 2 batteries and, remarkably, extending to Li||S (80°C) and Li||V 2 O 5 batteries (180°C). This work enriches the design philosophy of functional electrolytes and breaks the long‐standing temperature barrier of metal batteries.

title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Chiral 1,4‐Dicarbonyls Bearing All‐Carbon Quaternary Stereocenters via Photoredox/Nickel Dual Catalyzed Tandem Radical Addition/Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT The asymmetric synthesis of 1,4‐dicarbonyl compounds bearing all‐carbon quaternary stereocenters remains a significant challenge in organic synthesis. Herein, we report a photoredox/nickel dual‐catalyzed tandem radical addition and oxidation protocol that directly converts β ‐keto esters and styrenes into enantioenriched 1,4‐dicarbonyl products in a single operation. This approach harnesses the synergistic cooperation of a photocatalyst and a chiral nickel catalyst to generate α ‐carbonyl radicals chelated to the chiral catalyst, via single‐electron oxidation of in situ‐formed Ni‐enolate complexes. The resulting radical intermediates are stereoselectively trapped by alkenes, and the ensuing benzyl radicals are subsequently oxidized by molecular oxygen to furnish the desired scaffolds. This catalytic system operates under mild conditions using molecular oxygen as the terminal oxidant, thereby obviating the need for prefunctionalized coupling partners while offering excellent functional group compatibility and broad substrate scope.

title: Atomic‐Shell Amplification of Intrinsic Coordination Asymmetry Enables Giant Optical Nonlinearity
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing bulk nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals that simultaneously combine outstanding optical performance with excellent crystal growth capability remains a major challenge. Here, we introduce an intrinsic coordination asymmetry strategy that exploits highly polarizable tetrahedral Hg–S coordination and conformationally flexible ligands to amplify local structural distortions within discrete homoanionic modules. Guided by this concept, Cc ‐(NH 4 ) 2 Hg(SCN) 4 ( Cc ‐AHT) and its C 2/ c polymorph were synthesized. Structural and theoretical investigations reveal that the flexible (SCN) − ligands propagate distortions originating in the [HgS 4 ] core throughout the [Hg(SCN) 4 ] 2− module, establishing an atomic‐shell distortion amplification model that quantitatively traces the evolution of local coordination asymmetry. Cc ‐AHT exhibits a giant second‐harmonic generation response (14 × KH 2 PO 4 and 1.2 × KTiOPO 4 at 1064 nm), a band gap of 3.25 eV, and large birefringence (Δ n = 0.341 at 1064 nm), while centimeter‐sized single crystals can be readily grown under mild conditions. This work establishes intrinsic coordination asymmetry and its atomic‐shell amplification as a chemically guided strategy for designing high‐performance homoanionic NLO materials and provides a general framework for understanding how local structural distortions propagate through coordination modules containing conformationally flexible ligands.

title: Bromide‐Activated Four‐Electron Iodine Chemistry Enabled by a Pyridinium‐Integrated Hydrogel Electrolyte
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous four‐electron zinc–iodine (Zn–I 2 ) batteries offer high capacity and operating voltage, yet most reported systems rely on Cl − to activate the I 0 /I + conversion, generating hydrolysis‐prone ICl 2 − intermediates that cause rapid capacity decay. However, how inner I‐X bond polarization (X = F, Cl, and Br) governs the hydrolytic stability of interhalogen intermediates remains unclear. Here, we conduct both experimental and computational analyses, revealing Br − as the most effective halide. Compared with F − and Cl − , Br − forms less‐polarized and more hydrolytically stable IBr 2 − intermediates, markedly improving high‐voltage iodine reversibility. Building on this Br − ‐mediated stabilization, we further design a multifunctional PNA‐PyBr hydrogel electrolyte by incorporating pyridine hydrobromide into a sulfonate‐rich poly(sodium p ‐styrenesulfonate‐ co ‐acrylamide) network. Pyridinium cations immobilize IBr 2 − as water‐insoluble Py + IBr 2 − complexes, protecting I + species from hydrolysis, while sulfonate groups regulate the aqueous hydrogen‐bond network and establish Zn 2+ ‐selective transport pathways. The resulting cells deliver a near‐theoretical capacity of 422.6 mAh g −1 and a record lifespan of over 20 000 cycles at 20 C. Moreover, a 500 mAh pouch cell with an areal capacity of 3.5 mAh cm −2 sustains 600 cycles with negligible capacity decay, demonstrating the practical potential of Br − ‐activated four‐electron Zn–I 2 chemistry.

title: Atroposelective Construction of Tetra‐ ortho ‐Substituted Dibenz[ c , e ]azepines Using an Engineered Imine Reductase
abstract: ABSTRACT Atropisomeric dibenz[ c , e ]azepines are privileged scaffolds in asymmetric synthesis, medicinal chemistry, and materials science, yet their atroposelective preparation remains challenging due to the difficulty of controlling axial chirality while constructing a strained medium‐sized ring. Tetra‐ ortho ‐substituted dibenz[ c , e ]azepines are especially elusive, with no catalytic asymmetric method reported owing to extreme steric hindrance. Here, we report the first biocatalytic strategy for the atroposelective synthesis of these congested bridged biaryls, employing an engineered imine reductase (IRED) that catalyzes a sequential inter‐ and intramolecular reductive amination cascade. Structure‐guided directed evolution of an IRED from Streptomyces tricolor provided a triple mutant (IRED‐04‐M3) that delivers various tetra‐ ortho ‐substituted dibenz[ c , e ]azepines in high yields with excellent atroposelectivity (up to 97% yield, >99:1 er) by dynamic kinetic resolution. Gram‐scale preparation was also demonstrated. Mechanistic studies and molecular dynamics simulations provide insight into the cascade reaction and stereocontrol exerted by the engineered enzyme.

title: Molecular Basis of NPY Recognition and Ligand Selectivity at the Neuropeptide Y 5 Receptor
abstract: ABSTRACT Neuropeptide Y receptors (YRs) have been demonstrated to mediate physiological functions such as food intake, energy expenditure and mood regulation. Despite the low sequence identity exhibited by the four YR subtypes, Y 1 R, Y 2 R, Y 4 R, and Y 5 R, all of them recognize the endogenous ligand neuropeptide Y (NPY), which demonstrates their complex ligand recognition and activation mechanisms. The Y 5 R is regarded as a promising drug target for cachexia and cancer, but drug development has been hampered by the lack of structural information on ligand‐Y 5 R interactions. We report the cryo‐electron microscopy structure of Y 5 R in complex with NPY and the G i1 protein, revealing unique features of the Y 5 R extracellular regions that participate in ligand recognition and illustrating the specific binding mode of the NPY C‐terminus to Y 5 R. The structural information is supported by mutagenesis studies investigating ligand binding and receptor activation with the endogenous ligand NPY and the selective Y 5 R agonist sY 5 ago. Structural analysis provides valuable insights into the factors driving receptor subtype selectivity, thus offering an opportunity for drug discovery of Y 5 R.

title: Light‐Driven Surface Lattice Oxygen Activation in Oxygen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a key bottleneck in sustainable hydrogen production and energy conversion. Conventional pathways such as the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) and lattice oxygen oxidation mechanism (LOM) both suffer from electron‐transfer inefficiencies at their potential‐determining steps ( * OOH formation in AEM and deprotonation in LOM) and structural instability (metal oxidation in AEM and oxygen‐vacancy accumulation in LOM). As a result, a unified mechanism that simultaneously overcomes these kinetic limitations and structural degradation processes remains absent. Here, we present a light‐driven surface lattice oxygen activation mechanism (LSOM) that synergizes photoexcitation and electrocatalysis to activate surface lattice oxygen into high‐energy non‐bonding orbitals, enabling their direct participation in O─O bond formation. This strategy circumvents the potential‐determining steps inherent to both AEM and LOM, while preserving metal oxidation states and lattice structural integrity. Experimental validation confirms remarkable enhancements in electrocatalytic activity and stability, outperforming conventional OER systems. By unifying catalytic efficiency with structural durability, the LSOM redefines the design principles for OER and establishes a universal framework for robust energy conversion technologies.

title: Anisotropic Near‐Infrared Amplified Spontaneous Emission in Single‐Benzene Organic Crystals
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic materials capable of near‐infrared (NIR) amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) are attractive for compact photonic and sensing technologies, yet efficient NIR ASE typically requires extended π‐conjugated frameworks. Herein, we report a structurally simple donor– π –acceptor (D– π –A) dye molecule, butyl (2E,4E)‐2‐cyano‐5‐(4‐(dimethylamino)phenyl)penta‐2,4‐dienoate ( M1 ), containing only a single benzene ring, that exhibits efficient NIR emission and ASE. Despite its limited π ‐conjugation, M1 crystals show a photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of up to 19% and NIR emission centered at 760 nm with a large Stokes shift. Notably, M1 crystals over a broad range of dimensions exhibit ASE, indicating that ASE generation does not require a narrowly defined crystal size. The ASE response also varies substantially with crystallographic orientation. Block‐ and plate‐like crystals exhibit direction‐dependent ASE along distinct crystallographic axes, whereas rod‐ and needle‐like crystals simultaneously generate two ASE bands centered at approximately 750 and 670 nm along the growth direction. In contrast, the analogous tert‐butyl derivative exhibits markedly weaker emission and no detectable ASE, underscoring the importance of substituent flexibility and crystal packing. These results show that pronounced and direction‐dependent NIR ASE can be realized in organic crystals with remarkably limited π ‐conjugation.

title: Orthogonal Chemical Encoding Enables Sequence‐Independent GlycoRNA Imaging in Organoids and Tissues
abstract: ABSTRACT Current methods for imaging glycosylated RNAs (glycoRNAs) rely on sequence‐specific recognition or bulky DNA nanostructures, which compromise spatial fidelity and largely confine applications to simplified cell systems. Here, we report a Co valent M olecular P roximity Ass ay (COMPASS) that enables sequence‐independent visualization of glycoRNAs in complex physiological contexts. COMPASS integrates orthogonal encoding with proximity‐gated signal readout. Through chemoselective precursor uptake, azide groups are installed on terminal sialic acids and alkyne groups on nascent uridine residues, establishing a dual‐encoded chemical framework. Independent analysis confirmed the efficient installation of both functionalities. Subsequent dual‐color click labeling introduces donor and acceptor fluorophores to these orthogonal handles, producing sensitized acceptor emission when they are located in the same glycoRNA molecule. Accordingly, COMPASS reports the metabolically labeled, sialylated, uridine‐containing glycoRNA population generated during the labeling window. This design eliminates the need for bulky nucleic acid probes, reduces probe‐induced signal spreading, and enables glycoRNA imaging across diverse systems, including cell cultures, cerebral organoids, and mouse tissues. COMPASS revealed spatially heterogeneous glycoRNA‐associated signals, including relatively stronger signals near lumen‐adjacent VZ‐like regions of cerebral organoids and lower signals in pulmonary metastatic nodules. These observations establish spatial associations with neurodevelopmental and tumor‐associated states.

title: Cu/Ce Bimetallic Porphyrin MOFs with Enhanced Charge Transfer for Efficient Photocatalytic–Photothermal Sterilization
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract A series of bimetallic CuxCey (x = 1–5, y = 10 – x) metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) were prepared via a solvothermal method. Results reveal that the coordination between Cu2+ and the central N atoms of the porphyrin ring is consistent with partial metallation of the porphyrin macrocycle and alters excited-state and charge-transfer behavior, which contributes to the enhanced photocatalytic bactericidal activity. The Cu/Ce bimetallic sites alter the excited-state and charge-transfer behavior of the framework, which may facilitate the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), including singlet oxygen (1O2), while the photothermal effect derived from TCPP ligands contributes to bacterial inactivation. Under visible light irradiation (0.2 W cm–2, λ ≥ 420 nm) for 15 min, the optimized Cu2Ce8 achieves a bactericidal rate of over 99.99% against Escherichia coli (E. coli), and the bactericidal rate remains above 90% after 4 recycling cycles.

title: A Microscopic View of Protein Soft and Reactive Landing on Flexible Polyethylene Glycol Surfaces
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The interaction of proteins with polymer surfaces is central to understanding biomaterial compatibility and developing advanced deposition techniques. In this work, we investigate the collision dynamics of lysozyme and neurotensin with polyethylene glycol (PEG) surfaces in the vacuum using the reactive force field (ReaxFF). These simulations mimic the soft and reactive landing processes encountered in electrospray ionization (ESI)-, matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization (MALDI)- and cluster ion beam-based preparative mass spectrometry approaches. Various PEG structures, including vertically aligned chains and amorphous configurations, with or without surface chain terminations, were considered. Collision velocities ranging from 1 to 6 km/s were employed to explore structural preservation, energy transfer, and chemical bond formation between the biomolecules and the PEG. For lysozyme (∼14 kDa), where 1 km/s corresponds to approximately 74 eV, our results show that PEG acts as a soft, cushion-like substrate, effectively dissipating impact energy and preserving protein structure under most conditions. Notably, covalent bond formation was observed only at high velocity (≥5 km/s) in the amorphous PEG structure lacking surface chain terminations. The findings indicate that PEG offers a promising medium for preserving protein integrity during deposition, maintaining the capacity to build protein multilayers, and potentially facilitating controlled protein desorption in solvents when desired. Even though defining an exact energy threshold would require a more detailed investigation, our simulations also constitute a proof-of-principle that the molecular fragments also transferred in iBEAM may act as mediators to induce protein grafting at relatively low velocity (3 km/s).

title: Thermosensitive Hydroxybutyl Polyvinyl Alcohol Hydrogel for Vaginal Delivery of Progesterone Microcrystals to Treat Endometrial Hyperplasia
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Endometrial hyperplasia (EH), a common precursor lesion to endometrial carcinoma, represents a major gynecological challenge. Current noninvasive vaginal treatments are severely hampered by poor retention and inadequate mucosal adhesion. Herein, we developed a novel thermosensitive hydroxybutyl polyvinyl alcohol (HBPVA) hydrogel for efficient localized vaginal delivery of progesterone. By grafting hydrophobic hydroxybutyl groups onto the hydrophilic PVA backbone, the resulting HBPVA hydrogel exhibited good flowability at 4 °C and a rapid sol-gel transition at 37 °C. Progesterone microcrystals were directly incorporated into the HBPVA solution via simple physical mixing, yielding a stable formulation (Pro@HBPVA) without the need for organic solvents or purification. The thermosensitive hydrogel, once gelled at body temperature, leveraged its abundant surface hydroxyl groups to achieve superior mucoadhesion compared to commercial F127 hydrogel (mucosal adhesion duration >10 times that of the F127 control). Ex vivo fluorescence imaging revealed that the fluorescein-labeled HBPVA hydrogel was retained in the vaginal tract 4-fold longer and at significantly higher levels than a fluorescein sodium solution. Furthermore, the HBPVA formulation enabled preferential uterine accumulation with prolonged therapeutic exposure (>24 h). In an estrogen-induced EH rat model, Pro@HBPVA demonstrated superior therapeutic efficacy to intramuscular progesterone oil injection (positive control), effectively reducing uterine wet weight, restoring endometrial thickness and apoptosis balance, suppressing excessive endometrial angiogenesis and proliferation, and attenuating local inflammation to levels comparable to healthy controls. Collectively, with proven biocompatibility, this mucoadhesive platform offers an effective and noninvasive strategy for EH treatment.

title: Facet- and Size-Related Electrical Conductivity and Piezocatalytic Behaviors of Co3O4 Crystals from Lattice Deviation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Size-tunable Co3O4 cubes (136 and 276 nm), cuboctahedra (168 and 240 nm), and octahedra (180 and 258 nm) have been hydrothermally synthesized. Synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis suggests best fitting of peaks into bulk and surface layer lattice components for all the samples. Fast Fourier transform (FFT) processing of high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) images shows a regular array of lattice points in the interior bulk but significant spot distortion in the surface layer. The surface lattice deviation patterns are distinct for different particle morphologies. Their band gaps can vary with particle size and shape. For the smaller crystals, an octahedron is electrically highly conductive, but a cube is nearly insulating from representative single-particle measurements. Cuboctahedra and octahedra also show higher piezoelectric responses than cubes do. Regardless of the particle shape, the smaller crystals are clearly more piezocatalytically effective at dye degradation than the larger ones. Active species generated in piezocatalysis have been identified. Lattice deviations from crystal shape control is a good way to enhance material properties.

title: First Evidence and Role of γ -Fe2O3 Seeds in Low-Temperature-Processed Sn-Doped Hematite Photoanodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sn doping is an effective strategy to improve the photoelectrochemical response of hematite photoanodes, but its activation typically requires high-temperature treatments that can degrade conductive substrates and limit device integration. Considering photoelectrochemical water splitting as a case study, this work investigates the mechanism of photoelectrochemical activation of Sn-doped hematite-based photoanodes by oxidative annealing of thin metallic Fe–Sn alloy films at a low temperature. X-ray absorption spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction, and electron paramagnetic resonance reveal that while hematite is the main crystalline phase, poorly ordered γ-Fe2O3 seeds selectively form in Sn-containing films annealed at 450 °C and progressively transform into Sn-doped α-Fe2O3 at higher annealing temperatures. Under solar illumination in 1 M KOH, photoanodes annealed at 450 °C exhibit photocurrent density (≈480 μA/cm2) and onset potential (≈0.9 V vs RHE) comparable to those obtained after annealing at a higher temperature (750 °C). Sn K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy identifies Sn4+ in local Sn–Fe coordination environments consistent with incorporation into the hematite lattice. The γ-Fe2O3 domains may act as transient Sn reservoirs, accommodating Sn beyond the hematite solubility limit and promoting the formation of well-ordered, photoactive Sn-doped α-Fe2O3 nanocrystals, while limiting SnO2 segregation at an Sn/(Fe + Sn) atomic ratio of approximately 3 at %. Control films deposited under an oxygen atmosphere contain a lower γ-Fe2O3 fraction and show poor activity, indicating that low-temperature activation arises not from Sn addition alone but requires oxidation-driven restructuring of the metallic Fe–Sn precursor. The γ-Fe2O3 seeds represent structural fingerprints of a synthesis pathway that enables efficient Sn incorporation and low-thermal-budget fabrication of hematite photoanodes for solar water splitting.

title: Dual-Mode Memristors with Controlled Cluster Dynamics for High-Performance Neuromorphic Computing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In the process of realizing brain-like information processing based on artificial synapses, the conductive filament (CF) model has become an intensively studied topic. Its significant attraction stems from its ability to emulate the dynamic evolution of synaptic connection strengths in biological systems. However, owing to its inherent geometrical structural defects, traditional CF exhibits significant uncontrollability during its growth and dissolution processes, severely limiting the stability and accuracy of its synaptic function simulation. To address this limitation, a synaptic device was constructed in this study that features a dual-active-layer composed of polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP): graphene-oxide quantum dots (GO QDs), and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA). The thin PVA active layer enables compliance-current-controlled regulation of dendritic conductive filaments, resulting in volatile switching at low compliance currents and nonvolatile switching at higher compliance currents, thereby enabling compliance-current-controlled dual-mode operation. Ag ions originating from the electrochemically active Ag electrode migrate into the active layer driven by the external electric field and are reduced in situ around the GO QDs in the PVP:GO QDs nanocomposite layer, forming uniformly distributed and controllable silver clusters (Ag-C), resulting in enhanced device stability and improved synaptic emulation capability. The proposed mechanism is consistent with the voltage-dependent SEM/EDS observations and previously reported charge-trapping characteristics of GO QD-containing materials. Experimental results confirmed that diverse synaptic behaviors can be realized in the device. Meanwhile, a neural-network simulation based on its synaptic characteristics demonstrated its excellent performance (94.0%) in learning and inference tasks. Such performance further highlights the potential of the device for constructing reliable neuromorphic computing architectures.

Deconstructing the Nanoscale Electromechanical Response of Mixed Conductors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) techniques, which probe nanoscale electromechanical coupling, are often difficult to interpret. For ferroelectric mixed conductors useful for computation elements, this becomes more difficult due to non-piezoelectric electromechanical effects. The measured PFM signal can have tip-local and nonlocal contributions associated with multiple coupling mechanisms, and it is often unclear what material property is truly being probed. Here, using antimony sulfide (Sb2S3) as a model system, an emerging phase change material for optical and electrical memory and computation elements, we show that the PFM signal can be separated into a fast, capacitive contribution, and a slow, ionic contribution whose time-domain characteristics match well with diffusion-controlled kinetics. This ionic contribution, rather than ferroelectric switching, leads to electromechanical hysteresis in Sb2S3, with no clearly measurable ferroelectric switching effects. Uniquely, electromechanical behavior has a very clear spatial contrast that is decoupled from surface topography, showing that the signal arises from surface charging that reflects bulk-like properties and allowing a self-consistent interpretation in terms of dielectric behavior. This protocol establishes a clear interpretation of a non-piezoelectric signal, often mischaracterized as an indication of the ferroelectric state. Additionally, because all electromechanical experiments show a strong, low-frequency electric relaxation in crystalline Sb2S3 while the response of glassy Sb2S3 is static, we conclude that the crystalline phase of Sb2S3 is a mixed conductor, while the amorphous phase remains strictly insulating.

Hybrid Membrane-Coated Nanoplatform Enables Pyroptosis-Driven Photothermal Immunotherapy via Synergistic STING/TLR4 Activation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) remains a major barrier to effective cancer immunotherapy, largely due to deficient activation of innate immune pathways and insufficient immune cell infiltration. To address this issue, we developed a hybrid biomimetic nanoplatform (CL8-BO NPs + CLPS) that encapsulates a near-infrared photothermal agent (L8-BO) and the Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) agonist lipopolysaccharide, respectively, and is surface-functionalized with a mixed macrophage–red blood cell membrane, with the two components used in synergy. Upon 808 nm laser irradiation, L8-BO generated localized hyperthermia, inducing gasdermin D-dependent pyroptosis, which released cytosolic DNA and damage-associated molecular patterns to activate the stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway. Concurrently, released lipopolysaccharide engaged TLR4 signaling, potentiating innate immune activation. In a subcutaneous 4T1 breast carcinoma model, intratumoral administration of CL8-BO NPs followed by laser irradiation remodeled the immunosuppressive TME by promoting dendritic cell maturation, enhancing intratumoral CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration by 5-fold, and suppressing regulatory T cells and myeloid-derived suppressor cells. The combination therapy inhibits tumor growth by over 90%. This nanoplatform provides a promising strategy for converting “cold” tumors into “hot” tumors through photothermal–triggered pyroptosis and synergistic STING/TLR4 activation in a localized delivery model.

title: Construction of Single-Atom Cobalt in Ordered Mesoporous Metal–Organic Frameworks for Boosting CO2 Conversion
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Constructing single-atom transition-metal-implanted mesoporous metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2 conversion is of great importance for achieving carbon neutrality, yet remains a formidable challenge. This work presents a modular optimization of cerium-based metal–organic frameworks by incorporating Co single atoms with ordered mesopores (OMCU). These periodically arranged mesopores in OMCU were fabricated by synergistically combining the Hofmeister effect with a soft-template structure-oriented strategy. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the Co single atoms could not only accelerate photogenerated electron participation in CO2 conversion but also lower the energy barrier by promoting the formation of a new intermediate, *OCHO, along a specific reduction pathway, as directly observed by in situ Raman and operando ATR-IR spectroscopy. Density functional theory calculations corroborate that Co atoms favor the generation of *OCHO-related intermediates, omitting the high energy input for CO2·– formation and resulting in outstanding CO2 reduction performance, which is equivalent to a 10.84-fold enhancement in CO generation rate compared to that of the pristine MOF in the presence of TEA and bipyridinium ruthenium. This work provides an effective strategy through the construction of active cobalt sites within ordered mesoporous cerium-based MOFs for modulating the key intermediates in CO2 photoreduction.

title: Vertical van der Waals Graphene/h-BN/SnS2 Top-Floating-Gate Memory for Optoelectronic Storage and Neuromorphic Computing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nonvolatile memories based on two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures have attracted considerable attention because of their atomic-scale thickness, low energy operation, and prolonged data storage capability. However, most reported vdW floating-gate memories employ a bottom-floating-gate configuration, which often leads to a limited on/off ratio due to charge leakage and substrate-induced disturbance. Herein, a top-floating-gate memory based on a graphene (Gr)/h-BN/SnS2 vdW heterostructure is demonstrated, in which the top graphene layer serves as the charge-trapping layer. The device exhibits excellent nonvolatile memory performance, including an on/off ratio of 106, a memory window of 50.8 V, a low standby current of 1 pA, and an extrapolated retention time of 10 years. Owing to the low hole-tunneling barrier between SnS2 and h-BN, the device achieves more than 50 progressively modulated conductance levels under a weak optical pulse of 0.74 nW·mm–2. Moreover, stable long-term potentiation and depression characteristics can be regulated by optical and electrical pulses. Based on these synaptic behaviors, a three-layer multilayer perceptron neural network using the floating-gate memory achieved a classification accuracy of 96% for handwritten digit recognition using the Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology (MNIST) dataset. This work presents a top-floating-gate architecture for 2D-material memories, providing a feasible strategy for future logic-in-memory and neuromorphic computing applications.

title: Supramolecular Pulley Effect Enabling Highly Stretchable Transparent Electrodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Silver nanowires (AgNWs) are promising materials for stretchable transparent electrodes (STEs) due to their high aspect ratio, excellent electrical conductivity, and optical transparency. However, the flexibility of AgNW-based STEs is often constrained by the significant modulus mismatch between the rigid AgNWs and soft polymer substrates. Herein, we introduce acrylated polyrotaxane (PRA) between the AgNW network and a polyurethane (PU) substrate, resulting in a highly stretchable and transparent electrode. The pulley effect of the acrylated polyrotaxane helps alleviate stress concentration at the AgNW–PU interface. Therefore, the network structure of AgNWs can remain relatively intact even under large tensile strains. The resulting composite electrode combines a transmittance of about 86.8%, a sheet resistance of 47 Ω·sq–1, and a stretchability of up to 130%. The as-prepared AgNWs/PRA/PU electrode demonstrates great potential for applications in stretchable electroluminescent devices and electrophysiological signal monitoring. This study offers a straightforward and effective strategy for developing high-performance stretchable electrodes, presenting a viable pathway for next-generation electronic devices.

title: A two-stage real-time equalization control strategy for off-grid multi-electrolyzer systems considering electrolyzer degradation
Carbon–ITO Composite Electrodes with Silver Leaf Current Collectors for Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing vacuum-free and potentially scalable top electrodes is essential for the practical deployment of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Here, a hybrid carbon-based composite electrode is developed by incorporating carbon black and colloidal indium tin oxide (ITO) nanoparticles into a commercial carbon paste, followed by lamination of a silver (Ag) leaf as a highly conductive current collector. The resulting carbon–ITO/Ag architecture exhibits substantially improved electrical properties, achieving a low sheet resistance of 0.11 Ω sq–1 and a conductivity enhanced by approximately three orders of magnitude relative to pristine carbon electrodes. Morphological analysis reveals that carbon black improves particle packing and film compactness, while ITO colloids promote the formation of additional conductive pathways within the carbon network. When integrated into ambient-processed PSCs, the optimized electrodes deliver improved charge collection and reduced resistive losses, yielding a champion power conversion efficiency of 19.64%. In addition, the optimized CCB-ITO/Ag electrode, which forms a denser carbon network and more conformal contact with the Ag leaf current collector, maintained approximately 90% of its initial efficiency, compared with ∼85% for C-ITO/Ag, after 2000 h (∼83 days) of aging under continuous dark storage at 25 °C and 2% RH. Improved performance retention demonstrates the beneficial effect of the hybrid carbon architecture on electrode stability while preserving efficient charge transport. This hybrid carbon-ITO/Ag strategy provides a practical, vacuum-free route toward conductivity-enhanced carbon electrodes for high-performance PSCs and offers a promising platform for potentially scalable device fabrication.

title: Phage Cocktail-Mediated Ultrasensitive Real-Time Electrochemical Whole-Cell Detection of Klebsiella pneumoniae on a SPCE
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Rapid and selective detection of pathogenic bacteria is essential for timely clinical diagnosis and environmental surveillance. In this work, we report a bacteriophage-assisted electrochemical sensing platform for the selective detection of Klebsiella pneumoniae using an Er2O3/Co3O4/Au/polyethylenimine (PEI)-modified screen-printed carbon electrode (SPCE). The hierarchical nanocomposite was engineered to provide high surface area, enhanced charge transfer kinetics, and abundant functional sites for efficient phage immobilization. PEI served as a cationic linker to facilitate electrostatic attachment of lytic bacteriophages while maintaining their biological activity and host specificity. Upon target recognition, phage–bacteria binding at the electrode interface produced pronounced impedance changes due to interfacial blocking and altered electron transfer dynamics. The developed biosensor exhibited high selectivity for Klebsiella pneumoniae over nontarget bacteria and could distinguish live from dead bacteria. The sensor showed a wide linear detection range of 10–107 CFU/mL with a low detection limit of 7.36 CFU/mL and good repeatability with an RSD of ∼1.17%. The real-world applicability of the sensor was tested using aquarium water samples and demonstrated good performance, with recovery percentages ranging from ∼91.71 to 96.26%. This work establishes a robust nano–bio hybrid interface strategy that integrates rare-earth/transition metal oxide electrocatalysts with phage biorecognition on disposable SPCE platforms. The developed system shows strong potential for point-of-care pathogen monitoring in clinical, environmental, and food safety applications.

title: Catalysts or constraints? The dual role of natural resources and greenfield investment amid geopolitical risk
abstract: Rapid urbanisation, industrialisation, population growth, and fast economic expansion have made emerging economies significant contributors to greenhouse gas emissions. This study assesses the impact of key economic and environmental factors on economic development, emphasising the role of green growth as an effective means to achieve sustainable development. Specifically, it examines the effect of greenfield investment (GFI), geopolitical risk (GPR), natural resources (TNR), and renewable energy consumption (GET) on green growth (GG) across 17 emerging economies from 2003 to 2022. Utilising advanced panel estimation techniques, the study concludes that GFI and GET contribute positively to green growth, whereas GPR adversely affects green growth. Similarly, the greater dependence on natural resources significantly hampers green growth, thereby confirming the presence of the ‘resource curse’ hypothesis in our analysis. Moreover, the interaction between GPR and TNR significantly dampens green growth, while the interaction between GPR and GFI further exacerbates this adverse effect. Based on these results, the study suggests that policymakers should promote greenfield investment in sustainable sectors, strengthen natural resource management through robust regulations, and mitigate geopolitical risk by diversifying international partnerships to support long-term sustainable development goals.

title: Energy shocks, firm resilience, and policy responses: Evidence from the 2022 crisis*
Geopolitical risk and energy poverty in African net energy importers: Localized effects, structural vulnerability, and conditional resilience
Geopolitical energy shocks and consumer protection under fiscal constraints
abstract: How can energy-importing governments protect fuel-dependent households during geopolitical crises without suppressing conservation incentives or making unaffordable fiscal promises? We develop conditional insurance based on pre-crisis reference fuel consumption, with transfers independent of current purchases. Under stated assumptions, fixed payments preserve the marginal pump-price signal; a strictly concave allocation problem determines how to distribute scarce assistance. A dated liquidity rule prioritizes binding infrastructure guarantees and committed low-carbon investment before discretionary relief, and identifies the conditions under which protection must be rationed or financing fails. Guarantees require verified project-specific external losses and contractual caps. French monthly fuel-price analyses for 2020–2026, a longer exploratory global VAR, and a European synthetic-control comparison of France’s September 2022 intervention illustrate implementation. The latter captures a combined public–private discount and has low-powered donor placebos; it does not isolate the causal effect of the state rebate. Externally released geopolitical energy and macro surprises provide additional exploratory transmission diagnostics; their underlying structural model is not re-estimated and French event samples remain sparse. The framework offers conditional, auditable policy rules rather than a demonstrated universal welfare ranking or unconditional sovereign solvency.

title: Who leads the global gas market? Geopolitics and price transmission between the U.S. and Europe

Asymmetric Janus Patch Integrating Antifouling and Wet-Adhesive Functions for Infected Wound Repair
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The wet, dynamic, and bacteria-contaminated microenvironment of infected wounds creates conflicting demands for stable wound-facing adhesion and outward antifouling protection. To address these demands, we developed an asymmetric Janus hydrogel-film patch (JP-TA/Fe) with a coordination-stabilized bilayer interface. The patch consisted of a dense nonadhesive layer containing silk fibroin/tannic acid (SF/TA) and an adhesive hydrogel layer containing polyacrylic acid/recombinant collagen/tannic acid (PAA/rhCol/TA). TA-Fe3+ chelation was introduced at the bilayer interface through a facile process to strengthen interlayer bonding and maintain bilayer structural integrity during hydration and mechanical deformation. The outward-facing SF/TA layer provided mechanical support and an antifouling barrier, whereas the wound-facing hydrogel layer exhibited favorable fluid-uptake capacity and maintained stable tissue adhesion. Benefiting from this asymmetric design, the patch exhibited robust wet-tissue adhesion, pH-responsive TA release, asymmetric antifouling and adhesive properties, antibacterial activity, biofilm-disrupting performance, and efficient reactive oxygen species (ROS)-scavenging capacity. In a rat full-thickness skin incision model and a Staphylococcus aureus-infected full-thickness skin defect model, JP-TA/Fe promoted stable wound closure, reduced bacterial burden, and accelerated collagen remodeling and epidermal regeneration. This study presents a structurally stable Janus wound patch with spatially differentiated functions, providing a multifunctional material platform for infected wound repair.

title: From atomic structure to catalytic function: Morphology engineering of MXene for Electrocatalytic energy conversion
Energy cascade utilization in SOFC-GT hybrids: the approach to ultra-high efficiency and multi-generation
Angular solar absorption and thermal energy storage seasonally modulate radiative cooling
abstract: Passive daytime radiative cooling materials (RCs) maintain low surface temperatures under sunlight and can reduce building cooling loads and urban overheating. However, RCs with static optical properties overcool in cold seasons, and adaptive RCs proposed to date rely on temperature/humidity to switch their optical/radiative properties. Further, they address either daytime or nighttime response and are subject to ageing and to false switching on mild sunlit winter days. Here, we propose a system to seasonally modulate RCs with angular solar absorption, achieved with L-shaped fins, and with thermal energy storage (TES), implemented with phase change materials (PCMs) and concrete mass. The L-shaped fins have solar-absorptive, equator-facing walls shaded by horizontal eaves, enabling high direct solar absorption only at the low solar elevations of winter, with RC film on all other surfaces. Coupled with TES, the system is an angular-dependent thermal-mass-enhanced radiative cooler (ATMRC). In field campaigns in Western Sydney, the finned RC samples reached winter daytime surface temperatures 6–9 °C above the static RC and up to 11 °C above the unfinned RC + TES, resolving the daytime overcooling that TES alone introduces. The ATMRC with the 8 °C PCM reduced winter dew and frost durations by 56% and 73%, respectively, relative to the static RC. The summer daytime penalty against the static RC was 2 °C. Ray-tracing yields seasonal absorbed fractions of 37% in winter and 21% in summer in Sydney. Effective adaptive RCs therefore require both TES against night overcooling and angular-dependent solar absorption for daytime modulation.

title: Large language model-guided multi-agent reinforcement learning for low-carbon data center scheduling considering distribution-network constraint

Tuning Exciton Dynamics in Asymmetric Molecular Acceptors by End-Group Modulation Enables Efficient All-Small Molecule Organic Solar Cells
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Asymmetric small-molecule acceptors have been recognized as a pivotal component in the development of organic solar cells (OSCs). Here, we report the design and synthesis of two cost-effective asymmetric molecular acceptors, SM-11 and SM-12, featuring a simple coumarin–thiophene scaffold linked to different electron-acceptor end groups, such as dicyanoindanone and 3-ethylrhodanine units, respectively. This strategic variation precisely controls the absorption properties, molecular dipole moments, energy levels, and binding energies, thus effectively mitigating intramolecular charge transfer effects beneficial for OSCs. In binary OSCs with CA-CO as the donor, the achieved power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) were 11.73% (SM-11) and 6.78% (SM-12), respectively. The broader absorption profile, higher exciton generation/dissociation efficiency, along with lower binding energy of SM-11 account for the performance enhancement. Furthermore, integrating SM-11 into a ternary blend with CA-CO:Y7 further enhanced the PCE to 15.58%, outpacing the binary reference CA-CO:Y7 device (12.17%). The enhanced PCEs stem from the alteration of end-group functionalization in the small molecules, which accelerates exciton dissociation and charge transfer in the ternary system, promoting favorable blend morphology and efficient guest-to-host energy transfer.

title: High-Throughput Fabrication of Large-Area Optical Glass Microlens Arrays by Roll-to-Plate Hot Embossing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Microlens arrays (MLAs) play an essential role in advanced optical systems, especially in applications such as three-dimensional imaging and augmented reality. However, the mass production of large-area MLAs on optical glass substrates remains challenging due to limitations in replication area and manufacturing efficiency inherent in conventional plate-to-plate (P2P) hot embossing. To enable the fabrication of large-area optical glass MLAs with high efficiency and consistency, this study proposes a novel roll-to-plate (R2P) hot embossing technology designed to achieve high-throughput production while addressing critical challenges in microstructure replication, including embossing-induced surface defects, unsatisfactory forming accuracy, and excessive manufacturing costs for large-area optical microstructures. A combined computational and experimental approach was employed to systematically investigate the glass filling behavior during the R2P embossing process. The parametric effects on MLA filling uniformity were quantitatively evaluated through designed factorial experiments. Optimal processing parameters were subsequently identified, enabling the successful fabrication of glass MLAs with high precision and exceptional surface consistency. This study thus demonstrates R2P hot embossing as a promising and economically attractive solution for the fabrication of advanced glass-based optical systems.

title: Intranasal Mitochondria-Targeted Rosmarinic Acid Selenium Nanoparticles Restore Mitochondrial Function and Attenuate Dopaminergic Neurodegeneration in Parkinson’s Disease
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuronal loss, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and α-synuclein pathology, highlighting the need for mitochondria-targeted neuroprotective strategies. Here, we developed a mitochondria-targeted intranasal nanotherapeutic system comprising rosmarinic acid (RA)-loaded selenium nanoparticles (RASNPs) surface-functionalized with triphenylphosphonium (TPP)-conjugated chitosan (TCS-RASNPs) to enhance nose-to-brain delivery and improve mitochondrial function. TCS-RASNPs exhibited a spherical morphology, a uniform particle size distribution (140.13 ± 0.40 nm), a narrow polydispersity, and a positive surface charge (33.7 ± 0.75 mV), indicating good colloidal stability. Spectroscopic characterization confirmed successful RA loading and surface functionalization. Moreover, TCS-RASNPs enhanced antioxidant activity and sustained drug release compared with free RA and unmodified RASNPs. In neuronal cells, TCS-RASNPs significantly enhanced neuronal survival, reduced apoptosis, attenuated intracellular and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, and improved mitochondrial membrane potential under 1-methyl-4-phenylpyridinium (MPP+)-induced neurotoxicity. Confocal microscopy further confirmed efficient mitochondrial localization of TCS-RASNPs. Pharmacokinetic and biodistribution studies demonstrated prolonged retention of RA and significantly higher brain RA levels following intranasal administration. In 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP)-induced Parkinsonian mice, TCS-RASNPs increased tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) expression, reduced α-synuclein (SNCA) expression, and normalized oxidative stress biomarkers in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) and striatum (STR) regions. Together, these findings demonstrate that TCS-RASNPs facilitate mitochondrial targeting and nose-to-brain delivery, thereby representing a promising nanotherapeutic approach for the management of PD.

title: Synthesis of ammonia and its application in the sustainable steel process: A review
Synergistic O2 Activation and H2O Dissociation Triggered by Spatially Proximal Frustrated Lewis Pairs on Hydroxylated Indium Oxide for Boosted Photocatalytic H2O2 Generation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Efficient activation of O2 and H2O at active sites is the core prerequisite for high-performance photocatalytic H2O2 generation, yet current photocatalytic systems are severely restricted by spatially separated sites-induced blocked proton transfer/intermediate coupling and competitive substrate activation among different active sites. Herein, frustrated Lewis pairs (FLPs) are rationally engineered on the hydroxylated indium oxide (In2O3–x(OH)y) surface, where spatially proximal Lewis acid (LA) and Lewis base (LB) sites are integrated to realize synergistic photocatalysis. The electron-deficient LA sites efficiently adsorb and activate O2 through a Pauling-type adsorption configuration. The proximal LA/LB sites cooperatively facilitate H2O adsorption and O–H bond cleavage. Following H2O dissociation, the resulting surface In–OH species can participate in a water-assisted proton exchange process, providing a plausible pathway for proton transfer to oxygen-derived intermediates. Through the spatially coordinated activation of O2 and H2O, the proximal LA/LB sites facilitate interfacial proton transfer and promote the coupling of O2 reduction intermediates with protonic species, thereby enhancing H2O2 formation. Benefiting from the aforementioned dual-site synergistic effect, the optimized In2O3–x(OH)y catalyst exhibits a photocatalytic H2O2 production rate in pure water that is nearly three-fold higher than those of control samples with sole LA or LB active sites. This work successfully extends the spatial synergistic mechanism of FLPs toward efficient photocatalytic H2O2 synthesis, which provides a feasible strategy and insights for the rational design of high-performance bifunctional photocatalysts.

title: How the US mid-term elections could shake up science
abstract: A Democratic victory in Congress could halt the Trump administration’s controversial grant-review plan and curb some of its funding actions.

title: Spin Polarized Chiral Co 3 O 4 Boosts High‐Pressure CO 2 Electroreduction to Ethanol With 90% Selectivity
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction (CO 2 RR) to value‐added multicarbon products using non‐copper‐based catalysts remains a major challenge, especially for selective ethanol production. Herein, we report that chiral Co 3 O 4 featuring strong electron spin polarization achieves a maximum ethanol Faradaic efficiency of 90% at ‐0.9 V versus NHE in KHCO 3 electrolytes under a 30 bar CO 2 pressure, substantially outperforming both racemic Co 3 O 4 and previously reported non‐copper‐based catalysts. The enhanced spin polarization in chiral Co 3 O 4 facilitates electron transfer and promotes the activation of the adsorbed CO 2 , while also lowering the free energy change for C–C coupling to form *COCHO intermediate, thereby promoting ethanol production. Our work establishes spin polarization as a key determinant for efficient C–C coupling on non‐copper‐based catalysts and provides mechanistic principles for the rational design of CO 2 RR electrocatalyst.

title: LytU is a bridge-link isopeptidase that contributes to vancomycin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Emergence of antimicrobial resistance is a pressing global issue. Although myriads of mechanisms for survival against antimicrobial pressure have surfaced, one key strategy is the structural modification of peptidoglycan, the main defense line in Gram-positive bacteria e.g., notorious pathogen Staphylococcus aureus. Here we show that the recently identified peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH) LytU is an unusual catalyst in the lysostaphin (M23B) family of zinc-endopeptidases that hydrolyze the glycyl-glycine peptide bond in S. aureus. Unlike any other PGH recognized thus far, LytU hydrolyzes the isopeptide bond between the lysine ε amino group and pentaglycine, thus functioning as a bridge-link hydrolase. We discovered that LytM and LytU are functionally non-redundant, and they contribute to the cell wall remodeling at different stages of PG maturation. Additionally, we demonstrate that LytU particularly targets the PG precursor, pGly-Lipid II, and its overexpression leads to growth inhibition and a less densely cross-linked cell wall, which increases susceptibility to lysostaphin. Interestingly, LytU expression enhances resistance to the glycopeptide vancomycin, the drug of last resort against S. aureus.

title: Tree shrew more closely recapitulates primate spermatogenesis than the mouse in cross-species single-cell transcriptomic analyses
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The rapid evolution of spermatogenesis limits the utility of mouse models for studying human spermatogenesis because some genes are absent or divergent in mice. Primate models face practical and ethical constraints, whereas tree shrews are closely related to primates and suitable for laboratory research. Here we integrate histology and single-nucleus RNA sequencing data from human, rhesus macaque, mouse and tree shrew testes to assess the tree shrew as a model of human spermatogenesis. We show that transcriptional landscapes in tree shrew spermatogenic cells, particularly late-stage spermatids, more closely resemble those of primates than mice. Conservation and enrichment analyses identify two core gene modules shared among humans, macaques and tree shrews but distinct in mice. Gene expression trajectories also align between tree shrews and primates, including for genes without murine orthologs. Immunostaining and RNA-FISH support representative expression patterns. These findings define contexts in which tree shrews can complement existing models of human spermatogenesis and male infertility.

title: Exaiptasia diaphana core microbiome members are lost under climate change conditions despite host thermal tolerance
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Acute and chronic exposure to elevated temperatures associated with Global Climate Change (GCC) threatens the structure and function of host-associated microbiomes, yet predicting microbial responses to heat stress remains challenging. We exposed two lines of the sea anemone, Exaiptasia diaphana, to acute and chronic thermal stress to quantify the impacts on cnidarian physiology and microbiome composition. Acute exposure caused rapid algal bleaching that was paired with pronounced shifts in bacteriome structure in both lines within 14 days of thermal exposure. Chronic exposure significantly affected the population structure, photo-physiology and bacteriome composition in only one host line, suggesting acclimation capacity depends on host-algal genetic backgrounds. Using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing of 493 individuals sampled across 180 days, we found that sampling date explained nine-fold more variation in the microbiome composition than temperature exposure. Despite this temporal variation, we identified 16 indicator taxa that consistently changed in relative abundance under thermal stress. These taxa became central hubs in microbial association networks with increasing levels of thermal stress, suggesting they played key roles in bacteriome reorganization. As many of these taxa were present in other cnidarians, including reef-building corals, they may represent targets for conservation strategies that aim to enhance resilience on reefs.

title: Local albumin excess exacerbates Candida albicans-induced inflammasome activation linked with hyperinflammation during vulvovaginal candidiasis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) is a mucosal yeast infection, mostly caused by Candida albicans, where symptoms are driven by inflammation. The onset of VVC is instigated by C. albicans pathogenicity, but the underlying causes of disease-driving hyperinflammation remain incompletely resolved. We found that vaginal albumin concentrations are higher in women with recurrent VVC and during experimental VVC in mice. These albumin levels correlated with inflammatory cytokines in vaginal lavages. While the abundance of this serum protein in the vagina can be a hallmark of inflammation-induced vascular permeability, we reveal molecular mechanisms by which albumin can also drive inflammation. Albumin increased NLRP3 inflammasome activation in human macrophages elicited by C. albicans. This was associated with increased resistance of C. albicans to macrophage-mediated clearance in the presence of albumin. Further, albumin increased the expression of fungal secreted aspartic protease 1, which we identified as the effector driving inflammasome activation and IL-1β responses in vitro and in an in vivo VVC model. Moreover, neutrophils also exhibited impaired clearance of C. albicans in the presence of albumin. Collectively, vaginal albumin may not only be a consequence of inflammation of the vaginal mucosa, but also can drive C. albicans-induced hyperinflammatory IL-1β responses that underlie immunopathology in VVC.

title: Darutigenol ameliorates experimental colitis via promoting Akkermansia muciniphila-mediated proline synthesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The gut microbiota dysbiosis is a key factor leading to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Darutigenol (DL) is a natural compound with limited oral bioavailability but potent anti-inflammatory activity. However, its ameliorative efficacy in colitis and precise mechanism remain unexplored. This study demonstrated through multi-omics analysis and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) experiments that the alleviation of colitis in male mice by DL is dependent on the gut microbiota. Mechanistically, DL specifically enriches the abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila (A. muciniphila), which alleviates colitis by promoting the synthesis of proline. Interestingly, DL was found to promote the growth of A. muciniphila in the gut by targeting indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1). Additionally, exogenous proline supplementation alleviated murine colitis by downregulating the IL-17 signaling pathway and its downstream cascades. Our findings reveal that DL ameliorates colitis by inhibiting IDO1 expression to drive A. muciniphila expansion and proline synthesis, and highlights the potential of DL for the treatment of IBD.

title: Increasing prevalence and expanding diversity of tet(X4)-carrying Salmonella in China
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The plasmid-mediated tigecycline resistance gene tet(X4) threatens the efficacy of tigecycline. While prevalent in Escherichia coli across diverse ecological niches, its evolutionary trajectory in Salmonella remains underappreciated. Here, we conducted nationwide genomic surveillance of 42403 clinical nontyphoidal Salmonella isolates collected from diarrheal patients in China between 2014 and 2025, of which 102 were tet(X4)-positive. Although the overall prevalence remained low, detection showed a statistically significant upward trend over 2019-2025. Importantly, the newly accrued 2025 data were broadly consistent with short-term forecasts generated by the beta regression model, providing partial support for short-term trend consistency. Genomic analyses showed that tet(X4) remained concentrated in ST34 but was also detected in additional sequence types, including ST469, ST8971, ST11 and one isolate with an unassigned ST, across multiple provinces, indicating broader geographic representation and genetic diversification. Plasmid analyses likewise revealed broader replicon diversity, with the dominant IncHI1A/IncHI1B/IncFIA background accompanied by less frequent IncHI2/IncHI2A, IncI1(Alpha) and IncFIA/IncFIB/IncFIC. Phylogenetic analyses further revealed shared clustering of the dominant plasmid background across host species and bacterial genera, consistent with cross-host and cross-genus circulation.

title: Viral tRNA-like structure hijacks host ribosomes for poly(A)-independent translation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Positive-sense RNA viruses often use 3′ tRNA-like structures (TLSs) instead of poly(A) tails to capture the host translation machinery. While TLSs resemble canonical tRNAs and engage host factors, their ability to directly recruit ribosomes has remained unresolved. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy snapshots of the histidine-accepting TLS (TLSHis) from tobacco mosaic virus bound to the tobacco 60S subunit, the 80S ribosome, and the 80S-tRNAiMet initiation complex. Across these states, TLSHis is consistently anchored to the L1 stalk of 60S, even under cycloheximide treatment, yet remains dynamic on the 40S subunit. Structural analysis shows that TLSHis transitions from the E-site to an adjacent Z-site to accommodate initiator tRNA. Functional assays show that TLSHis preferentially associates with ribosomal subunits over polysomes and can substitute for a poly(A) tail to promote robust cap-dependent translation. These results provide structural and mechanistic evidence that the viral tRNA mimic exploits the tRNA-exit channel to stabilize initiation-competent ribosomes and drive poly(A)-independent translation.

title: Stabilization of insulin receptor mRNA by Star-PAP in metabolic homeostasis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Conserved polyadenylation b3y poly(A) polymerases (PAPs) is essential for mRNA stability, yet its metabolic functions remain unclear. Here we identify a rare variant p.D469N (Asp469Asn) in Star-PAP present in lean individuals but absent in obese cases. Adipose-specific Star-PAP knockout mice develop progressive adipose tissue loss, hepatic steatosis, and severe insulin resistance, phenocopying human lipodystrophy. Mechanistically, Star-PAP directly binds the insulin receptor (InsR) mRNA 3’–UTR to stabilize its transcript. Both deletion of Star-PAP and p.D469N variant decrease InsR mRNA maturation. Star-PAP deficiency impairs insulin receptor signaling and adipocyte lipid storage, while restoring InsR in adipocytes partially ameliorates the lipodystrophic phenotypes. Notably, Star-PAP deficiency disrupts acetyl-CoA homeostasis secondary to insulin signaling defects, accompanied by reduced histone acetylation at fatty acid synthesis genes. Pyruvate supplementation effectively restores acetyl-CoA levels and histone acetylation, thereby rescuing the gene expression and lipogenesis. Together, our results identify Star-PAP-mediated RNA polyadenylation as a mechanism governing adipose mass, positioning Star-PAP as a key regulator of insulin receptor signaling and lipodystrophy.
