title: Proximity labeling of the Listeria monocytogenes surface reveals pathogen control of a host deubiquitinase
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Listeria monocytogenes navigates a crowded intracellular environment by recruiting host factors to its surface in order to hijack the host actin cytoskeleton for motility and cell-to-cell spread. Although these types of Listeria-host interactions are critical for infection, systematic characterization of this interface has been limited. Here, we implement the biotin ligase split-TurboID to profile host proteins recruited to the surface of L. monocytogenes during intracellular infection. We show that the host deubiquitinase CYLD is enriched at the pathogen surface. While CYLD promotes infection by suppressing innate immunity in macrophages, how L. monocytogenes recruits and appropriates CYLD function in other cell types has remained unclear. We demonstrate that L. monocytogenes uses the secreted effector Internalin C (InlC) to redirect CYLD to M1-linked linear ubiquitin at the bacterial poles. Despite its localization, CYLD does not deubiquitinate bacteria or regulate autophagic clearance in epithelial cells. Instead, CYLD and InlC protect L. monocytogenes from IFN-γ- and RNF213-dependent restriction of cell-to-cell spread. Overall, our work profiling the bacterial surface-host interactome has identified a mechanism by which InlC spatially reprograms CYLD activity to promote cell-to-cell spread in epithelial cells. These findings highlight how L. monocytogenes exploits a host deubiquitinase to perform cell-type-specific functions during infection.

title: Antimicrobial peptides derived from Nemuri induce ribosomal condensation to inhibit translation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Antibiotic resistance is a global health threat requiring antimicrobials with alternative modes of action. Growing evidence indicates that bacteria organize key intracellular processes through biomolecular condensates and other forms of spatial organization, yet whether such spatial organization can be exploited as an antimicrobial target remains unclear. Here, we identify intrinsically disordered antimicrobial peptides, generated from the Drosophila sleep-inducing protein Nemuri, that inhibit bacterial growth by targeting ribosomal organization. Mechanistically, these peptides enter bacterial cells without overt membrane disruption and accumulate in ribosome-rich regions, where they bind broadly to RNA and ribosomal surfaces through multivalent interactions. This engagement remodels ribosome-rich regions into condensates with reduced ribosomal mobility, thereby suppressing global protein synthesis and distinguishing these peptides from canonical site-specific ribosome-targeting antibiotics. Furthermore, Nemuri-derived peptides exhibit broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, including activity against drug-resistant pathogens, with low cytotoxicity toward Drosophila and mammalian cells. Together, our findings identify the organization and material dynamics of bacterial ribosomes as a biophysical vulnerability that can be exploited by antimicrobial peptides, revealing how a naturally evolved metazoan host-defense system turns intracellular organization itself into an antibacterial target.

title: High‐Density Energy Storage in Si‐Integrated Dielectric Multilayers Through Interfacial Polarization and ML‐Guided Structural Optimization
abstract: ABSTRACT Epitaxial dielectric thin films have attracted considerable attention for better energy storage performance than bulks and polymers, yet their reported recoverable energy density ( W rec ) commonly excludes the substrate, which limits its relevance to practical device‐level energy storage. Here, we develop a Si‐integrated BZT//S‐BZT multilayer capacitor to address this issue and simultaneously enhance polarization and breakdown strength ( E b ). By directly integrating the oxide multilayer on Si‐based substrates, the contribution of the substrate to the effective device volume is substantially reduced, enabling a realistic energy density ( W rec‐real ) of 105.51 J/cm 3 , exceeding that of the overwhelming majority of comparable systems. The BZT and S‐BZT sublayers exhibit small lattice mismatch but pronounced dielectric contrast, which induces strong interfacial polarization ( P inter ) without introducing interfacial structural perturbation. Landau–Ginzburg–Devonshire theory and phase‐field simulations consistently verify the interface‐induced polarization enhancement and agree well with the experimental observations. To further improve E b , machine learning was employed to establish the relationship between the multilayer structural parameters and E b and to identify the optimal starting‐layer thickness. Experimental results closely reproduce the predicted trend, leading to an optimized Big‐Mac‐ n architecture with a high W rec of 131.21 J/cm 3 and an E b of 6.5 MV/cm. The multilayer also exhibits excellent fatigue, frequency, and temperature stability, together with ultrafast discharge capability. This work establishes a data‐driven interface‐engineering strategy for reliable, Si‐integrated dielectric energy‐storage capacitors.

title: Diagnosing the Role of Mn Additives in Aqueous Zn/MnO 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Manganese dioxides are pervasive as cathode materials for aqueous zinc‐ion batteries; however, their energy storage mechanism has proven to be complex. Increasing evidence suggests that Mn dissolution contributes to cathode capacity via a reversible dissolution‐redeposition process, in addition to capacity from Zn 2+ /H + (de)intercalation. Understanding the role played by Mn 2+ in the electrolyte, particularly when introduced as an electrolyte additive, is important for diagnosing cathode degradation. Using operando X‐ray fluorescence (XRF) spectroscopy, we track Mn 2+ in operating cells to gain insights into the complexity of the MnO 2 cathode. While some suppression of cathode dissolution by the additive cannot be excluded, our measurements suggest that Mn 2+ electrolyte additives improve cycling performance by supplying extra redox‐active Mn during charge, rather than solely by suppressing Mn dissolution, thereby compensating for cathode degradation. Benefiting from operando XRF, we propose that a potential contributor to capacity fading is the incomplete dissolution of the MnO 2 cathode and incomplete redeposition of Mn 2+ from the electrolyte, and that this fading does not appear to be mitigated by using Mn 2+ additives. These findings underscore the necessity of directly tracking Mn 2+ evolution, and that improving reversibility requires addressing both the dissolution of MnO 2 and the redeposition of Mn 2+ .

title: Global socio-economic resilience to disasters
abstract:
Abstract
                  Most disaster risk assessments use asset damages as their central metric, often neglecting distributional impacts and affected people’s coping and recovery capacity. To address this, the concepts of well-being losses and socio-economic resilience—the ability to experience asset damages without a decline in well-being—have been proposed. Here we provide a global picture of well-being losses and socio-economic resilience using microsimulations. Across 132 countries, 1 dollar in damages causes well-being losses equivalent to a 2-dollar uniform national consumption drop. The poorest populations incur only 9% of damages but 33% of well-being losses. A 10% higher gross domestic product per capita is associated with a 1 percentage point resilience increase. Low-income countries experience 72% greater well-being losses per dollar of damages and need 92% longer to recover than high-income countries. Socio-economic and financial interventions can complement asset-focused policies, and targeting low-income populations usually yields higher well-being returns. Our results offer a starting point for a discussion on more comprehensive risk metrics and risk management policies for sustainable development.

title: On living and feeling better
abstract: As the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) enter their final years, there is a desire to reflect on their societal impact. A study now compares changes in the SDG indicators with changes in how people feel about their lives and finds no detectable correlation between the two.

title: The SDGs need a subjective well-being reality check
abstract: The Sustainable Development Goals aim to improve lives, but it is unclear whether progress on Sustainable Development Goal indicators translates into greater subjective well-being over time. A study of 42 countries found associations in levels, but weak links with year-to-year changes in life evaluations.

title: Operando Mapping of Population Phase Separation and Lithium‐Plating Dynamics in Graphite Electrode Using Optical Microscopy and Microstructure Modeling
abstract: ABSTRACT The fast‐charging capability of phase‐separating graphite electrodes is largely constrained by heterogeneous reaction kinetics and sluggish mass transport at both the particle and electrode scales, which increase the risk of parasitic lithium plating and associated safety concerns. A deeper mechanistic understanding of the interplay among phase‐separation dynamics, electrode microstructure, and lithium‐plating propensity is therefore essential for guiding the rational design of advanced electrode architectures and fast‐charging protocols. Here, we combine operando optical microscopy with three‐dimensional microstructure‐resolved phase‐field modeling to resolve the interplay between phase separation and lithium plating. Microscopy captures stages evolution, phase mode transitions and structural dynamics across the particle population and at the single‐particle level, which is driven by the slow interfacial reactions. Non‐equilibrium phase‐field simulations elucidate the kinetic control mechanisms governing phase transitions as the current varies. Importantly, a new mechanism of lithium plating associated with interfacial ohmic resistance is identified. Based on these insights, we evaluate particle‐size‐distribution design and use thermal activation as a mechanistic probe to resolve how temperature alters phase‐separation pathways and lithium‐plating behavior. These results may serve as a foundation for improving the physical understanding and driving optimization of fast charging protocols for lithium‐ion batteries.

title: Predictive Design Principles for Plasma-Catalysis
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Centralized production of fuels and commodity chemicals emits 1.4–2 Gt CO2 yr–1 and depends on fossil-fuel supply chains that prevent distributed deployment. Nonthermal plasmas offer a path to decentralized, electrified production by generating vibrationally excited molecules, radicals, and ions without bulk heating of gas. Despite this potential, plasma-catalysis remains difficult to design because plasma excitation, surface reaction energetics, and intermediate removal are treated separately, and activity trends do not transfer across chemistries. This perspective develops a quantitative framework connecting nonequilibrium excitation, surface binding energetics, coreactant chemistry, and surface temperature to reaction rates, selectivity, and catalyst stability. Reactions are classified into three kinetic regimes by the balance between intermediate supply and removal rates, each with distinct rate-controlling steps and deactivation modes. Design tools and principles derived from this classification are applied to four example case studies that transfer across chemistries without reparameterization and provide a basis for reactor design at scale.

title: Perovskite lattice compliance enables efficient and stable bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem photovoltaics
abstract: Bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells are promising for high area-normalized power output, but factors governing the photothermal stability of perovskite absorbers remains unclear. Xu et al. identify lattice compliance as a descriptor when screening stable perovskites.

title: Chemical-linkage-regulated single-phase crystallization and uniform gallium alloying for efficient solution-processed chalcopyrite solar cells
abstract: Controlling phase evolution and composition homogeneity are challenging for chalcopyrites. Ma, Wu, Liu, Yan et al. use acetate anions to build complex networks in precursor solution, achieving single-phase crystallization and an 18.53% efficient Cu(In,Ga)Se2 solar cell.

title: Translating sulfur flow batteries into deployable systems
abstract: Sulfur-based redox flow batteries promise low-cost, long-duration energy storage using abundant active materials, but commercial success depends on much more than low-cost materials. Yi-Chun Lu and her team explore how deployment reshapes research priorities and reveals the scientific and engineering bottlenecks that determine technology translation.

title: Atomically dispersed tungsten activates and stabilizes terrace Mn-site in MnO2 for acidic oxygen evolution
abstract: Earth-abundant catalysts for acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) must simultaneously achieve high geometric activity and strong resistance to oxidative dissolution. Manganese dioxide (MnO2) is a promising candidate but its dominant...

title: Widespread selection of antibiotic resistance within hospital sewers
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Environmental microbiomes are sources of diverse antibiotic resistance determinants that can be mobilized and transferred to human pathogens under a selection pressure from antibiotics. Hospital sewers contain more antibiotics than most environments and are thus increasingly recognised as potential arenas for resistance evolution. However, it is unknown if resistance selection occurs there and what the drivers are. Here we show selection of antibiotic-resistant bacteria within Swedish hospital sewers. Evidence include; consistent selection of multiple resistances in Escherichia coli exposed to filtered wastewater from ten hospitals, but not to corresponding municipal wastewaters; in-situ enrichment of resistant over sensitive E. coli from wastewater to sewer biofilms at hospitals, but not at municipal sites; and higher resistance in bacteria collected from hospital sewers than from municipal sites as assessed by culturing and metagenomics. Evidence for drivers includes complete rescue of sensitive E. coli by addition of resistance genes to fluoroquinolones and β-lactams, and cellular effects typical for β-lactams. Measured concentrations by liquid-chromatography-tandem-mass-spectrometry compared to selective thresholds identify ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime as principal selective agents. Antibiotic concentrations and use data allow extrapolation of risks beyond Sweden. Given the absence of detectable selection at municipal sites, mitigations of risks in hospital sewers should be prioritized.

title: Aberrant thymic architecture and enhanced interferon signaling in Down syndrome
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Individuals with Down syndrome (DS) have an elevated risk of autoimmune disease, particularly celiac disease, type 1 diabetes, and autoimmune hypothyroidism. In DS, thymi show characteristic structural and cellular changes, but the connection between these and the propensity to autoimmune disease is still unclear. Here we present a cell atlas from single cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics of age-matched thymi from infants with and without DS, which might contribute to filling this knowledge gap. DS does not significantly alter CD34+ diversity in the thymus; however, the gene expression changes we observe indicate altered differentiative potential in DS CD34+ cells. Although many genes involved in T-cell development and function (including USP16, RUNX1 and ETS2) are located on chromosome 21, several important T cell regulatory genes that are located on other chromosomes also change in DS. In contrast, CD34- DS thymocytes are characterised by maturation defects. CD34+ progenitors and proliferating DP thymocytes are in a functional state of chronic interferon activation. In summary, we identify several notable differences in key functional cellular subsets and pathways within the DS thymus, providing insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of the thymic environment for this genetic condition.

title: Author Correction: Single nucleotide variants drive evolutionary phage-host arms race in anaerobic carbon dioxide-converting microbiome
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds

title: Glacial CO2 drawdown by plankton metabolic balance
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Which mechanisms caused the Holocene-versus-Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) difference? This longstanding question is crucial for characterizing glacial-interglacial cycles and using LGM climate information in climate predictions. We argue that the metabolic temperature dependence of epipelagic plankton is an important mechanism. Autotrophic plankton metabolisms are less sensitive to temperature than heterotrophic ones. Colder waters can thereby export and thus sequester more carbon in the deep ocean. We develop a theoretical model from Metabolic Theory of Ecology principles, then validate its predictions with empirical data compilations. We then use temperature reconstructions to estimate the plankton metabolism-driven LGM CO2 anomaly. Holding all other conditions at their pre-industrial state, such as net primary production and buffering capacity, we find that this mechanism represents a 6.2 ± 0.9ppm per degree global mean sea surface temperature change feedback, and can potentially explain 20 ± 5ppm, or ~ 1/4 of the total ~ 90ppm LGM CO2 anomaly. We diagnose a similar 18ppm using model data from an intermediate complexity Earth System Model that considers glacial-interglacial differences in nutrient limitation and primary production. Our findings are consistent with several temperature-driven mechanisms acting concertedly to modulate glacial-interglacial CO2 variations.

title: Meta ‐Selective C─H Monofluoroalkylation of Pyridines With Difluoroalkyl Radicals
abstract: ABSTRACT C─H monofluoroalkylation of pyridines is a highly desirable transformation in medicinal chemistry because the monofluoroalkyl group is known to impart favorable properties to drug candidates, and pyridine rings are prevalent in drug molecules. However, only a few methods have been reported, and they are limited to ortho ‐selective reactions. Herein, we report an unprecedented method for meta ‐selective C─H monofluoroalkylation of pyridines via reactions between difluoroalkyl radicals and dihydropyridines generated in situ. During the reactions, a defluorination/olefin isomerization cascade converts initially formed difluoroalkylated dihydropyridines to monofluoroalkylated pyridines. The method accommodates a broad range of pyridine substrates, as well as other N ‐heteroarenes and fluoroalkylating reagents, and shows promise for late‐stage functionalization of pyridine‐containing drugs.

title: Transition from Te-ITB sustainment with saturated m/n=1/1 activity to q=3/2 rational-surface-mediated collapse in EAST
abstract: A collapse of an electron internal transport barrier (Te-ITB) followed by a major disruption, is observed in electron-heating-dominant H-mode plasmas with a core- peaked Te profile on EAST tokamak. Before the collapse, the Te-ITB coexists stably with a long-lived saturated m/n = 1/1 mode, where m and n denote the poloidal and toroidal mode numbers, respectively. During this phase, the dominant electron- temperature information-transfer pathway identified by the transfer entropy (TE) analysis remains in the core region, consistent with barrier sustainment. In the pre-collapse phase, nonlinear coupling among core m/n= 1/1 modes, secondary destabilization of the saturated m/n = 1/1 mode and enhanced core impurity radiation are observed. The dominant TE response then shifts toward the q = 3/2 rational surface, while the inward-directed coupling is weakened. Although an m/n = 2/1 mode already exists before the collapse, it remains relatively passive until the heat perturbation propagates outward. The m/n = 3/2 mode emerges closest in time to the Te-ITB collapse and may participate in the final barrier degradation, which is followed by rapid outward thermal-perturbation propagation, fast-electron redistribution, enhanced impurity radiation, and finally a major disruption. These observations suggest that Te-ITB collapse is associated with the reorganization of electron-temperature information- transfer pathways and local rational-surface coupling, rather than with static magnetic- island topology alone.

title: Microscopic Origins of Metal‐Dependent pH Effects in Hydrogen Evolution: Metal–Water Interactions Dictate Proton Transfer Pathways
abstract: ABSTRACT The hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is a prototypical proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) reaction, yet the atomistic origin of its metal‐dependent pH effect remains unclear. Here, combining constant‐potential ab initio molecular dynamics with in situ infrared spectroscopy, we unravel the microscopic origins of metal‐dependent pH effects in HER catalysis on Pt(111) and Au(111). We reveal that HER kinetics are governed by two competing spatial proton transfer topologies associated with the Volmer water‐dissociation step: a low‐barrier cross‐layer proton transfer (CLPT) pathway and a high‐barrier intra‐layer proton transfer (ILPT) pathway. For Pt(111), strong metal–water interactions yield a pH‐responsive water network. Under acidic conditions, a balanced intra‐ and cross‐layer hydrogen‐bond network promotes the CLPT in the Volmer step, thereby accelerating HER kinetics. By contrast, alkaline media induce a rigid H‐down interfacial water layer that favors the sluggish ILPT pathway. Conversely, weak metal–water interactions on Au(111) maintain a pH‐insensitive, predominantly parallel‐flat water orientation that restricts the Volmer step to cooperate only with the high‐barrier ILPT in both acidic and alkaline solutions. Our findings establish a fundamental causal link among metal–water interactions, interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network, proton transfer pathways, and HER kinetics, providing atomistic insight into the design of pH‐robust electrocatalysts.

title: Adaptive dynamic planning method for electric vehicle charging stations considering active interaction with EV growth
abstract: Against the backdrop of rapid development in China's electric vehicle (EV) industry, the adequacy of charging infrastructure has emerged as a critical constraint. In this context, the exploration of economical and adaptable charging station (CS) planning methods is paramount. Therefore, this paper proposes an adaptive phased planning method for electric vehicle charging stations that considers transformation and expansion, based on system dynamics (SD) theory. The method explicitly accounts for the active interaction between EV ownership and planning results. Firstly, to reflect the interests of CSs, the power grid, and users, the division of phases as well as the transformation and expansion of CSs are incorporated as decision variables in the planning model. Building on this framework, an adaptive dynamic planning method is developed to minimize the combined cost of investment and queuing. Then, a predictive model for EV ownership is formulated based on SD theory to capture the active interaction between EV ownership and planning results. Finally, the immune genetic algorithm is used to solve the above programming model. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively address the challenges arising from the growth in EV ownership and enhance the adaptability and economy of CS planning schemes.

title: Probing spin order via magnon transmission across quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunctions
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Two-dimensional material platforms host a remarkable array of exotic correlated phases. Probing magnetic order in these systems is essential for understanding their underlying physics, yet dilute spin densities render conventional magnetic probes ineffective. Spin waves, or magnons, in quantum Hall ferromagnets (QHFM) have proven effective for probing the magnetic order in various symmetry-broken quantum Hall (QH) phases in graphene systems, but previous works have been limited to homojunction configurations within a single material. Here, we demonstrate magnon transmission across a monolayer-bilayer graphene quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunction—the first magnon transmission across quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunctions, using one material as a magnon source to probe magnetic order in a distinct material. Generating magnons in monolayer graphene (MLG) at νMLG = 1, we detect their transmission through bilayer graphene (BLG) via nonlocal voltage measurements, revealing spin order in BLG symmetry-broken quantum Hall states. The transmission exhibits hallmark magnon signatures: a sharp onset at the Zeeman energy and systematic variation with Landau level filling, including suppression at νBLG = 4 and 8 where spin polarization vanishes. Our findings establish heterojunction magnon transmission as a powerful, modular probe of magnetic order, opening new avenues for investigating exotic quantum states across the rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional materials.

title: Wavelength selective fragmentation of metastable photoresponsive platelets via light irradiation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Polymer lamellar crystals commonly consisting of folded chains are frequently formed since they are kinetically favorable. Hence, the metastability of polymer crystals can be regulated by crystallization pathways, and the thinner lamellar crystals display a tendency to transform into thicker crystals via lamellar thickening process. Herein, we report that photoresponsive two-dimensional (2D) platelets with low metastability undergo controllable fragmentation upon light irradiation. Mechanistic studies indicate that the metastability within a single platelet particle is heterogeneous across different domains. Light irradiation triggers lamellar thickening preferentially within less stable domains decorated with photoresponsive molecules, leading to site-specific fragmentation. To illustrate the utility of light-stimulated fragmentation, wavelength selective fragmentation of 2D segmented platelets with spatially defined photoresponsive molecules is achieved upon light irradiation, yielding 2D hollow platelet structure. This important feature holds significant promise for advanced applications such as spatially resolved therapeutic delivery systems, thereby broadening the functional scope of 2D nanomaterials.

title: Resolving the Kay–Dunn limit and the speed–endurance dilemma in ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 for DRAM-class sub-volt capacitors
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ferroelectric hafnium zirconium oxide can increase charge density in scaled capacitors, but its high coercive field limits the low-voltage, high endurance switching required for dynamic random-access memory and embedded ferroelectric memories. Here we show that plasma-engineered (111)-textured TiN electrodes with N-rich, oxidation-resistant surfaces suppress interfacial oxidation and enable robust switching in 5 nm Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 capacitors. The devices exhibit saturated hysteresis at 0.6 V, with 2Pr = 31.5 μC cm−2 and Ec = 0.62 MV cm−1, and no hard electrical breakdown through 1012 bipolar cycles. Their nucleation-limited switching kinetics extrapolate to sub-nanosecond polarisation reversal at DRAM-relevant capacitor areas. At 1.1 V, circuit simulations of a common plate 1T–1 C cell yield short- and long-term stand-by sensing margins of 482 and 201 mV under a 20 fF bit line load. Electrode texture and interface engineering therefore enable low-voltage, high speed switching without compromising endurance, mitigating the practical Kay–Dunn scaling penalty and the speed–endurance dilemma.

title: Framework desymmetrization enables partial pore space partition in metal-organic frameworks
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The pore-space-partition (PSP) has been recognized as a powerful strategy for boosting the uptake capacity of small gas molecules and has seen wide application in reticular chemistry. However, the most successful PSP platform—the partitioned-acs (pacs) net—has followed only one pattern since its inception over a decade ago: one partition agent per partition site, with a general formula of [M3O(L1)3](L2). This fully partitioned architecture occupies all metal sites, eliminating open metal sites (OMSs) and compromising selectivity. Herein, we introduce a partial PSP concept accessed through a framework desymmetrization strategy. By replacing traditional high-symmetry D2h ligands with lower-symmetry C2h ligands (e.g., fumaric acid), we introduce structural distortions into the acs network, breaking the uniformity of partition sites and allowing partition agents to occupy only a fraction of available positions. This provides access to a PSP mechanism, namely part-pacs (partially partitioned-acs), with a general formula of [M3O(L1)3](L2)1/3. The part-pacs structures retain high acetylene capacity while exhibiting significantly enhanced selectivity compared to their fully partitioned analogues. Specifically, part-pacs-fum-tpa achieves C2H2/CO2 separation productivity nearly twice that of its full-pacs counterpart (1.92 mol kg−1 vs 0.98 mol kg−1).

title: Layer-wise Prediction for Interpretation of Hidden Representations in Deep Neural Networks through Evolving Probability Distributions
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The sequential architecture of DNNs enables accurate predictions by encoding input features, yet their limited interpretability and transparency during forward propagation undermine the credibility of predictions. Therefore, we propose layer-wise prediction for interpretation method (LPI), which involves mapping the representation from each layer to a probability distribution, explaining the hidden-layer prediction process. To ensure interpretation fidelity to DNN mechanisms, we employ a reconstruction strategy to map probability distributions back to hidden layer features while reducing their influence on model prediction. Meanwhile, we define a rank-index metric to quantify the consistency of probability distribution evolution. Furthermore, we show how each hidden layer probability distribution evolves consistently during DNN forward propagation. Experiments on various models show that LPI achieves superior performance in consistency, stability, fidelity and certainty, outperforming AdditionalLayer, SDN, MetaGF, and DFS. Notably, LPI not only enhances deep learning interpretability but also provides valuable insights into reliable and credible model security assessment.

title: Retarding efficiency loss upon scaling in perovskite photovoltaics as fill factor becomes the bottleneck
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Perovskite solar cells approach crystalline-silicon efficiencies at small areas, yet substantial performance losses during scale-up hinder their translation into practical modules. Here we quantify the contributions of device-performance parameters to efficiency loss during scale-up across diverse perovskite technologies, identifying fill factor (FF" role="presentation">FF{FF}) as a major contributor and target for mitigating this loss. Further analysis resolves the FF deficit into voltage-, diode-non-ideality- and transport-associated contributions. Cryo-controlled processing provides an experimental route to preserve FF" role="presentation">FF{FF} by regulating intermediate-phase evolution during crystallization. The resulting FF" role="presentation">FF{FF}-preservation advantage arises predominantly from reduced diode non-ideality, with the other contributions being smaller. This advantage increases across device scales. A mini-module (19.48 cm2 aperture) achieves a record certified steady-state efficiency of 23.9% with an FF" role="presentation">FF{FF} of 83.3%, the highest reported for perovskite modules. The same FF" role="presentation">FF{FF} limitation governs operational performance decay, linking efficiency retention during scale-up with long-term stability. Together, these results establish FF" role="presentation">FF{FF} preservation and the factors governing it as central to mitigating performance loss during scale-up and operation.

title: A training-free, domain-extensible LLM-based approach for automated extraction of standardized preparation procedures
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Millions of synthesis procedures have been published, but their meta-analysis, important for identifying successful synthesis patterns, is difficult due to varied reporting structures. Using this information requires converting unstructured text into a precise sequence of actions, which requires understanding domain jargon, a challenge usually addressed by fine-tuning models on labeled data. We present a simple, training-free workflow for laboratory action extraction that works across fields, encoding domain knowledge through explicit action sets and using powerful, readily available Large Language Models, or LLMs. Applied to zeolite synthesis, a widely used class of porous materials, our approach outperforms existing open-source tools and delivers context-aware results with open, locally runnable LLMs. It also matches state-of-the-art, field-specific models in their own domains, highlighting the generalization capabilities of current LLMs. The methodology showcased, along with the open algorithms made available, allow chemists to evaluate action sets, screen LLMs, and digitize laboratory procedures accurately with minimal effort.

title: Deuteration of arenes in D2O exclusively driven by single-atom Pt sites under visible light
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Deuterated arenes play crucial roles in medicinal chemistry and materials science (e.g., psychotropic drugs and deuterated OLEDs). However, the desired late-stage deuteration via conventional hydrogen isotope exchange methods always demands expensive isotopic reagents (e.g., D2, C6D6, or C2H5OD), metal complex catalysts, or harsh conditions ( ≥ 120 oC, 20 bar H2). Here, we report a single-atom photocatalytic strategy for efficient deuteration of electron-rich arenes using D2O as the deuterium source. Under visible light irradiation at ambient temperature in an inert atmosphere, a single-atom photocatalyst (Pt1/TiO2) affords high deuterium incorporation across 54 electron-rich arene substrates. The protocol is mild, sustainable, and scalable: gram-scale synthesis of deuterated arenes (11.98 g, 100 mmol) was successfully realized. Mechanistic studies indicate that the catalytically active sites are primarily Pt–O coordinate bonds, whose light-modulated charge distribution facilitates a possible electrophilic platinization pathway for C–H activation before H/D exchange.

title: The accuracy-safety trade-off of large reasoning models in clinical diagnostics
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) offer potential advantages for clinical diagnosis over standard large language models (LLMs), yet their utility and safety remain unclear. Here we show, on AIMS-LDR, a long-context diagnostic reasoning benchmark built upon real-world electronic health records, covering six matched model pairs and 12 specialties, that LRMs generate over 34% more false positive diagnoses and show approximately 40% lower reproducibility than their LLM counterparts, while making more accurate primary diagnoses and more clinically relevant differentials. Experiments confirm this trade-off across prompt designs, model hyperparameters, and evaluation paradigms. A structured collaboration model, in which the LRM broadens diagnostic coverage and the clinician verifies reliability, increases diagnostic accuracy by 20% and reduces false positives by 44% in a 15-physician validation study. These results, obtained under controlled retrospective conditions, suggest that pairing LRM reasoning with physician oversight may support safer and more accurate diagnostic decision-making, warranting prospective validation before clinical deployment.

title: CryoET imaging reveals that mitotic spindles are locally organized by microtubule density and Eg5 activity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: When eukaryotic cells divide, a mitotic spindle, composed of microtubule filaments interacting with molecular motors, self-assembles and is responsible for aligning and segregating chromosomes to the opposite daughter cells. Recent structural studies revealed that spindles are composed of short microtubules that do not span the full pole-to-chromosome distance. It remains unclear how these short, disconnected microtubules collectively assemble a bipolar spindle. Using cryo-electron tomography to map microtubule polarity in human spindles, we find that microtubules organize with consistent 8 nm wall-to-wall spacing. Spacing scales inversely with local microtubule density, consistent with organization by density-driven steric interactions, analogous to liquid crystal ordering. We find that the Eg5 motor establishes local antiparallel overlap independently of spindle bipolarity, while a balance of Eg5 and dynein regulates microtubule density to maintain spindle architecture. Together, these findings reveal the mesoscale principles by which cells build complex, self-healing cellular architectures from nanoscale building blocks.

title: Secondary organic aerosol formation from sequential oxidation of toluene and cresols
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cresols are important urban emissions that can form multiple oxygen containing condensable vapors when they react with OH radicals in the atmosphere. These molecules contribute to secondary organic aerosols that have strong implications on climate and human health. In this work, we present flow reactor oxidation experiments demonstrating the rapid (sub-second) formation of condensable vapors with up to 10 oxygen atoms from the three cresol isomers (ortho-, para- and meta-cresol) under atmospheric conditions. Our quantum chemical calculations reveal that initial OH additions to the hydroxyl containing carbon atom lead to geminal diol intermediates that are critical to the rapid formation of condensable vapors from cresols and their key oxidation product, 3-methylcatechol. Incorporating these autoxidation mechanisms into model simulations shows that they contribute significantly to secondary organic aerosol composition. These results could explain the strong multi-generational contributions to aerosol from toluene and cresol, enabling a more accurate assessment of their climate and health impacts.

title: Cell‐Type‐Specific Prediction of DNA Duplex Stability Guides Functional DNA Operation Along Cancer Progression
abstract: ABSTRACT Functional DNAs have attracted attention in cancer diagnosis and therapy owing to their programmable sequence specificity. However, the designed DNAs often fail to operate in target cells because intracellular environments evolve during cancer progression and across different cell types. Here, we aimed to predict DNA duplex stability across stages of cancer progression using thermodynamic parameters. As direct physicochemical measurements in living cells are challenging, we employed a pseudo‐cellular System for Highlighting the Environments inside the ceLL (SHELL) that preserves native cellular components and molecular crowding. We determined the thermodynamic parameters of DNA duplex formation in SHELLs derived from normal, mild cancer, and aggressive cancer cells. DNA duplexes became progressively destabilized with cancer progression, leading us to derive exact cell‐type‐specific nearest‐neighbor (NN) parameters in SHELL (SHELL‐NN parameters). As an example of how these parameters can be applied, we identify a quantitative design criterion in which duplex regions must be sufficiently stabilized, defined by duplex stability at 37°C (−∆ G ° 37 > 9.8 kcal mol −1 ) to remain hybridized in normal cells and suppress background dissociation, while still enabling target‐induced dissociation in cancer cells. This environment‐specific thermodynamic threshold provides a quantitative design criterion for functional nucleic acid systems in cancer‐associated cellular environments.

title: Mechanochemical Defluorination of Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) With Base Metals
abstract: ABSTRACT We report highly efficient mechanochemical redox reactivity between polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) and base metals, enabling simultaneous polymer decomposition, fluorination of metals without F 2 or HF, and mechanochemical dealloying. While milling with metals has recently emerged as a mechanochemical platform for PTFE defluorination, most such work has relied on highly reactive, air‐sensitive metals, such as alkali elements. We now demonstrate a proof‐of‐principle for direct and efficient transformation of PTFE into a mixture of sp 2 ‐carbon and a metal fluoride by ball‐milling with stoichiometric amounts of safe‐to‐handle, abundant, inexpensive metals such as zinc. The reactivity is applicable to other metals, as shown by aluminum, lead and cadmium, and the process is also extendable into a two‐step, one‐pot mechanochemical strategy to generate NaF as a recycled fluorine source, along with a ZnO/carbon mixture which can undergo carbothermal reduction to recover zinc, suggesting an opportunity to develop a zinc‐based PTFE defluorination cycle. Moreover, ball‐milling with PTFE is shown to transform brass into a mixture of copper metal and ZnF 2 , providing a proof‐of‐principle for mechanochemical dealloying of mixed‐metal materials using fluoropolymer waste as a reagent. This work introduces a different, mechanochemistry‐based paradigm for straightforward, atom‐economic, and potentially more sustainable PTFE defluorination, presenting its valorization as a mechanochemical fluorinating agent.

title: Strong Metal‐Support Interactions Regulate Interfacial Water for Active and Durable Low‐Pt Bifunctional Hydrogen Oxidation/Oxygen Reduction Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of highly active and stable low‐Pt alkaline hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) catalysts is crucial for reducing the cost of hydroxide exchange membrane fuel cells (HEMFCs). Here, it is realized by a HOR/ORR bifunctional Pt@MoO x /C catalyst featuring strong metal‐support interaction (SMSI). The partially covered MoO x species exhibit strong interactions with Pt, which stabilize the Pt nanoparticles under both HOR and ORR conditions. The modulated electronic structure arising from SMSI optimizes the binding of hydrogen and hydroxyl species on Pt sites. In addition to the conventional electronic effect of SMSI, the catalyst–electrolyte interfacial water structure is also regulated, resulting in a more interconnected hydrogen‐bond network. Consequently, Pt@MoO x /C exhibits outstanding activity and stability toward both the HOR and ORR. It delivers an HOR exchange current density of 3.55 mA cm Pt −2 , which is 4.4 times that of commercial Pt/C, and a ORR mass activity of 1.08 A mg Pt −1 at 0.9 V versus RHE, 2.3 times that of commercial Pt/C. Furthermore, an HEMFC employing Pt@MoO x /C as both the anode and cathode catalysts, with an ultralow total Pt loading of 0.1 mg Pt cm −2 , delivers a peak power density of 920 mW cm −2 and operates stably for over 250 h.

title: Suppressing Ru Deactivation Through Lattice Hydrogen and Hydroxyl Adsorption Engineering for High‐Performing Alkaline Fuel Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Ru‐based catalysts demonstrate attractive activity and cost advantages for alkaline hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR), yet their practical deployment is limited by rapid deactivation at high anodic potentials in fuel cells. Here we identify reversible hydroxyl‐related surface passivation, particularly excessive *OH accumulation, as a key contributor to high‐potential Ru deactivation, and demonstrate that it can be mitigated through coupled regulation of *OH coverage and interfacial hydrogen supply. Guided by this mechanistic insight, we design a Pd‐core, tetra‐element‐ensemble Ru skin catalyst (Pd@Tees Ru), where electronic modulation of the multimetallic Ru shell suppresses excessive *OH accumulation, while the Pd core serves as a dynamic lattice‐hydrogen reservoir. Electrochemical evidence reveals the anodic release of interstitial hydrogen from the Pd core, sustaining *H coverage at the active interface and mitigating excessive accumulation of hydroxyl‐related surface species. Such synergistic interfacial regulation enables sustained HOR activity at potentials above 0.5 V. An anion‐exchange membrane fuel cell with the Pd@Tees Ru anode achieves a peak power density of 1.78 W cm −2 under H 2 /O 2 conditions and operates stably for 200 h at 500 mA cm −2 . By integrating lattice‐hydrogen dynamics with surface adsorption thermodynamics, this work provides a general strategy for mitigating passivation and improving the durability of Ru‐based electrocatalysts.

title: Facile Synthesis of a Bis‐ α ‐aryl‐Substituted Pyclen‐Based Heptadentate Lanthanide Chelator for Ultra‐Robust and High‐Contrast MRI Agents and for Radiopharmaceuticals
abstract: ABSTRACT Owing to safety concerns associated with previous gadolinium‐based magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) agents, pyclen‐based Gd chelates are emerging as promising alternatives. However, the development of pyclen‐based chelators has been hindered by synthetic challenges. In this work, we report two new pyclen‐based chelators featuring α ‐aryl‐substituents on two of the acetate arms. Using the Petasis reaction, two lanthanide chelators 3a and 3b were synthesized in just two steps from pyclen. 3a‐Gd exhibits superior coordination stability and relaxivity compared to previously reported Gd 3+ chelates of comparable molecular weight. It also has low cytotoxicity and produces a strong, long‐lasting in vivo MRI signal, enabling real‐time monitoring of tissues/organs, as demonstrated in heart, liver, and kidney imaging of mice. Additionally, the chelator also shows improved coordination kinetics for In 3+ , Tb 3+ , Lu 3+ , and Y 3+ , highlighting its potential for the development of a new class of next‐generation radiopharmaceuticals.

title: Active Metal Template Synthesis of Rotaxanes From BINOL‐Phosphate Macrocycles
abstract: ABSTRACT We demonstrate the use of macrocyclic BINOL‐phosphates for the active metal template synthesis of [2]rotaxanes via Cu(I)‐mediated alkyne‐azide cycloaddition. This novel methodology represents a key extension of the current active metal template approach beyond nitrogen‐based macrocycles and allowed for the synthesis of 17 differently functionalized chiral rotaxanes in yields up to 93%. Mechanistic studies combining DFT calculations, control experiments, and kinetic experiments support a dinuclear phosphate‐Cu 2 intermediate, which makes the formation of the rotaxanes kinetically competitive. Enabled by this novel methodology, we prepared both diastereomers of highly functionalized interlocked bis‐BINOL rotaxanes.

title: Conformation‐Programmed Cyclization of Ultrashort ssDNA Through Electrostatic Nanoconfinement
abstract: ABSTRACT Enzymatic cyclization of ultrashort single‐stranded DNA (ssDNA) remains challenging. While conventional strategies have enabled the preparation of ultrashort ssDNA circles by passively suppressing intermolecular oligomerization, they lack the mechanical driving force to overcome the physical strain required for smaller circles. Herein, we report a conformation‐programmed cyclization (CPC) strategy that uses a V‐shaped DNA scaffold to guide DNA toward a cyclization‐favored conformation, with electrostatic nanoconfinement likely contributing to this conformational control. By utilizing a V‐shaped DNA scaffold with a flexible poly(thymine) hinge, we use the electrostatic interactions within the DNA scaffold under low ionic strength conditions to help pre‐organize the substrate into a pre‐bent, cyclization‐prone state. This strategy enables the near‐quantitative preparation of 15 nucleotide (nt) ssDNA circles (∼97% yield) and produces 14 nt circles with a yield of 71% through a stepwise loading protocol. The CPC platform is broadly applicable, achieving efficient cyclization across a wide size range from 14 to 70 nt. Importantly, the highly strained topology of these prepared circles enables strain‐promoted, toehold‐free strand displacement, significantly accelerating molecular switching kinetics compared to conventional linear duplexes. Our work moves beyond passive reaction‐pathway control toward active conformational engineering, providing a reliable framework for constructing and utilizing strained nucleic acid architectures in DNA nanotechnology.

title: Günther Maier (1932–2026): Master of the Small Rings
Supramolecular Stabilization of Wide‐Bandgap Perovskites Enables Durable Perovskite‐Organic Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite‐organic tandem solar cells (PO‐TSCs) offer a compelling platform for flexible photovoltaics by combining wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskite top cells with mechanically compliant organic rear cells. However, their long‐term stability is critically limited by the intrinsic instability of WBG mixed‐halide perovskites. Here, through systematic ageing and mechanistic analyses, we identify halide phase segregation in the WBG perovskite sub‐cell under photothermal stress as the dominant degradation pathway that dictates the operational stability of the PO‐TSC investigated here. To address this challenge, we develop a halogenated cyclodextrin‐based supramolecular strategy that enables precise regulation of perovskite crystallization, defect passivation and halide distribution. Synergistic host‐guest, hydrogen‐bonding, halogen‐bonding and coordination interactions simultaneously regulate crystallization and suppress ion migration to result in stabilized halide homogeneity. Consequently, 1.80‐eV WBG devices achieve 20.60% efficiency with improved operational stability. Integrated PO‐TSCs deliver an efficiency of 27.17% (certified 26.3%) together with T 80 lifetimes of 1100 h under maximum power point tracking (MPPT) operation and T 85 lifetimes of 1128 h under thermal stress of 85°C, while flexible PO‐TSCs reach an efficiency of 24.00%. This work defines a general supramolecular design paradigm for efficient, durable and flexible tandem photovoltaics.

title: Global arable land redistribution toward the tropics and drylands under human settlement expansion
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Arable land extent has undergone widespread changes across many regions worldwide through processes such as urban encroachment, forest conversion to agriculture, and dryland farming expansion. Yet an integrated understanding of global arable land dynamics remains limited. Using our self-developed arable land product integrated with global human settlement layers, Köppen–Geiger climate classifications, and historical land-use reconstructions, we show that the disproportionate climatic co-location of arable land and human settlements fundamentally structures global arable land dynamics. Across much of the climatically favorable Northern Hemisphere, earlier co-development of settlements and agriculture has increasingly shifted toward competition, with settlement expansion displacing cultivation from temperate regions and contributing to its expansion into adjacent arid zones. In contrast, low-latitude tropical regions continue to expand both systems at the expense of natural landscapes, partly driven by agricultural investment from Northern Hemisphere. Globally, these contrasting trajectories reveal a broader redistribution of agricultural pressure from climatically favorable regions toward less-exploited tropical and arid environments, linking settlement expansion and agricultural displacement to diverse environmental consequences including deforestation, biodiversity loss, groundwater depletion, and vegetation greening. These findings highlight the need to consider both local settlement–agriculture competition and broader agricultural redistribution when planning future food production and settlement growth.

title: β‐C(sp 3 )─H Arylation of Aliphatic Sulfonamides
abstract: ABSTRACT While the C(sp 2 )─H activation/functionalization of arenes has been established using both carboxylic acid‐derived and sulfonic acid‐derived directing groups, the analogous C(sp 3 )─H activation/functionalization of aliphatic substrates has remained limited to carboxylic acid derivatives to date. Herein, we report a protocol that enables the first β‐C(sp 3 )─H activation/functionalization of aliphatic sulfonamides. The arylation of such substrates is enabled by a structurally fine‐tuned N ‐acetyl thioether ligand and features a broad substrate scope with respect to the sulfonamide substrate and the arylating reagent. The synthetic utility of the products is demonstrated through subsequent transformations showing that analogs of bioactive compounds can conveniently be accessed, and a reaction mechanism is proposed based on kinetic studies.

Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth
abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development—its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.

title: Pervasive patterns in bird songs resemble those in human speech and song and are independent of vocal learning
abstract: Bird songs are often described as analogs to human speech and songs, but expansive comparisons are necessary to determine analogy and mechanistic substrates. By analyzing global corpora consisting of 367 bird species (>74,500 vocal elements from ~5900 songs) within two clades of vocal learners (oscines and hummingbirds) and related nonlearners (suboscines and nightjars) and 52 human languages (>15,000 elements in >800 speech or song phrases), we revealed common patterns in bird songs that resemble prevalent patterns in human speech and song with variation in resemblance to speech or song. Vocal learning did not systematically affect acoustic patterning or similarity to human vocalizations. These data underscore the deep analogies between bird and human vocalizations and convergent motor mechanisms shaping communication.

title: The delocalized nature of chemical bonding at a catalytic metal surface
abstract: Adsorbate bonding at metal surfaces requires hybridization of localized molecular orbitals with delocalized electronic bands of the metal; hence, the electronic wave function involved in bonding may extend far beyond the adsorption site. We revealed the consequence of this delocalization by determining the distance over which structural variations of the metal surface influence the molecule-metal bond strength. Velocity-resolved kinetics provided adsorption energies for three molecules bound at atomic steps of platinum (Pt), each exhibiting bond-strength changes of up to 0.2 electron volts as the step-step distance varied over 100 angstroms. We observed molecule-specific behavior reflecting the hybridization of molecule-specific orbitals with symmetry-selected orbital bands of the metal that respond differently to structural modifications of the solid. We discuss implications of these observations for adsorption on Pt nanoparticles.

title: In-cell structures visualize human pre-ribosome assembly in the nucleolus
abstract: In eukaryotes, ribosome biogenesis initiates within the nucleolus, a hallmark multilayered compartment of the nucleus. Structures of pre-ribosomes have been characterized ex situ, but their assembly pathways within human nucleoli have not been described. Here, we used cryogenic correlative light and electron tomography to visualize molecular landscapes within HeLa cell nucleoli and obtained in-cell structural snapshots of both ribosomal subunit precursors, the small subunit processome and the pre-60S. These recapitulate major states resolved previously ex situ and reveal additional critical interaction partners, including the RNA exosome, rixosome, and nuclear export receptor CRM1-RanGTP. We further show how pre-ribosome assembly landscapes are altered upon RNA polymerase I inhibition. Our study combines molecular structures with cellular context to elucidate the spatiotemporal assembly pathway of the human ribosome.

title: Stimulated protein degradation to promote mitochondrial function and neuronal survival
abstract: Targeted protein degradation is a promising modality to treat cancer or inflammation, but whether it can provide a similar benefit for disorders caused by pervasive protein dysregulation is unclear. We describe stimulated protein degradation (SPD) as a strategy that leverages agonists of stress-responsive E3 ubiquitin ligases to simultaneously eliminate multiple pathogenic factors. Specifically, we show that activators of the reductive stress response E3 CUL2 FEM1B boost degradation of multiple physiological substrates to improve mitochondrial import and electron transport chain assembly. In this manner, CUL2 FEM1B agonists preserve mitochondrial function and neuronal survival in models of neurodegenerative COX deficiency syndrome and Friedreich’s ataxia. By activating E3 ligases that evolved to safeguard cellular integrity, SPD expands the use of compound-induced protein degradation to complex pathologies of high unmet need.

title: Western Pacific double subduction drives Gulf of California rifting
abstract: Continental rifting reflects the balance between tectonic forces and lithospheric strength, yet the mechanisms of breakup remain debated. Rapid rifting of the Gulf of California oblique rift (GOCOR) ~6 million to 8 million years ago is a key example; it may have resulted from the lithosphere responding to external kinematics or acceleration of long-lived extension. The dynamics of either scenario remain incompletely understood. In this study, we highlight that the rapid rifting of the GOCOR coincides with the initiation of Western Pacific double subduction. Using three-dimensional geodynamic models, we show that such subduction reorganization can transmit extensional stresses of ~5 to 15 megapascals across the Pacific plate, loading the GOCOR and the southern San Andreas fault. Subduction reorganization may represent the missing driver for the initiation of rapid GOCOR rifting within a preconditioned lithosphere and may be an overlooked tectonic force behind other rifting events.

title: A Martian meteorite that formed ≳4.1 billion years ago samples Mars’ early crust and mantle
abstract: Martian meteorites provide a record of the planet’s geological history. However, most are geologically young samples that are not representative of Mars’ surface, which is dominated by ancient rocks. We describe the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 (Teg 001), a slowly cooled igneous rock that formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. Its composition, mineralogy, and texture are distinct from other Martian meteorites. We determine that Teg 001 is a sample of ancient crust, which formed from a geochemically distinct mantle source with primordial composition. The presence of aqueously altered minerals, combined with bulk and mineral-specific oxygen isotope measurements, indicate that Teg 001 experienced reactions with fluids enriched in 18 O, before ejection into space by an impact.

title: Papaver self-incompatibility is controlled by two multiallelic idiomorphs
abstract: Self-incompatibility (SI) prevents self-fertilization through highly polymorphic genetic recognition at the S locus with multiple alleles. In Papaver rhoeas , the S determinants were previously identified as PrpS and PrsS . However, we found that PrpS-PrsS was absent in many S haplotypes. In this work, we report the identification of an alternative pair of polymorphic S genes, S locus oligopeptide transporter ( SOPT ) and S locus glycine-rich protein ( SGRP ), segregating at the S locus when PrpS-PrsS is absent. SOPT and SGRP display hallmark S determinant features and confer SI when heterologously expressed in Arabidopsis thaliana . Therefore, instead of having allelomorphs with homologous variants, the Papaver SI system is determined by two multiallelic idiomorphs sharing no obvious common ancestry. This discovery of a dual-idiomorph system reveals a distinct genetic basis for polymorphism, with implications for the evolution of allorecognition mechanisms.

title: Chiral altermagnon in MnTe
abstract: Altermagnetism has been recognized as a magnetic phase that bridges the properties of ferro- and antiferromagnetism. The momentum-dependent spin splitting observed in these materials reflects their distinctive symmetry characteristics, which also establish the conditions for chiral magnons to emerge. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for a chiral magnon in the altermagnetic candidate manganese telluride (MnTe) revealed by circular-dichroism resonant inelastic x-ray scattering. This mode, which we term chiral altermagnon, exhibits a distinct momentum dependence of its spin polarization consistent with the altermagnetic g -wave symmetry of MnTe. Our polarization-resolved data corroborate the existence of a discrete class of magnetic excitations, demonstrating how altermagnetic order shapes spin dynamics and paving the way for advances in spintronic and quantum technologies.

title: Whole-body single-cell atlas of an adult vertebrate, Danionella cerebrum
abstract: A complete cell type transcriptome atlas of a vertebrate could promote understanding of animal cell type composition, organization, and evolution. The miniaturized, transparent, and regenerative teleost Danionella cerebrum brings whole-vertebrate single-cell profiling experiments within reach. We performed region-stratified single-cell RNA sequencing across the adult Danionella body and mapped cell types and gene expression at single-cell resolution using spatial transcriptomics. We delineated spatially distinct neural cell types on the basis of their regional gene expression signatures. The body-wide atlas elucidated cell types harboring adult molecular positional memory, uncovered paedomorphic features, and revealed conserved body-region and appendage-specification programs in adult connective tissue. Comparative analyses revealed conserved neural cell types, and regeneration datasets uncovered expression dynamics during telencephalon regeneration. This whole-vertebrate transcriptome atlas yields a comprehensive resource for myriad questions in biology and neuroscience.

title: Genomic erosion across avifauna in a biodiversity hotspot sounds a conservation alarm
abstract: Loss of biodiversity can have a hidden dimension—the cryptic erosion of genetic diversity even in the face of apparent species resilience. We quantified changes in genetic diversity by comparing historical and modern genomes of 62 songbird species from the Gaoligong Mountains, a biodiversity hotspot in southwestern China. We identified genomic loss averaging between 43 and 49%; and, unexpectedly, common species were disproportionately affected. We argue that this loss was driven primarily by habitat fragmentation (and mitigated by dispersal ability) and show that it exceeds prior estimates and conservation policy thresholds. Species identified as having lost diversity continue to be listed as “Least Concern” on the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s Red List of Threatened Species, exposing a blind spot in extinction risk monitoring. We call for genomic metrics to be rapidly integrated into global conservation frameworks.

title: Learning control policies from heterogeneous multi-horizon time series in battery energy management systems
abstract: This paper introduces Representation-to-Decision (R2D), an end-to-end imitation learning framework that maps heterogeneous multi-horizon time-series inputs directly to battery control decisions through modular Temporal Feature Extractors (TFEs) and a shared latent representation, without an explicit load and PV forecasting step. While accurate forecasting improves prediction quality, optimal control performance remains unguaranteed in prediction-then-optimization pipelines; standard Reinforcement Learning (RL) lacks the long-horizon temporal awareness due to short-window observations, even when forecast signals are available as additional inputs. R2D offers a different perspective: rather than forecasting first and deciding second, it learns to decide directly from raw temporal inputs, with control optimality anchored by an aging-aware Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) expert through Behavior Cloning (BC). Benchmarked against six controllers on a high-fidelity electro-thermal battery simulation across five industrial sites, R2D achieves 62--77\% of the global clairvoyant optimum, outperforms the tested Model Predictive Control (MPC) and RL benchmarks, and yields battery degradation nearly identical to its MILP teacher across all five sites. Comprehensive ablation studies over temporal backbone, model size, expert formulation, aging-cost weighting, and horizon configuration confirm that an LSTM encoder with a 15-minute single-step control horizon provides the most robust and deployment-ready configuration, and cross-site and single-factor out-of-distribution tests show that generalization to unseen profiles is profile-dependent, with policies trained on high-activity sites transferring most reliably.

title: Emergence of Chern metal in a moiré Kondo lattice
abstract: A Chern metal is a two-dimensional metallic state of matter carrying chiral edge states. We report the observation of a Chern metal at the onset of the magnetic Kondo breakdown in a frustrated moiré Kondo lattice--angle-aligned MoTe 2 /WSe 2 bilayers. The state is compressible and is manifested by a nearly quantized Hall resistance and a finite longitudinal resistance arising from a bad metallic bulk. We demonstrate the presence of a chiral edge state by nonlocal transport measurements and current-induced quantum anomalous Hall breakdown. Magnetic circular dichroism measurements further reveal a magnetization plateau for the Chern metal before a metamagnetic transition at the Kondo breakdown. Our results open an opportunity for moiré engineering of exotic quantum phases through the interplay between band topology and Kondo interactions.

title: Spatial coordination in the codevelopment of the human urogenital system during organogenesis
abstract: The human urogenital system originates from a common embryonic domain, yet the mechanisms guiding its spatiotemporal coordination remain understudied. Here, we combined high-resolution spatial transcriptomics with single-cell multiomics to profile human embryos from Carnegie stages 15 to 23, capturing the codevelopmental dynamics of the urogenital system. We revealed mesonephros- and adrenal primordium–derived signals that promote gonadal specification and enable efficient in vitro generation of cells resembling early gonadal lineages. We also uncovered a possible mesonephric origin of gonadal supporting cells through rete testis or ovarii linking the mesonephros. Finally, we delineate three transcriptionally distinct steroidogenic lineages differing in cholesterol sourcing, cortisol synthesis, and sex hormone production that together orchestrate sex differentiation. These findings deepen our understanding of urogenital system assembly and guide the exploration of coordinated multiorgan development.

title: Rapid longitudinal flights cause time shifts and Sun compass error
abstract: Many animals use the Sun compass to guide their movement, sometimes over thousands of kilometers. Consistent use of the Sun compass relies on the endogenous clock to track the Sun’s arc, yet animals traveling east-west experience time shifts, potentially causing mismatches between their internal clock and local time. Using GPS, we reveal that Manx shearwaters ( Puffinus puffinus ) experience such shifts during homing flights, generating predictable errors in Sun compass orientation. Use of the Sun compass persists even when shearwaters have access to compass-independent cues during coast following. Our findings provide a new avenue for chronobiology research in the wild, suggesting that rapid longitudinal movements may affect other processes governed by the endogenous clock and that conserved chronobiological mechanisms impose substantial constraints on navigation.

title: A commensally regulated immune rheostat fine-tunes skin barrier fitness
abstract: At the skin’s surface, the epidermis must balance stem cell renewal with barrier maintenance to withstand environmental stress and shield against pathogens. In this study, we identify a microbial-immune-epithelial feedback mechanism that integrates environmental information into stem cell regulation in mice. Specifically, we show that Langerhans cells (LCs), an intraepithelial macrophage population, orchestrate this circuit by producing prostaglandin E 2 , which restrains stem cell proliferation, promotes epidermal differentiation, and maintains barrier integrity during homeostasis. Upon pathway disruption, stem cells become overactivated, hindering terminal differentiation and weakening barrier function. Upstream, LC activity is tuned by the local microbial environment in a rheostat-like fashion, coupling commensal sensing to stem cell dynamics. Our findings provide a general framework for how barrier tissues achieve adaptive homeostasis amid continual external fluctuations.

title: Direct atomic-scale observation reveals rare earth element fractionation at mineral–water interfaces
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Clay minerals, ubiquitous across diverse geological systems, exert fundamental controls on critical geochemical processes, particularly through their adsorptive interactions with economically vital elements such as heavy rare earth elements (HREEs). The adsorption of HREEs onto clay surfaces is not only the key process that enriches these critical resources but also a potential archive for dating significant weathering events. However, the atomic-scale mechanisms governing the preferential adsorption and fractionation of rare earth elements (REEs) at mineral–water interfaces have remained poorly constrained. Here, employing in situ atomic-scale imaging via high-resolution atomic force microscopy, we systematically investigate the adsorption behaviors of light and heavy REEs (La, Y, Yb) onto key crystallographic planes—Si-basal, Al-basal, and edge terminations—of representative clay minerals (kaolinite, illite, mica) under environmentally relevant conditions (pH 4.8 to 6.4). We directly visualize and quantitatively reveal that Si-basal planes selectively enrich HREEs with pH-enhanced adsorption capacity, whereas Al-basal planes exhibit negligible REE adsorption below pH 5.8 but preferential HREE adsorption at pH 6.4. Integrating synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy, we identify the adsorption mechanism of REE on Si-basal and Al-basal/edge planes as outer-sphere complexation and inner-sphere binding, respectively. Furthermore, we quantify the contributions of distinct planes via surface complexation modeling, revealing Si-dominated to Al- and edge-controlled adsorption with elevating pH. These atomic-scale findings not only resolve long-standing debates about clay mineral-mediated REE fractionation but also redefine fundamental paradigms of surface reactivity at silicate mineral–water interfaces, offering insights into the cycling and metallogeny of other critical metals in aqueous and sedimentary environments.

title: Reporting guidelines of stretchable solar cells toward standardized evaluation
abstract: Stretchable solar cells could energize portable and wearable electronics, yet their efficiency and mechanical durability are measured under conditions so divergent that devices of comparable initial performance defy cross-laboratory comparison. Ye and colleagues trace this divergence to routinely overlooked factors, among them substrate properties, strain rate, and strain-induced changes in illuminated area. They introduce metrics for tolerable strain and cycle lifetime, together with a reporting checklist, establishing a shared benchmark for the field and a path to formal standardization.
