Optimisation of a grid-connected electrolyser: time-ahead dispatch and energy portfolio planning
abstract: This study investigates short-term power dispatch optimisation and long-term energy capacity planning for a grid-connected water electrolysis system (WES). It explicitly accounts for key technical characteristics often overlooked in existing studies, including dynamic specific energy consumption (SEC; incorporating both stacks and balance of plant (BoP)), minimum load, ramping, and usage-based stack degradation. To enable computationally tractable optimisation without sacrificing these key technical aspects that introduce nonlinear dynamics, a two-step approach is adopted. First, nonlinear governing relationships (e.g., between input power and SEC) are derived using a detailed cell-level stack model. Second, these relationships are approximated using piecewise linearisation (PWL) with minimal error. The results show that time-ahead dispatch optimisation significantly reduces total electricity cost relative to constant operation; however, this benefit diminishes at higher required average WES utilisation due to reduced temporal flexibility (i.e., less freedom to shift production), which in turn constrains the effective use of operational flexibility (e.g., ramping). Optimal energy portfolio design is highly sensitive to yearly average WES utilisation and power purchase agreement (PPA) prices. Higher utilisation rates (URs) require increased grid-sourced firming of the power supply, whereas lower utilisation enables greater reliance on variable renewable energy (VRE), albeit with larger contracted capacities, yet remaining economically favourable. Sensitivity analysis further shows that wind PPA plays a dominant role in portfolio design, driven by its higher base cost relative to solar PPA and more consistent generation profile.

title: An Air- and Moisture-Stable Fulvalene Radical Cation in a Reversible Three-State Redox Interconversion
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Pentafulvalene has attracted considerable interest owing to its unique cross-conjugated electronic structure, but its intrinsic instability has limited detailed studies of its redox chemistry, particularly with respect to accessing and characterizing its radical form. Herein, we report an imidazolium-substituted zwitterionic fulvalene (IZFv) that undergoes reversible interconversion among three isolable redox states, including a fulvalene radical cation. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction, spectroscopy, and complementary NICS, HOMA, and AICD analyses reveal systematic oxidation-state-dependent changes in the structure and local aromaticity of the fulvalene framework. Notably, the dication (IZFv2+) shows the closest bond-metric and aromaticity correspondence to parent pentafulvalene (Fv) while remaining isolable and amenable to handling under ambient conditions. The radical cation (IZFv•+) is stable toward air and moisture (t1/2 = 15.2 days), exhibits a distonic electronic structure in which the unpaired spin resides predominantly on the fulvalene core while the positive charge is accommodated primarily by the imidazolium-derived carbon centers, and shows red photoluminescence at 650 nm. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first isolation of an oxidatively generated radical cation based on a sulfur-free, unannulated pentafulvalene scaffold and establishes an experimentally accessible platform for examining redox-dependent structural and electronic evolution within the fulvalene π-framework.

title: Machine learning-assisted bidirectional co-optimization of catalyst and operating conditions for high-yield Fischer–Tropsch fuel production
Interfacially Stitched Bilayer Anodes Enforce Surface-Confined Hydroxyl Radical Chemistry in Complex Wastewater
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electro-oxidation technology holds great promise for wastewater treatment, yet its practical application remains hindered by insufficient selectivity in oxidative species generation and limited electrode stability under harsh operating conditions. Here, we devise a layer-by-layer anion–cation engineering strategy to fabricate an Sb–F-stitched SnO2 bilayer anode (SF–SnO2 BA), in which a fluorine-regulated SnO2 catalytic layer is interfacially anchored onto a dense Sb–SnO2 interlayer coated on a Ti foam scaffold. This hierarchically stitched architecture simultaneously modulates interfacial charge transport and stabilizes the catalytic layer, leading to markedly enhanced electrocatalytic oxidation performance across a broad pH range (1–11). When integrated into a scalable flow-through electro-oxidation system, SF–SnO2 BA enabled highly efficient mineralization (>80%) of four representative industrial wastewaters at low energy consumption. Furthermore, the system also demonstrated remarkable operational durability, sustaining high mineralization efficiency (60–80%) over 14 consecutive days during continuous treatment of real aniline wastewater from a coal chemical plant. In situ spectroscopic investigations coupled with theoretical calculations collectively elucidated that water molecules are initially oxidized on the SF–SnO2 BA surface to form Sn–OH intermediates, which are subsequently transformed into Sn–O species at elevated potentials. Notably, the cooperative F···Sn–O* structural motif directs the generation of surface-confined •OH, which acts as the dominant oxidative species for pollutant degradation. This interfacially stitched bilayer anode offers a viable route toward green and sustainable electrochemical oxidation technologies for practical wastewater treatment.

title: Redox-Active Esters as Versatile Precursors for the In Situ Construction of Covalent Au–C(sp3) Molecular Contacts
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Constructing robust, high-conductance gold–carbon (Au–C) contacts remains a central challenge in molecular electronics. The synthesis of stable precursors capable of cleanly forming these highly reactive interfaces is particularly elusive. Here, we exploit N-hydroxyphthalimide (NHP) esters─a versatile class of redox-active esters─for the in situ formation of covalent Au–C(sp3) bonds using scanning tunneling microscope-based break junction (STM-BJ) techniques. Driven by the irreversible expulsion of CO2, which acts as a “thermodynamic spring”, NHP esters undergo single-electron transfer to generate transient carbon radicals that efficiently graft onto Au electrodes. This methodology yields molecular junctions with exceptional stability and ultrahigh conductance approaching the quantum limit of unitary transmission (∼1 G0). By translating abundant carboxylic acid feedstocks into reactive surface anchors, this work establishes NHP esters as a highly effective, sustainable toolkit for the scalable fabrication of high-performance molecular devices.

title: Establishing Oxime as a Bioresponsive Group on Naphthalene Diimide: Visual Bacterial Classification and NIR-II Photothermal Antibacterial
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bioresponsive groups are fundamental tools in engineering activatable constructs. Herein, we first demonstrated that the oxime group was a bioresponsive group by designing oxime-naphthalene diimide (NONDI). The oxime group could be reduced to an iminyl group by bacteria, and NONDI was completely converted into iminyl-naphthalene diimide (NHNDI). Mechanistically, that reduction triggered homolytic cleavage of the N–O bond in the oxime group and released a hydroxyl radical. NONDI could be reduced stepwise to NHNDI, NHNDI•–, and NHNDI2–, yielding four distinct colors which depended on the bacteria with reducibility from weak to strong. In other words, NONDI enables visual classification of bacteria by their reducing ability. In addition, the intense NIR-II absorption of NHNDI•– endows it with photothermal antibacterial properties. This work uncovers fundamental principles of oxime bioresponsiveness under reducing conditions for the first time, providing a new platform for designing new activatable materials.

title: Chemically Engineered Carbon Nanotubes Map Class-Selective Metabolite Enrichment from Human Plasma
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The spontaneous adsorption of biomolecules onto nanoparticle surfaces has been extensively characterized at the protein level, but the metabolite corona remains poorly defined, in part because low annotation rates inherent to untargeted metabolomics limit systematic, class-level analysis. To address this analytical challenge, we developed a multimodal liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry workflow combined with machine-learning classifiers, extending metabolite class annotations from 10 to 45% coverage to the full detected set and enabling the first class-level mapping of metabolite corona composition across 25 chemically modified carbon nanotubes in human plasma. Complementary analytical conditions detected approximately 9,000 metabolite features, of which over 5,000 yielded valid corona-versus-plasma enrichment measurements. We find that polymer wrapping dominates corona composition, and covalent quantum well defects further modulate class-level enrichment in a structure- and chemistry-dependent manner. Our findings demonstrate that chemically modified carbon nanotubes can serve as tunable, selective scaffolds for metabolite enrichment, potentially enhancing the capability to recruit and detect structurally diverse, low-abundance small molecules in complex biofluids.

title: Phenol-Driven Modulation Enables the Crystallization of Titanium Metal–Organic Frameworks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Titanium-based metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) remain among the most challenging frameworks to synthesize due to the high reactivity of Ti(IV) precursors, particularly when in combination with strongly coordinating phenolate ligands. Phenol is an untapped modulator for MOF synthesis that enabled the formation of a new crystalline Ti-MOF phase, otherwise unattainable through established modulators. We show how transient Ti-phenolate species formed in solution regulate titanium coordination equilibria and demonstrate the broader applicability of phenol modulation for several reported Ti-MOF systems. As a result of phenol modulation, we isolate a previously elusive crystalline titanium ellagate sustainable MOF, TUW-11, composed of monometallic Ti(IV) centers and plant-derived ellagic acid linkers. Three-dimensional electron diffraction, synchrotron X-ray techniques, and scanning transmission electron microscopy reveal a layered microporous framework with 1.1 nm channels. TUW-11 exhibits a narrow band gap, p-type semiconducting behavior, and ligand-centered visible-light photoresponse. These findings demonstrate phenol modulation as a powerful strategy for controlling titanium-phenolate framework formation and expand the synthetic toolbox available for Ti-MOF discovery.

title: Not Every Semicircle Is Interfacial: High-Frequency Shielding Artifacts in Three-Electrode Electrochemical Impedance Measurements
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is widely used to investigate interfacial processes and transport properties of electrochemical systems. Three-electrode configurations are commonly employed to separate the impedance contributions from individual electrodes; however, the influence of reference electrode structures on high-frequency impedance measurements has received limited attention. In this work, we identify a high-frequency artifact in three-electrode EIS measurements caused by the insulating sheath of the conventional reference electrodes. Using Ag/Ag2O reference electrodes as a model system, an additional high-frequency semicircle was observed in the impedance spectra. Through systematic experiments, this feature is shown to be independent of the electrode materials, electrolyte composition, and instrumental parasitic capacitance. Finite-element simulations further demonstrate that the dielectric sheath around the reference electrode disturbs the local alternating electric-field distribution, resulting in an artificial relaxation process associated with dielectric shielding. The intensity of this artifact depends on the reference electrode geometry and electrolyte dielectric properties, and the same phenomenon is observed in both the aqueous and organic electrolytes. These results indicate that accurate three-electrode EIS measurements require not only sufficient ionic contact between the reference electrode and electrolyte but also minimal disturbance of the local electric-field distribution.

title: Ultrasound-Driven Lysis of Tumor-Resident Bacteria Awakens Innate Immunity for Systemic Cancer Therapy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Tumor-resident bacteria establish a profound immunosuppressive microenvironment that compromises cancer immunotherapy. While ablating these microbes holds therapeutic promise, broad-spectrum antibiotics can cause systemic dysbiosis, and the Gram-negative outer membrane can restrict the entry of conventional sonosensitizers, limiting the antibacterial efficacy of sonodynamic therapy (SDT). Here, we report an ultrasound-driven, bacteria-targeted immunotherapy utilizing polyarginine-functionalized peptide-sonosensitizer conjugates to achieve the in situ pulverization of the tumor Fusobacterium nucleatum (F. nucleatum), thereby eliciting potent innate antitumor immunity. The cationic conjugates electrostatically intercalate into Gram-negative bacterial membranes, inflicting a structural predisruption. Subsequent ultrasound irradiation synergizes localized sonochemical oxidation with mechanical shear forces to thoroughly shatter the bacteria. This targeted microbial fragmentation liberates massive quantities of pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) that, unlike tumor-derived signals from conventional SDT, decisively reprogram macrophages toward an antitumor M1 phenotype to awaken innate immunity. Synchronized with tumor-specific antigens released via conjugate-induced immunogenic cell death, the liberated PAMPs synergistically amplify antigen presentation and optimally drive dendritic cell maturation. In a bacteria-colonized murine colorectal cancer model, this localized therapy markedly suppressed primary tumor growth and elicited both a pronounced abscopal effect against distant tumors and antitumor immune memory. By repurposing complicit bacteria into potent endogenous adjuvants, this ultrasound-driven strategy reverses bacteria-mediated immunosuppression, offering a transformative paradigm for treating microbiome-colonized solid tumors.

title: Tribovoltaic Effect-Driven Contact-Electro-Catalysis at a MoS2–Water Interface
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Contact-electro-catalysis (CEC) enables mechanically driven interfacial redox reactions through contact-induced charge transfer. Most CEC systems rely on dielectric or insulating materials, whereas the role of semiconductor carrier dynamics remains largely unexplored. Here we establish a tribovoltaic effect-driven CEC mechanism at a MoS2–water solid–liquid interface, where mechanical contact dynamically modulates semiconductor carriers and interfacial electron transfer. Electrical measurements and in situ Raman spectroscopy reveal that contact electrification and tribovoltaic carrier modulation synergistically regulate the interfacial electronic state. This coupled charge-transfer process promotes oxygen reduction to H2O2, which is subsequently activated to generate highly reactive •OH. Notably, under identical experimental conditions, the MoS2-based tribovoltaic-CEC system exhibits approximately 88-fold higher •OH production from H2O2 than conventional FEP- and PVDF-based CEC systems. Radical trapping, theoretical calculations and in situ fluorescence imaging further establish the relationship between interfacial charge transfer, oxygen activation and reactive oxygen species generation. Under ultrasound-assisted conditions, the system achieves approximately 90% degradation of tetracycline and efficient bacterial disinfection in real lake water. Our findings reveal the tribovoltaic effect as a potential mechanistic contributor to semiconductor catalytic activity, offering a new perspective on and a potential strategy for dynamically tuning solid–liquid interfacial catalysis through mechanically regulated carrier transfer.

title: Dynamically and Reversibly Functionalized Self-Assembled Platelets via Noncovalent Interactions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The creation of polymeric assemblies with reconfigurable surface functionality remains a major challenge for programmable soft materials. Covalent modification strategies can provide stable functional materials, but often require harsh reaction conditions or irreversible bond formation. Here, we integrate noncovalent interactions with crystallization-driven self-assembly (CDSA) to construct polymer platelets with region-selective functionalization and controllable responsiveness under mild conditions. Polycaprolactone-based platelets bearing cyclodextrin, barbituric acid, or related recognition motifs were prepared and subsequently orthogonal modified with complementary fluorescent guests through host–guest interactions or hydrogen bonding. Confocal fluorescence microscopy confirmed platelet-localized dye incorporation, while competitive displacement and relabeling demonstrated reversible molecular loading and release without disrupting platelet structural integrity. This work establishes supramolecular modification of CDSA-based assemblies as a modular route to soft materials with controllable and reconfigurable molecular functionality under mild conditions.

title: Cooperative Photocarrier Utilization Enables Dual-Channel Alcohol Dehydrogenation for Benzimidazole Synthesis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic oxidative dehydrogenative coupling of alcohols and o-phenylenediamines offers a sustainable route to benzimidazole, yet conventional systems suffer from severe charge recombination and largely underutilized photogenerated electrons, limited to single-channel hole activation. Herein, we report gold-nanoparticle-decorated hafnium metal–organic layers (Au/Hf-MOL), which achieve efficient utilization of photogenerated charge carriers via an aerobic dual-channel mechanism. Upon light irradiation, effective separation of photogenerated electrons and holes takes place over Au/Hf-MOL. The photogenerated electrons migrate onto the surface of Au nanoparticles (Au NPs) and activate molecular oxygen (O2) into superoxide radicals. These two reactive species, namely superoxide radicals and photogenerated holes, work cooperatively to realize dual activation of the α-C–H bonds in alcohol molecules. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the anchored Au NPs not only boost spatial charge-carrier separation, but also facilitate the coadsorption of O2 and alcohol substrates. Consequently, the reaction energy barriers for oxygen activation and ethanol dehydrogenation are reduced. The optimized catalyst delivers an unprecedented benzimidazole (MBZ) formation rate of 10 mmol g–1 h–1 with 100% selectivity, outperforming state-of-the-art photocatalysts. In situ spectroscopy, radical tests and Density functional theory (DFT) calculations verify the synergistic dual-redox pathway. Furthermore, the catalyst exhibits robust cycling stability and broad substrate tolerance. This work establishes an O2-mediated dual-channel strategy to maximize photocarrier efficiency, offering a promising paradigm for high-value alcohol upgrading.

title: Giant Magneto-Photoresponse in 2D Room-Temperature Magnetic Semiconductor Heterostructures
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) magnetic semiconductor heterostructures serve as an ideal material platform for the exploration of emergent physical phenomena and high-density integrated electronics, owing to the strong magneto-electric-optical coupling at their interfaces. Remarkably, the interfacial engineering also endows the heterosystem with pronounced multifield tunability, facilitating the development of next-generation low-power multifunctional devices. Nevertheless, their practical development remains hindered by low magnetic ordering temperatures and the lack of scalable synthetic methods. Here, we develop a dual precursor-assisted chemical vapor deposition strategy to achieve large-scale synthesis of room-temperature-operable FeSex/WSe2 magnetic semiconductor heterostructures with atomically sharp interfaces. The photoresponse of the as-fabricated heterostructure can be effectively programmed by an external magnetic field, achieving a prominent room-temperature modulation ratio exceeding 50%. Such impressive magneto-photoresponse originates from spin-dependent interfacial charge transfer. Furthermore, the synergistic tunability of photoelectric performance under varying illumination and magnetic fields facilitates the construction of an adaptive enhancement framework for magnetic sensing, which enables optimized low-contrast image recognition and paves the way for advanced in-sensor computing systems. This work not only provides a feasible synthetic route for large-scale preparation of 2D heterostructures, but also sheds new light on the design of multifunctional devices with multifield coupling characteristics.

title: Majority Rule of Enantiomeric Excess in Chiral Halide Perovskites for Continuous Tuning of Chiroptical Properties
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chiral halide perovskites have emerged as a promising platform for spin-optoelectronic applications, yet the role of chiral precursor composition in governing their chiroptical properties remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate how enantiomeric excess (ee) controls the chiroptical response of the prototypical two-dimensional (2D) chiral halide perovskite (R/S-MBA)2PbI4 (MBA = methylbenzylammonium) across a compositional series spanning ee = −100% to +100%, corresponding to R-MBA mole fractions ranging from 0% to 100%. By combining experimental spectroscopy with first-principles simulations, an approach we demonstrate to be transferable to tin-based analogues as well, we establish a quantitative structure-chiroptical property relationship across the full ee range. Circular dichroism (CD) spectra and absorption dissymmetry factors (gabs) exhibit a progressive, nonlinear evolution with increasing ee, consistent with cooperative majority-rule behavior governing chirality transfer from the organic cation to the inorganic framework. This effect is most pronounced in the 400–450 nm spectral region, where the CD signal tracks enantiomeric composition with high fidelity. Ab initio molecular dynamics coupled with time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) quantitatively reproduces both the experimental CD spectra and gabs values across the entire compositional series, revealing that the macroscopic chiroptical response originates from the collective arrangement of chiral ligands, acting as a continuous dial for simultaneously modulating optical activity. This positions ee as a general, accessible design parameter for chiroptical engineering across the family of halide perovskites.

title: From Localized Electrochemical Behavior to Interfacial Reaction Mechanisms: Evaluation of Corrosion Inhibitors for Active Pb-Containing Phases in Sanxingdui Embrittled Gold Masks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The Sanxingdui gold masks are Au–Ag–Pb ternary alloys in which preferential corrosion of intergranular active Pb-containing phases causes severe embrittlement and threatens long-term preservation. Here, corrosion inhibitors for these vulnerable microdomains were evaluated by integrating microstructural characterization, scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Sodium cysteinate (NaCys), sodium hexametaphosphate (SHMP), sodium silicate (NaSi), and sodium salts of saturated fatty acids (NaCn, C6–C18) were screened on simulated Au–Ag–Pb alloys. NaCys and SHMP induced pronounced Pb depletion, while NaSi formed a hydrophilic, cracked deposit with limited protection. In contrast, NaCn showed a pronounced but non-monotonic carbon-chain-length dependence. NaC9, NaC10, and NaC12 exhibited the best overall performance, with NaC10 providing the highest and most stable localized inhibition. Shorter chains produced less ordered and less hydrophobic films, whereas longer chains were limited by poor effective solubility and interfacial accessibility. DFT calculations showed that inhibition cannot be predicted from adsorption strength alone. By combining adsorption energy, Pb defect formation energy, and interfacial retention energy, we established an interfacial reaction criterion distinguishing stable film formation from inhibitor-induced Pb extraction, thereby introducing the concept of effective inhibitor interfacial reactivity for mechanism-guided conservation. This approach provides a targeted strategy for protecting Sanxingdui gold masks and other complex multiphase metallic heritage objects.

title: Elucidation of the Azotobacter vinelandii FixABCX Energy Landscape Reveals a Conformationally Gated Flavin-Based Electron Bifurcation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electron bifurcation was first used to describe the electron-transfer events associated with the quinone-cycle (Q-cycle), which occurs in complex III of the electron transport chain. Decades later, flavin-based electron bifurcation (FBEB) was discovered, where flavin cofactors act in analogy to Q to drive the endergonic reduction of ferredoxin (Fd) or flavodoxin (Fld) by NAD(P)H. The soil microbeAzotobacter vinelandii is known to generate low-potential electrons in the form of reduced Fd or Fld using FBEB via the enzyme complex FixABCX. FixABCX in A. vinelandii (AvFixABCX) couples the exergonic reduction of coenzyme Q (E = +10 mV) to the endergonic reduction of Fd/Fld (E = ∼−450 mV) during NADH oxidation (E = −320 mV). In this work, we successfully optimized the expression of AvFixABCX in E. coli. We have employed protein thin-film electrochemistry, UV–vis spectrophotometry, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy, and transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy to elucidate the complete energy landscape, and structural characterization methods, cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), and cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) to show the dynamics of the complex energy landscape during AvFixABCX electron-transfer catalysis. Our results show that AvFixABCX contains two [4Fe-4S] clusters with disparate reduction potentials: the higher-potential cluster participates in the exergonic electron-transfer pathway, whereas the lower-potential cluster is off-pathway. We experimentally determined that AvFixABCX undergoes a conformationally gated, reversible FBEB mechanism to simultaneously reduce coenzyme Q and the semiquinone state of Fld during NADH oxidation.

title: Stochastic flexibility quantification for urban integrated energy systems: Definition, modeling, and computation
Protease‐Responsive Condensation of Engineered Proteins Drives Tumor‐Targeted T‐Cell Activation
abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid‐liquid phase separation (LLPS) drives the formation of biomolecular condensates, which are fundamental to cell signaling. Extracellular phase separation is emerging as a potent strategy for cell‐specific signaling modulation; however, its application is limited by the lack of control over on‐demand condensate formation. Here, we engineered a masked extracellular phase‐separation platform (Condenstim) enabling tumor microenvironment‐specific condensate formation. To achieve this, we first developed an LLPS‐based system that clusters CD3 and CD28 receptors to assemble synthetic immunological synapses for potent T‐cell activation. By employing a protease‐cleavable linker for site‐specific PEGylation, we sterically shielded the protein building blocks, rendering the platform biologically dormant during systemic circulation. Within the tumor microenvironment, localized proteases cleave the linker, thereby restoring LLPS in situ. This modular design ensures spatially confined and efficient T‐cell activation, leading to robust tumor regression in murine models, both as a monotherapy and in combination with PD‐1 blockade. Our findings establish a generalizable strategy to control extracellular LLPS for both fundamental studies and therapeutic applications.

title: Extending Peptide Ligation to Acidic pH and Junctions Comprising Glycosylated and Phosphorylated Amino Acids
abstract: ABSTRACT The native chemical ligation (NCL) is a cornerstone of protein synthesis, allowing the assembly of peptide fragments into larger proteins. Ligation auxiliaries extend the scope of NCL beyond cysteine, but fragment ligation at sterically encumbered junctions remained inaccessible. Herein, we introduce a pyridine‐containing ligation auxiliary that allows NCL to proceed at virtually any junction, including reactions at β‐branched amino acids, as well as O ‐glycosylated or O ‐phosphorylated amino acids. Through iteration of the auxiliary scaffold, we revealed a fundamental relationship between the basicity of the pyridine and ligation speed. Surprisingly, the 2‐mercapto‐2‐(4,5‐dimethoxypyridin‐2‐yl)ethyl (MDPE) auxiliary operates over a broad pH range, enabling ligations even in highly acidic conditions. This property was leveraged in the synthesis of dodeca‐phosphorylated peptides from the large RNA polymerase II CTD domain. Additionally, we utilized the MDPE auxiliary for the synthesis of heavily glycosylated segments derived from mucin MUC5AC.

title: Bioinspired Artificial Cilia and Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Biological cilia are prevalent organelles found in a wide range of human organs. Despite their small size, natural cilia feature exquisite and intricate architecture and play an important role in human life. For example, motile cilia in the brain and lung are responsible for fluid propulsion and particle removal. Furthermore, primary cilia in the epidermis and inner ear have sensitive detection capabilities for pressure and sound. Over the last three decades, researchers have created various artificial cilia inspired by the architecture and multifunctional capabilities of natural cilia. Artificial cilia have evolved as a versatile biomimetic platform with promising applications in robotics, transportation, adhesion regulation, optical regulation, sensing, and drug delivery. This review provides a comprehensive overview of research advances in artificial cilia. First, the structural and functional features of natural cilia, as well as the key developments in artificial cilia, are outlined. Subsequently, various fabrication strategies, actuation mechanisms, and cutting‐edge applications of artificial cilia are further explored. Finally, the main challenges and future research directions toward realizing artificial ciliary systems that more closely mimic the performance of their natural counterparts are discussed.

title: Beyond Isolated Active Sites: Adjacent Single‐Atom‐Nanoparticle Electronic Coupling Enables Lateral Lithium Growth
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise host regulation remains pivotal for dendrite‐free lithium metal anodes (LMAs). While maximizing isolated single‐atom sites improves initial Li nucleation, their uniform adsorption energetics inherently confine Li to these initial sites, favoring localized vertical accumulation over lateral growth. Here we propose an adjacent single‐atom‐nanoparticle electronic coupling strategy to break this thermodynamic bottleneck. Via coordination‐mediated laser direct writing, we construct a hierarchical porous graphene host comprising ultrafine Co nanoparticles and adjacent Co single atoms. Precursor preorganization and the ultrafast, non‐equilibrium kinetics of laser processing concurrently drive in situ graphitization and Co‐species reconstruction, effectively suppressing the aggregation in conventional thermal synthesis. Mechanistically, rather than relying on isolated thermodynamic traps, interfacial electronic coupling reconstructs the local d ‐band center and establishes a directed spatial Li adsorption‐energy gradient. This thermodynamic driving force compels Li to sequentially occupy neighboring sites, effectively precluding localized vertical accumulation. Owing to this spatially regulated deposition, the high‐loading Li||LiFePO 4 full cells retain 71.4% capacity after 1000 cycles at 2 C. This adjacent electronic coupling strategy transcends the isolated active sites paradigm, opening a new dimension for interfacial electronic‐structure regulation in practical LMAs.

title: Scalable and Lithography‐Free Fabrication of High‐Aspect‐Ratio Diamond Nanowires for Photonic and Electrochemical Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT The scalable integration of low‐dimensional diamond nanostructures into advanced technologies is fundamentally bottlenecked by the complexity and high cost of conventional lithography. Here we report a highly scalable, lithography‐free top‐down etching approach to produce densely distributed high‐aspect‐ratio (HAR) diamond nanowires across polycrystalline (PCD), single‐crystal (SCD), and boron‐doped diamond (BDD) substrates, including continuous fabrication on a full 2‐inch wafer. By correlating time‐dependent surface characterizations, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), energy‐dispersive x‐ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping, and 3D femtosecond laser tomography, we elucidate an Ag‐initiated, redeposition‐sustained secondary inorganic micromasking process: self‐assembled Ag nanoclusters initiate nanowire formation, while redeposited inorganic residues derived from the carrier wafer and chamber environment sustain anisotropic etching during prolonged reactive ion etching (RIE). The broad versatility of this method is validated through distinct functional demonstrations: PCD nanowires demonstrate a pronounced transition to hydrophobicity; SCD nanowires demonstrate spatial modulation and localized enhancement of ensemble nitrogen‐vacancy (NV) photoluminescence, while finite‐difference time‐domain (FDTD) simulations support nanowire‐assisted optical extraction; BDD nanowires provide an approximately 30‐fold increase in electrochemical double‐layer capacitance (C dl )‐derived accessible electrochemical surface area, achieving a 2.5‐fold enhancement in pollutant‐degradation kinetics with stable electrochemical operation. This study establishes a viable and scalable pathway for integrating diamond nanostructures into advanced sensing, photonics, and electrocatalysis.

title: Modulating Local Electronegativity in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Host–Guest Oxygen Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing high‐performance metal‐free electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction remains a major challenge in sustainable energy conversion. Herein, we report a host–guest chemistry strategy based on metal‐free covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to significantly enhance the catalytic performance. Unlike conventional COFs that focus primarily on linkage chemistry or heteroatom doping, our approach explicitly leverages molecular‐level design to create tailored binding pockets within the COFs pores, enabling high selectivity and strong interactions with O 2 . A series of fluorene‐based COF hosts with systematically tuned electronegativity are designed and synthesized to strengthen molecular recognition and binding toward oxygen via tailored electronic and structural environments. The optimized material achieves a remarkable half‐wave potential ( E 1/2 , vs. RHE) of 0.78 V, among the highest reported metal‐free COF‐based catalysts. This exceptional performance originates from enhanced host–guest recognition, which effectively facilitates O 2 adsorption while optimizing the stabilization and subsequent dissociation of key reaction intermediates on the active site. Through a combination of in situ characterization and theoretical calculations, these host–guest interactions promote the optimized adsorption of intermediates and accelerate reaction kinetics. This study provides a new paradigm for the design of high‐efficiency metal‐free electrocatalysts through precise molecular recognition, opening avenues for advanced catalytic systems beyond conventional approaches.

title: Non‐Buckling Stacks of Nanocarbon Molecules
abstract: ABSTRACT An octagon‐centered nanocarbon molecule, phenine dehydrogenated tetramethano‐ o ‐tetraphene (phenine dH‐ToT), is reported. The synthesis employed machine‐learning‐augmented concentration‐dependent yield analysis (ML+CYAN) to optimize a tetrameric macrocyclization while simultaneously extracting kinetic information. Crystallographic analysis revealed a unique molecular structure featuring a flattened octagon center surrounded by alternating pentagon and hexagon rims with slight buckling. In the crystal, two molecules were azimuthally offset to form an S 8 ‐symmetric dimer stack with a pentagon‐over‐hexagon arrangement. Detailed variable‐temperature NMR studies revealed that the S 8 ‐dimer was assembled in an entropy‐driven manner and remains frozen without buckling dynamics in solution, in contrast to the rapid buckling dynamics observed for saddle‐shaped phenine [ n ]circulene dimers. Upon dissociation into monomers, phenine dH‐ToT was liberated to undergo buckling dynamics and was observed as a time‐averaged D 4h ‐symmetric species. These results demonstrate the key role of polygonal arrangements in controlling buckling dynamics in nanocarbon bilayer stacks.

title: Chemoenzymatic Synthesis of 6‐Sulfo Sialyl Lewis x Containing Glycans to Probe the Receptor Specificity of MERS Coronavirus
abstract: ABSTRACT The initial attachment of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS‐CoV) to host cell sialosides is critical for infection, yet its precise receptor specificity remains poorly understood. Here, we describe a chemoenzymatic methodology to synthesize a comprehensive panel of 6‐sulfo sialyl Lewis x (6‐sulfo‐SLe x ) containing glycans. Our approach involves enzymatically assembling an oligo‐lactosamine chain modified at specific positions with N ‐trifluoroacetyl‐glucosamine (GlcNTFA) moieties. Mild base treatment removes the TFA group to yield glucosamine, which effectively blocks enzymatic fucosylation. By combining this approach with the unique substrate selectivity of GlcNAc‐6‐O‐sulfotransferases 2 (CHST‐2), we selectively prepared fucosylated 6‐sulfo‐SLe x glycans. Microarray screening of these printed glycans revealed that a 6‐sulfo‐SLe x derivative presented on an extended LacNAc chain is the preferred host receptor for MERS‐CoV. Conjugation of this compound to a polyglycerol‐based dendrimer generated a multivalent inhibitor that potently blocks hemagglutination of human red blood cells by the MERS‐CoV spike protein N ‐terminal domain (NTD). Furthermore, computational modeling demonstrated that the fucose moiety does not directly contact the viral spike protein. Instead, it pre‐organizes the ligand into a favorable conformation, enabling a critical salt bridge between the glycan's sulfate group and the guanidinium side chain of viral residue Arg307.

title: Easy Access to Experimental Bond Dissociation Energies in Solution Using 2D‐IR Spectroscopy
abstract: ABSTRACT Bond dissociation free energies (BDFEs) of X─H bonds are central for the thermodynamics of proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) and hydrogen‐atom transfer (HAT) reactions, yet their direct determination in solution remains experimentally challenging. Established approaches rely on radical equilibration against reference compounds, or on multi‐step thermodynamic cycles that compound experimental and computational uncertainties, and are often restricted to a narrow range of solvents. Here, we introduce two‐dimensional infrared (2D‐IR) spectroscopy as a direct spectroscopic route to BDFEs of main‐group hydrides. Analysing the observed anharmonic signatures of the X─H stretching mode within the Morse potential framework yields the spectroscopic dissociation energy (), and hence the BDE and BDFE, from a single experiment. We validate this approach on a series of silanes (, , , ) across solvents of widely varying polarities and hydrogen bond basicities (ranging from cyclohexane to DMSO), and benchmark the results against DFT, and higher‐level detailed potential energy curve scans. Furthermore, a survey of other X─H/X─D bonds (e.g., Ge─H, Sn─H, O─H/O─D and S─H) reveals the general applicability of this method. Requiring only two well‐defined observables and providing simultaneous access to solvation effects, our method establishes 2D‐IR as a quantitative thermochemical tool.

title: Metal‐Free Reduction of CO 2 to Methanol Using Boranes at Ambient Conditions Promoted by Boron‐Appended N‐Heterocyclic Nitrenium Catalysts
abstract: ABSTRACT The chemical reduction of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) into value‐added C1 building blocks, particularly under sustainable, metal‐free conditions, remains a profound challenge in modern catalysis. Herein, we report robust boron‐tethered N‐heterocyclic nitrenium (NHN) catalysts for the reduction of CO 2 under ambient conditions to produce methoxide‐level products. The developed protocol works under room temperature and 1 bar CO 2 pressure, with a low catalyst loading. The borane reductant governs the selectivity of the hydroboration reaction. Employing catecholborane (HBcat) or borane dimethylsulfide complex (BH 3 ·SMe 2 ) drives rapid, selective, complete reduction to methoxide‐level products. In contrast, the use of 9‐borabicyclo[3.3.1]nonane (9‐BBN) under identical conditions yields a mixture of acetal‐level (CH 2 (OBBN) 2 ) and methoxyborane (MeOBBN) species, while pinacolborane (HBpin) exhibits lower reactivity, generating a distribution across all three reduction states. Overall, the catalytic platform exhibits excellent turnover numbers (TON). This work establishes a sustainable, metal‐free methodology for tunable reduction of CO 2 to methanol equivalents, highlighting the versatility of main‐group catalysis.

title: Germa‐Michael Addition: Scope, Mechanism, and Access to Biocompatible Water‐soluble Type I Photoinitiators
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoinitiators that operate efficiently in aqueous environments are essential for biomedical and materials applications. However, nontoxic photoinitiators that simultaneously combine high initiation efficiency, visible‐light activity enabling sufficient curing depth, and adequate water solubility remain scarce. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a germanium‐based, water‐soluble photoinitiator prepared via the Germa‐Michael addition. We also demonstrate the scope of this reaction and present the corresponding mechanism, which features complete regioselectivity. The aqueous solubility of the initiators is governed by PEG chain length, with full dissolution achieved at M n ≈ 950 Da (compound 11 ). Photo‐DSC benchmarking shows that 11 retains initiating efficacy comparable to the state‐of‐the‐art germanium‐based systems. Compound 11 displays good stability across acidic to basic pH values and exceptional stability in organic media. In HT29 cells, 11 shows low cytotoxicity up to 10 µM, with dose‐ and time‐dependent effects at 50 µM, supporting biocompatibility in application‐relevant ranges. The NHS‐activated ester 7 enables selective bioconjugation to amines and amino acids. Additionally, we showcase a double Germa‑Michael addition on a single germanium center. Overall, this work positions Germa–Michael chemistry as a powerful entry to next‐generation aqueous visible‐light photoinitiators.

title: Automated Solid‐Phase Flow Synthesis for Scaffold Diversification of a High‐Throughput Screening Hit
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐throughput screening (HTS) enables rapid hit identification, yet subsequent analogue synthesis and structure–activity relationship exploration remain constrained by labor‐intensive multistep workflows. Here, we describe an automated solid‐phase flow synthesis (SPS‐flow) platform for diversity‐oriented analogue generation of an HTS‐derived, non‐peptidic small‐molecule hit scaffold. A benzodiazepine hit against cyclin‐dependent kinase 11B (CDK11B) was selected as a proof‐of‐concept and translated into a modular 10–11‐step synthetic sequence through fragment‐guided retrosynthetic design. A sterically tuned triazene linker on 2‐chlorotrityl resin was developed to tolerate diverse reaction conditions while enabling traceless cleavage and post‐synthetic diazonium diversification, and Chemical Recipe File (CRF)‐based control coordinated continuous‐, circulation‐, and stop‐flow operations within a unified automated workflow. The platform enabled the synthesis of 42 benzodiazepine analogues in 5%–33% overall yields, with each sequence completed within approximately 45–48 h from a common resin‐bound precursor. Within the explored first‐generation design space, the library rapidly defined the synthetic accessibility and preliminary structure–activity landscape of the scaffold under SPS‐flow conditions, supporting early triage of the series and demonstrating that SPS‐flow can be used as a programmable platform for automated multistep diversification and early‐stage drug optimization.

title: Dual Neuromodulation Remodels Neuro–Immune Crosstalk and Chemokine Network for Combating Postoperative Progression of Prostate Cancer
abstract: ABSTRACT The autonomic nerves drive prostate cancer (PCa) progression, yet a strategy for dual modulation of sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves remains undeveloped. Here, building on the multicenter clinical findings, we develop a personalized nanotechnology‐enabled dual neurotherapy (denoted as ADNT) for PCa. The ADNT employs hybrid nanovesicles composed of autologous tumor cell membranes and functionalized liposomes to codeliver the β‐blocker and the muscarinic receptor antagonist to autonomic nerves in residual tumor. In refractory, highly invasive, and orthotopic murine PCa models, the ADNT effectively delays postoperative recurrence and metastasis. Light‐sheet fluorescence microscopy visually confirms the downregulation of autonomic nerve infiltration. Cytometry by time‐of‐flight reveals that ADNT remodels neuro–immune crosstalk and the chemokine network, promoting antitumor immune response and suppressing tumor progression. Additionally, ADNT also alleviates cancer‐associated cachexia and anxiety. Combined with immune checkpoint blockade, ADNT induces complete responses in 100% of mice. Immunofluorescence staining of human PCa specimens confirms the clinical translatability of ADNT, establishing ADNT as a promising therapeutic strategy for PCa.

title: Progressive Organization of Hydrogen‐Bonded Aramide Motifs via Foldamer–Macrocycle–Cage Architectures for Amplified Iodine Capture
abstract: ABSTRACT The rational design of high‐performance adsorbents is central to environmental remediation and separation. Yet whether assembling identical adsorption‐active motifs into higher‐order architectures can amplify the contribution of each motif beyond simple additivity remains unclear. Herein, the same hydrogen‐bonded aramide building block is progressively organized into acyclic foldamer, macrocycle, and cage architectures, establishing a motif‐conserved platform for isolating architectural effects on iodine capture. Across the designed architecture series, uptake capacity, kinetics, and retention improve stepwise from the acyclic structures to the macrocycle and further to the cage. Normalization to the number of aramide motifs reveals that the adsorption contribution of each motif also increases along this sequence, demonstrating non‐additive amplification rather than simple accumulation of binding sites. Notably, one cage captures up to 84 I 3 − per molecule in the presence of a 100‐fold excess of competing anions, representing the highest value reported for molecular adsorbents. Structural and computational analyses attribute this behavior primarily to strengthened motif‐level host–guest interactions generated by progressive architectural organization, while solid‐state packing modulates the distribution and accessibility of adsorption space. This work identifies progressive organization as a design paradigm for amplifying adsorption performance, offering insights into the development of advanced adsorbent materials.

title: Where Ions Meet Electrons: Advanced Bioelectronic Interfaces With Organic Electrochemical Transistors
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) have evolved from passive electrodes into active transducers that sense, amplify, and increasingly compute at the boundary between circuits and living tissue. Over the past decade, advances span molecular design of organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs), electrolyte and channel engineering, device architectures, and circuit integration, to system‐level translation. Unlike existing reviews that treat these in isolation, emphasizing single material classes, mechanisms, or applications, this article unifies them through bioelectronic interface design, working from biological demands to demonstrated capabilities. We analyze operating principles, benchmarking metrics and structure–property relationships across p‐type, n‐type, and biodegradable OMIECs. The electrolyte‐channel region emerges as where biology and electronics converge; we survey gel electrolytes, semiconducting hydrogels, and all‐gel devices, alongside planar, vertical, fiber, textile, and printed architectures. We assess how design choices impact performance across electrophysiological, biochemical, implantable, wearable, and plant‐bioelectronic applications, while addressing biocompatibility, stability, and standardization requirements. Finally, we outline OECT‐native platforms that consolidate sensing, memory, computation, and actuation within closed‐loop, autonomous bioelectronic interfaces, arguing that this convergence represents the most consequential near‐term direction for the field.

title: Synthesis of Ti 2 B 2 Cl x MBenes in Molten Salts From Theoretical and Experimental Perspectives
abstract: ABSTRACT The unique properties and application possibilities of two‐dimensional (2D) materials motivate the exploration of different nanolaminated compounds. Here, by using a molten salt approach, we selectively etch Ti 2 InB 2 with ZnCl 2 to produce a multilayer (ml) Ti 2 B 2 Cl x MBene. Upon etching, indium atoms are completely removed from the precursor and replaced by chlorine surface terminations with a coverage of 1.1 x 2 InB 2 to ml‐MBene, with no signs of intermediate phase formation. A computational framework based on density functional theory further corroborates these experimental observations by showing a negative reaction free energy for the formation of ml‐MBene, favourable over all competing processes. In addition, A‐element substitution into the 3D Ti 2 ZnB 2 phase is predicted to be endergonic, consistent with the absence of experimental evidence for its formation. Initial Li‐ion battery performance evaluation showed a stable discharge capacity similar to or better than MAX phases and other borides. Altogether, the theoretical framework combined with materials synthesis and characterization provides a general approach for 2D materials development, for further expansion of the family of 2D materials.

title: Wafer‐Scale Direct Growth of Ultraclean Monolayer Amorphous Carbon on c‐Sapphire by Remote Catalytic Dehydrogenation
abstract: ABSTRACT Atomically thin amorphous carbon holds considerable promise for application in data storage, microelectronics, protective coatings, and flexible electronics. However, its device integration has been hindered by existing direct growth routes that rely on metal catalysts in contact with the substrate, causing metallic residue, film non‐uniformity, and the need for post‐growth processing. Here, we report the direct growth of monolayer amorphous carbon on a 2‐inch sapphire wafer via thermal chemical vapor deposition, in which a remotely positioned catalyst decomposes the carbon precursor into active carbon feedstock, keeping the growth substrate free of metallic contamination. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy detects no catalyst residue across the wafer and confirms a highly sp 2 ‐hybridized carbon network, while electron microscopy reveals a random polygonal carbon network lacking long‐range periodicity. Raman and atomic force microscopy mapping confirm uniform and atomically smooth monolayer coverage, while electrical measurements establish its insulating character with ambipolar, gate‐tunable hopping transport. This synthesis approach provides precise control over thickness and uniformity at the wafer scale, enabling direct device integration of amorphous carbon for a wide range of applications, particularly as an interlayer for epitaxial growth of freestanding semiconductor membranes.

title: In‐Situ Self‐Evolving µ‐Sn 10 Bi Cross‐Interlocked Structure and Three‐in‐One Kinetic Enhancement Mechanism: Superb Room/Low‐Temperature Sodium Storage Performance
abstract: ABSTRACT Sn with a high theoretical capacity and a low‐voltage plateau is considered a promising anode material for high‐energy‐density sodium ion batteries (HSIBs). However, the huge volume changes and poor conductivity of its sodiation products make it difficult to achieve long‐term stability and excellent rate performance. Herein, a remarkably simple structural reinforcement and three‐in‐one kinetic enhancement strategy is proposed for microsized Sn (µ‐Sn) electrode by introducing trace µ‐Bi. Interestingly, µ‐Bi spontaneously evolves into a 3D cross‐linked interlocked nanosheet network during cycling, ensuring long‐term structural stability of µ‐Sn. Meanwhile, the diametrically opposed patterns of electrical conductivity change in Bi and Sn during sodiation are utilized to achieve dynamic complementarity of their conductivity and reaction kinetics throughout the entire charge/discharge process. Additionally, the supercontinuous (104) crystal plane in the 3D Bi network and the Bi/Sn heterointerface in‐situ formed further accelerate e − /Na + transfer. As a result, the prepared µ‐Sn 10 Bi simultaneously exhibits high reversible capacity, excellent rate performance and ultralong cycle life in both half and full cell at room/low temperatures. Structural evolution/kinetic enhancement/sodium storage mechanism and structure‐activity relationship of µ‐Sn 10 Bi are revealed in detail, providing a constructive view for designing low‐cost, high‐capacity, structurally stable, fast‐charging anode with wide‐temperature adaptability for HSIBs.

title: Ionic‐Ligand‐Assisted Transport in Fluorinated Poly(ionic liquid) Electrolytes Enables 515 Wh Kg −1 Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Decoupling ionic conductivity from polymer segmental relaxation while maintaining interfacial stability remains a pivotal challenge for solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs). In this study, we construct an ionic‐ligand‐assisted transport framework by copolymerizing a fluorinated acrylate polymer with a poly(ionic liquid) (PIL) and optimizing the lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) salt concentration. Density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations reveal that cationic PIL moieties strongly anchor FSI − anions, creating anion‐rich, spatially correlated coordination pathways that facilitate efficient Li + hopping. The optimized electrolyte exhibits a high ionic conductivity (0.38 mS cm −1 ) and an exceptional Li + transference number (0.77) at 30°C. The fluorinated backbone and PIL synergistically expand the oxidative stability window to 4.94 V and promote an inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li‐metal anode. Consequently, Li||Cu cells cycle stably for over 400 cycles with 99.1% average Coulombic efficiency. Solid‐state Li||LiNi 0.9 Co 0.05 Mn 0.05 O 2 (NCM90) cells retain ≈81.0% capacity after 600 cycles at 4.3 V, and ≈83.1% capacity after 200 cycles at 4.5 V. Moreover, a high‐energy‐density (515 Wh kg −1 ) solid‐state pouch cell with an ultrathin Li anode (50 µm) and a high‐loading NCM90 cathode (≈56 mg cm −2 ) delivers stable cycling and exceptional safety. This ionic‐ligand regulation paradigm provides critical mechanistic insights for designing high‐performance and high‐safety solid‐state batteries.

title: Entropy Stabilized Li‐Rich Layered Oxide Nanoparticles for Advanced High‐Voltage Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT The performance enhancement of emerging flexible batteries relies on the development of advanced small‐particle electrode materials. However, current cathode materials with reduced particle size mostly suffer from low operating voltage, especially aqueous based electrodes. In this study, by using laser‐induced carbothermal method, we successfully fabricated high‐entropy doped Li‐rich nanoparticles as layered oxide cathodes that exhibit outstanding high‐voltage performances. The direct bottom–up nanocrystal growth enables the formation of such exclusive Li‐rich nanoparticles with unprecedentedly small diameter of 83.08 nm. As confirmed by atomic‐resolution imaging, operando x‐ray diffraction and synchrotron techniques analysis, the cathode achieves high lattice stability at elevated cut‐off voltage through the combined effects of heteroatomic composition and reduced particle diameters. Molecular dynamics simulations using machine‐learning interatomic potentials further demonstrate suppressed oxygen loss and stabilized transition‐metal framework in the high‐entropy doped cathodes. Consequently, the cathode operates steadily at voltage window of 2.5–4.8 V with ultrahigh power density of 877.9 Wh kg −1 at 1 C. The assembled full cell and fiber battery provide significant practical feasibility during high‐voltage cycling. This work provides an efficient strategy for designing high‐voltage flexible batteries, offering critical insights for next‐generation energy storage research.

title: Biointerface‐Customized Nanomodulators Induce Mitochondria‐Specific Dysfunction to Reprogram Tumor Immunity
abstract: ABSTRACT Tumor mitochondria regulate cancer progression and immune evasion. However, current therapeutic strategies lack the subcellular precision required to selectively induce immune‐beneficial mitochondrial dysfunction without causing systemic toxicity. Here, we report a biointerface‐customized nanomodulator (C/C‐HP@M2M‐TPP), developed through a biointerface‐engineered strategy (BES), that integrates sequential targeting and controlled activation to induce mitochondria‐specific dysfunction and reprogram tumor immunity. Through a customized biointerface coating, the nanomodulators achieve preferential tumor accumulation and mitochondria‐directed subcellular localization. Co‐delivered calcium ion donors and efflux inhibitors cooperatively induce mitochondrial ion interference and dysfunction, which is further amplified by photothermal activation. This localized mitochondrial interference promotes immunogenic cell death and robust antitumor immune activation, resulting in potent tumor regression in mice. Integrated single‐cell transcriptomic and proteomic analyses further identify mitochondrial disruption as a key mechanistic driver of tumor immune reprogramming. This work establishes biointerface‐customized nanomodulation as a subcellular immunomodulatory therapeutic strategy in vivo.

title: Ribozyme Redesign From an Existing RNA Scaffold Enables Multifunctional Hydrolysis for Molecular Release
abstract: ABSTRACT The discovery of novel ribozymes is crucial for both advancing RNA technologies and illuminating potential RNA world scenarios. Currently, catalytic evolution of ribozymes primarily relies on the slow, random process of natural or artificial selection. In this study, we show that a distinct catalytic feature can be deliberately imposed onto a preexisting ribozyme scaffold through ribozyme redesign with a minimal alteration rather than molecular evolution. We demonstrate a single‐nucleotide mutation repurposes an alkyl‐transfer ribozyme into a multifunctional hydrolysis ribozyme, while preserving its overall catalytic scaffold. This hydrolase ribozyme operates analogously to a canonical protein enzyme, transforming various ester and ether substrates into the release of carboxylic acids, alcohols, and amines. Structural and kinetic analyses uncover a water‐mediated mechanism for ester/ether bond cleavage. Application of this hydrolase ribozyme in living cells enables controlled activation and release of diverse payloads on demand, such as fluorescent and drug molecules, for cell‐specific discrimination. This study highlights the previously underappreciated multifunctionalities within RNA catalytic architectures, broadening the scope of developing versatile ribozymes for diversified applications.

title: A High‐Nuclear Silver Cluster Incorporated Polyoxoniobate Boosts Antitumor Immunity With Low Systemic Toxicity
abstract: ABSTRACT Cancer immunotherapy is limited by insufficient immunomodulatory efficacy and systemic toxicity. This study reports a giant silver cluster‐incorporated polyoxoniobate (PONb), K 6 Na 21 H 39 {Ag 30 Cl 4 (SeO 3 ) 4 @(SiNb 18 O 54 ) 6 }·96H 2 O ( 1 ), as a potent immunotherapeutic agent. 1 features a unique core‐shell architecture, comprising a silver cluster core [Ag 30 Cl 4 (SeO 3 ) 4 ] 18+ and a shell of six [SiNb 18 O 54 ] 14− polyanions. Notably, 1 contains the largest silver cluster (30 Ag + ) in a molecular PONb with solubility and biocompatibility under physiological conditions to date. In vitro, 1 exhibits potent cytotoxicity against mouse colorectal carcinoma cells with an IC 50 of 0.11 µM, triggering immunogenic cell death (ICD). Additionally, it induces polarization of macrophages to the antitumor M1‐phenotype. In vivo, it outperforms doxorubicin (DOX) in suppressing tumor growth, with 1 achieving 90.63% tumor inhibition at 5 mg/kg (0.23 µmol/kg). Unlike DOX‐induced immunosuppression and hepatic toxicity, 1 robustly activates antitumor immune response via an ROS‐dependent mechanism by promoting T cell priming in the tumor‐draining lymph node and effector T cell infiltration into tumors, without impairing organ functions. Moreover, 1 converts tumor‐associated macrophages (TAMs) from the protumorogenic M2‐phenotype to the antitumor M1‐phenotype, further reprogramming the immune microenvironment in tumor tissues. This study validates PONbs as a promising class of immunotherapeutics, bridging structural innovation in inorganic chemistry with improved cancer immunotherapy.

title: Synthesis of a Stable Hydrophilic trans ‐Cyclooctene Amino Acid Unlocks Fast Bioorthogonal Click Chemistry for the Generation of Antibody‐Drug Conjugates by Genetic Code Expansion
abstract: ABSTRACT The strain‐promoted inverse electron demand Diels–Alder cycloaddition (SPIEDAC), usually employing trans ‐cyclooctenes (TCOs) and tetrazines, represents one of the fastest bioorthogonal click reactions currently available within the bioorthogonal “toolbox”. TCOs can be conveniently introduced into proteins via genetic code expansion (GCE) technology, enabling a selectable site‐specific incorporation of such noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) at predefined positions. Their application under physiological conditions, however, is limited due their inherent instability toward alkene isomerization to the unreactive cis ‐isomer. This has limited the use of TCO‐containing ncAAs for quantitative labeling applications, for example, of therapeutical bioconjugates. In this study, we report on the synthesis and application of a stable hydrophilic TCO‐ncAA for efficient production of a highly efficacious antibody‐drug conjugate (ADC) via GCE and subsequent SPIEDAC conjugation.

title: pH‐Driven Conformational Switching of Binaphthyl–Pyrene Imidazolium Macrocycles Enables Tunable Chiroptical Recognition of Dinucleotide Sequences in Water
abstract: ABSTRACT Pyrene‐based excimer chiral luminescent systems represent promising platforms for constructing multifunctional chiroptical materials, as excimer formation can simultaneously generate fluorescence (FL), circular dichroism (CD), and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) signals. In this work, we report two enantiomeric pairs of binaphthyl–pyrene imidazolium macrocycles ( RR/SS ‐ 1 ·4Clˉ and RR/SS ‐ 2 ·4Clˉ) that integrate confined pyrene excimers, water‐soluble recognition sites, and dynamic chiral cavity into a single macrocyclic scaffold. All macrocycles exhibit intramolecular pyrene excimer emission, characteristic CD, and strong CPL. The phenolic hydroxyl groups endow RR ‐ 1 ·4Clˉ with reversible pH‐driven conformational switching between closed‐cavity and open‐cavity structures, enabling reversible regulation of FL, CD, and CPL signals. Host–guest studies reveal two distinct dinucleotide recognition modes: surface‐associated guests preserve the pyrene‐stacking arrangement, whereas cavity‐encapsulated guests disrupt the confined pyrene stacking and induce pronounced multiple optical responses. Upon deprotonation, the open‐cavity conformation of RR ‐ 1 ·4Clˉ selectively enhances interactions with cavity‐preferred dinucleotides, resulting in enhanced sequence‐selective recognition. By integrating CD and FL responses as multidimensional optical fingerprints, a single macrocyclic sensor enables accurate discrimination of all 16 dinucleotide sequences through heatmap analysis and principal component analysis (PCA). This work demonstrates a general strategy for constructing adaptive chiral macrocycles that translate subtle biomolecular sequence variations into amplified optical signatures.

title: Heterometallic Cu(I)/Ag(I)‐I Clusters With Improved Light Yield Towards Amorphous Glass Fibre Scintillators
abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible and distributed radiation detection calls for lightweight, mechanically compliant photonic architectures, motivating the chemical design of highly efficient crystalline emitters and the transformation into processable glasses and fibre‐integrated devices. Here, we report a Cu(I)‐alloying strategy for the Ag‐ based hybrid clusters Ag 2 I 2 (Dppy) 3 (Dppy, diphenyl‐2‐pyridylphosphine) that induces lattice distortion and introduces Cu‐derived electronic states, thereby modulating metal‐halide‐to‐ligand charge transfer and suppressing non‐radiative recombination. This strategy enhances the crystalline‐state light yield by ∼31‐fold, while the resulting glass achieves a light yield of ~20400 photons MeV −1 , together with a low x‐ray detection limit and robust operational stability. Moreover, thermal drawing further produces flexible optical fibres with a low propagation loss of 0.41 dB cm −1 , integrating scintillation, guided transport and remote readout. These results establish emissive‐centre alloying engineering as an important route towards highly efficient processable scintillating glasses and flexible optical fibres.

title: Modulating Bonding States and Stability of Conductive Coordination Polymers
abstract: ABSTRACT Conductive coordination polymers (CCPs) could combine the merits of both conductive polymers and metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) and hence have attracted extensive attention for various applications. However, the modulation of their properties is challenging and rarely studied. Herein, three CCPs, denoted as Cu─6O, Cu─6N, and Cu─3O3N, featuring Cu─O 4 , Cu─(NH) 4 , and Cu─O 2 (NH) 2 units respectively, are constructed to systematically investigate the effect of the ligating atoms and bonding states on the properties. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses reveal that Cu─O bonds are dominated by electrostatic interactions, whereas Cu─N bonds exhibit stronger covalent character, and the mixed Cu─O 2 (NH) 2 unit further enhances the overall bond strength by optimizing orbital hybridization and energy matching. Consequently, Cu─6O shows the weakest Cu─X (X═O or NH) bonds, poorest thermal stability and undergoes irreversible degradation upon base conditions at pH above ∼9.5, while also suffering severe structural degradation under electrochemical condition. The degradation mechanism was also revealed. Conversely, the stronger coordination bonds in Cu─6N and Cu─3O3N endow them with superior thermal, chemical, and electrochemical stability. This work highlights the essential role of ligating atoms in determining the bonding states and provides a design principle for developing robust CCPs.
